jobs.title: Summer Camp Director, Galileo X San Juan Capistrano 4 (2027)
jobs.location: San Juan Capistrano, CA, United States
jobs.description:
Galileo is looking for an experienced leader to join our team as a Camp Director. Camp Directors lead our dynamic summer camps for K–8th grade, serving as both site General Manager and the public face of the organization.

You will open and operate a Camp Galileo location serving campers and their families within your community! You will lead a dynamic seasonal team of educators as well as enthusiastic entry-level staff to create joyful, safe environments and ensure smooth daily operations. With a focus on exceptional camper and family experiences, you will uphold program quality, foster creativity, and deliver excellence in customer care, curriculum, and team leadership.

Why This Role Matters

Galileo started in 2002 with a single summer camp in Palo Alto, named for Galileo Galilei, one of history’s great innovators. Today we run 90+ sites across eight states, and Camp Directors are still the people who give each camp its own traditions and magic. Our mission is to develop innovators who envision and create a better world, and at camp, you’re the one who makes that real for campers, families, and staff every day.

You will be Accountable for

Bringing Galileo’s Spirit to Life

• Infuse camp with joy, tradition, and creativity
• Build an inclusive environment where every camper, staff member, and family feels seen, supported, and inspired

Leading with Ownership and Vision

• Own every aspect of your camp’s launch, from preseason planning through end-of-summer wrap-up
• As both operational lead and culture builder, oversee every detail from daily camp operations to parent communication while delivering an exceptional program

Keeping Camp Safe and Running Smoothly

• Prioritize camper safety, family trust, and program fidelity at all times
• Anticipate needs, adapt quickly, and problem-solve on the fly so camp runs seamlessly, even when things don’t go as planned

Developing and Managing Your Team

• Train and mentor a staff of 7 to 40 (depending on site size), including educators and entry-level staff, while actively building your team culture
• Provide clear expectations for instructional and program standards, ongoing feedback, and professional development
• Own core management responsibilities such as training support, scheduling, payroll, and ongoing performance management

Embracing Challenge and Innovation

• Use the Galileo Innovation Approach (GIA) to encourage curiosity and problem-solving
• Lead your team in turning challenges into opportunities, keeping both spirit and operations aligned to Galileo’s mission
• Communicate openly with your Field Program Manager, seek out feedback, and turn it into action
• Take ownership of your own professional development, staying self-motivated to learn, grow, and improve throughout the summer

Building Strong Partnerships

• Serve as the primary face of camp within the community
• Communicate proactively with families, facilities partners, and cross-functional teams
• Collaborate with your Field Program Manager and cultivate trust with community partners, staff, and campers

Location & Work Schedule:

This is a seasonal role running March–September 2027, with a schedule divided into three phases. Exact dates will vary based on hire date and specific site operating dates:

• Phase One: Training & Prep (March–June): 5 to 15 hours per week, depending on tenure and start date — mostly flexible and remote, with some required scheduled and in-person commitments. This phase includes in-person training(s), a Bay Area retreat, scheduled virtual training(s), marketing events, and on-site prep at your camp location during the week leading up to camp. Some events may take place during evenings and weekends.
• Phase Two: On-Site (June–August): On-site hours typically range from 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM (M-F), up to 50 hours per week over 5–8 weeks, depending on camp placement.
• Phase Three: Wrap-Up (Aug–Sept): Up to 5 hrs total, remote, for final admin tasks and staff reviews.

Compensation:

(Year 1 estimate):

• Preseason (Feb–June): Earn hourly pay ($23-25/hour) for flexible, part-time prep and training
• Camp Season (June–Aug): Transition to a weekly salary ($1,500/week, plus an additional $50/week for each year of returning tenure in this role) as a full-time, exempt Camp Director during summer operations
• Postseason (Aug–Sept): Wrap up with light part-time work, paid hourly ($23-25/hour)
• Bonus/Commission: Earn an additional $1 per camper-week enrollment, plus potential commission for add-on weeks

Exact compensation may vary and will be based on multiple factors, including geography and Galileo camp director tenure. Our pay practices are guided by a commitment to equity and informed by market benchmarking and internal audits to minimize bias and ensure fairness across all roles.

Perks:

• Free camp for your child(ren) or two giftable weeks (incl. extended care)
• 15% Friends & Family discount
• Priority nomination for financial assistance for someone you know

• 3+ years of experience working directly with students in an education setting (out-of-school time, teaching, education administration, camps/recreation, etc.) is required
• Minimum 1 year of experience managing or supervising adult staff is required
• Proven experience creating safe, inclusive environments for children and building trust with families
• Proven experience setting clear expectations, giving ongoing feedback, and coaching staff to improve
• Demonstrated ability to manage operational details like scheduling, staffing, and payroll
• Track record of staying calm and making sound decisions in fast-paced situations, including safety issues and challenging conversations with families
• Strong written and verbal communication with families, partners, and supervisors
• Experience with hands-on, project-based learning (STEAM, art, design, maker programs) is a plus
• Availability for part-time remote work starting March 2027, and full-time on-site work starting June 2027 (dates vary by location)
• Willingness to travel in the region to up to 3 in person marketing events, in the preseason
• Ability to complete all required training before camp begins
• Ability to meet state requirements to work with children, including mandated screenings and Adult & Child First Aid/CPR/AED certification

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team and strongly encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds and experiences. If you think you have what it takes to be successful in this role, we encourage you to apply.

Please note that our job descriptions are a summary of the typical functions of the job, not an exhaustive or comprehensive list of all possible responsibilities, tasks, and duties.

jobs.title: Reentry Career Advisor
jobs.description:
The Reentry Career Advisor provides pre-release and post-release workforce and reentry services to justice-involved individuals preparing to transition back into the community. This position supports participants through career planning, employment preparation, case management, and supportive services coordination to help individuals successfully obtain employment, training, and long-term stability. Work is performed in correctional facilities, detention centers, NCWorks Career Centers, and community settings, with flexibility to work evenings, weekends, and multiple office locations as needed.

• Recruit, enroll, and guide eligible participants through program services within correctional facilities and community settings.
• Assess participant work history, education, skills, abilities, and barriers to employment while helping participants identify solutions and career pathways.
• Develop individualized employment and service plans focused on short and long term employment, education, training, retention, and self-sufficiency goals.
• Provide career advising, employment readiness coaching, resume assistance, interview preparation, job search support, workshops, and referrals to community resources and supportive services.
• Maintain regular contact with participants to support job readiness, employment retention, advancement, and ongoing program participation.
• Coordinate with employers, correctional facilities, NCWorks partners, educational institutions, and community organizations to connect participants with employment, training, and supportive services opportunities.
• Maintain information on local employers, workforce resources, training opportunities, and community services available to participants.
• Participate in and/or host job fairs, hiring events, and workforce outreach activities.
• Maintain accurate participant files, case notes, data entry, attendance records, retention tracking, and required program reporting in compliance with program requirements.
• Any additional duties as assigned.

• Associate degree from an accredited college or university in workforce development, social work, criminal justice, public administration, human services, or a related field; or equivalent combination of education, work experience, and lived experience.
• One to three years of experience in workforce development, reentry services, case management, counseling, or related programs is preferred.
• Knowledge of or experience working with justice-involved individuals and understanding the challenges associated with incarceration and community reentry.
• Some local travel may be required.
• Familiarity with the communities being served and available local resources.
• Excellent communication, computer skills, customer service, organizational, and relationship-building skills.
• Ability to work effectively with participants, correctional staff, employers, and community partners.

jobs.title: Truck Driver
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Truck Driver to join our Mayer Team in Norcross, GA!

Summary:

Employee’s level and pay will be dependent on their level of experience, knowledge, and capabilities. The Truck Driver is responsible for delivering products to/from customers, company branch/warehouse locations, and company suppliers in a delivery van or box truck (No CDL required). Responsible for ensuring that deliveries are prepared to meet customer requirements in the most efficient manner and materials are correct and free of damage.

What You'll Do:

• Inspect company vehicle for visual and operating defects; responsible for completing a daily inspection report
• Keep company vehicle clean, serviced, and maintained; alert supervisor of repair and/or service needed
• Must follow Department of Transportation (DOT), local and state driving laws and regulations
• Load or unload vehicle and ensure all material for each order is correct (quantity and type of material) and that material is free of damage before departure
• May assist in preparing orders for delivery
• Ensure all appropriate documentation is thoroughly completed at the time of delivery, including delivery receipt is signed by the customer, packing list and branch/warehouse manifest
• Pick up material returns from customers; responsible for inspecting the condition of the material and verifies quantities and catalog numbers
• Pick up material from company suppliers
• Senior Truck Driver will participate in the training of entry level Truck Drivers; and provides mentorship and coaching
• May be required to perform other job functions within a branch when required including but not limited to counter sales, preparing and filling orders and/or receiving, stocking, staging, and shipping material, and maintaining branch equipment

The information contained in this job description is intended to describe the essential job functions required of those assigned to this job. jobs.title: Outpatient Physical Therapist IHR-Casual As Needed
jobs.description:
The Physical Therapist reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

• A licensed physical therapist who complies with the Code of Ethics/Standards of Practice as outlined by their professional organization and by the State of Illinois.
• The position includes direct patient care, teaching, participation on appropriate committees and departmental process improvement.
• Serves as a role model for all therapists and clinical interns in all aspects of professional, clinical, communication, education and leadership activities.

Responsibilities:

• Demonstrates the four NM values of teamwork, patients first, integrity, and excellence in daily work and interactions.
• Presents a friendly, approachable, professional demeanor and appearance.
• Provides accurate information and timely updates to patients and customers. Addresses questions and concerns promptly or identifies appropriate person and resources to do so. Provides directions to help patients and customers with finding their way.
• Uses effective service recovery skills to solve problems or service breakdowns when they occur.
• Maintains primary responsibility over patient plan of care through timely and consistent collaboration with treating PT/ PTA s.
• Demonstrates teamwork by helping co-workers within and across departments. Communicates effectively with others, respects diverse opinions and styles, and acknowledges the assistance and contributions of others.
• Uses organizational and unit/department resources efficiently.
• Manages work schedule efficiently, completing tasks and assignments on time.
• Contributes to opportunities and processes for continuous improvement.
• Participates in efforts to reduce costs, streamline work processes, improve and grow services we provide.
• Demonstrates creative problem solving and diversity when adapting the treatment to special circumstances as evidence by team feedback and documentation.
• Demonstrates essential skill competencies in selecting the appropriate evaluation in the use of treatment modalities, equipment and protocols. Performs re-evaluations according to department guidelines, adjusting the treatment plan accordingly. Evidenced by chart review.
• Assumes complete responsibility over the course of physical therapist patient management from the time of initial contact to discharge for functional progress, safety and treatment outcome as evidenced by team feedback and documentation. Maintains primary responsibility over patient plans of care through timely and consistent collaboration with treating PTA(s).
• Adheres to department policy regarding evaluations, progress notes, and discharge summaries. All notes are documented in electronic medical record (EMR).
• Completes daily notes that reflect patient’s response to treatment, actual performance, and an assessment as to status, relevant to the treatment plan and eventual discharge needs as evidenced by chart review, meeting all documentation requirements (e.g., allows other therapists to continue treatment, allows for interpretation by payers, supports reimbursement).
• Provides educational materials and methods appropriate to the patient’s level of understanding and motivation as evidenced by chart review, observation and team feedback.
• Participates in committees, department processes and special projects in accordance with clinical expertise and individual performance plan.
• Works to develop and maintain professional relationships with members of healthcare teams (ex: physician, nurse, case manager). Participates in internal and external marketing per department expectations.
• Creates a culture of respectful communication by listening, asking for team member input, open and honest conversation, approachability, and timely acknowledgement of individual and team contributions.
• Accepts constructive feedback and can make timely changes as evidenced by written coaching forms/chart audits and team feedback.
• Proactively completes non-patient care responsibilities within established timelines (coverage notes, PTO/schedule change requests, bonus pay (forms and follow up phone calls).
• Contributes to educational efforts of department/clinic (e.g., in-services, journal clubs, new hire orientation, PI) as per department expectations.
• Actively participates in student clinical or observation programs by serving as a clinical instructor, mentor, or observation host as per department expectations
• Maintains productivity standards per department expectations
• Demonstrates willingness to flex schedule or assignment to meet patient care needs, staff meetings and department specific meetings outside of normal work hours.

Minimum Requirements:

Education:

• Bachelor’s Degree in Physical Therapy.

Licensure:

• Licensed Physical Therapist in State of Illinois

Certification:

• BLS from American Heart Association upon hire

Preferred:

• Masters or Doctoral Degree in Physical Therapy

jobs.title: Engineer, Manufacturing
jobs.description:
Responsible for moderate to complex configuration and programming of Operation Technology (OT) Systems as per AbbVie change management procedures for the manufacturing process, utilities and Facilities Control Systems. This role is responsible for leading small to medium-sized automation projects to assure project is implemented as per project schedule. This role provides technical support and system troubleshooting for systems and\or areas assigned to this position. Responsible for the administration and maintenance of assigned OT systems as per applicable departmental procedures.

Responsibilities

• Develops moderate to complex control configuration or programming in accordance with the design documents to meet the functional requirements.
• Provides process controls inputs and recommendations regarding manufacturing operation continuance issues and process improvements.
• Performs and reviews configuration and programming using defined practices to establish compliance with users and functional requirements.
• Establishes project management techniques in monitoring, reporting, and controlling automation projects according to size and criticality (small to medium projects). This role will support Capital projects when automation expertise is required.
• Coordinates and develops schedule with supply chain and operations to perform or support maintenance works and other changes to systems in production during off-peak hours. This might require working overtime, overnight or on weekends. Conform to EHS management system requirements and compliance obligations, promote continuous improvement, and consider EHS aspects during the design and change process.
• Provides training for OT Systems Users/Engineers in new automation technologies and process control applications.
• Diagnoses and troubleshoots OT System hardware, software, and networking issues, replace defective components as needed. Responsible for implementing and validating OT systems upgrades and data migrations for DCS, PLC’s, SCADA, and Data Historian systems. Conform to EHS management system requirements and compliance obligations, promote continuous improvement, and consider EHS aspects during the design and change process. Complies with all EHS procedures and policies including incident reporting.

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related discipline with a minimum of two (2) years of relevant experience required. Master’s degree in computer science, engineering or related discipline, no experienced is required.
• Working experience with SCADA and PLCs (such as Allen-Bradley ControlLogix), programming in ladder logic and instructional texts. HMI graphics development and management would be a plus.
• Solid understanding of pharmaceutical and biotechnology manufacturing processes, including operational best practices and regulatory expectations.
• Industry experience exposure to FDA, GMP, 21CFR11, Data Integrity, Safety and Environmental legislation.
• Experience designing and implementing Windows Server Operating Systems and related components including Active Directory, NTFS Setup and Security, User Administration, TCP/IP with DHCP, WINS and DNS would be a plus.

This range may be modified in the future. ​

jobs.title: Staff Supplier Quality Engineer - ISO 13485 Lead Auditor - Remote from Atlanta, GA Region (50% Travel Internationally)
jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position

The Staff Supplier Quality Engineer operates with a high degree of independence to determine methodologies, audit frameworks, quality systems, and procedural controls across the global supply chain ecosystem, reporting to the Director, Global Supply Chain Audits.

This role is responsible for the technical execution, continuous improvement, strategic projects, and global harmonization of Third-Party Logistics (3PL) quality management, distribution center controls, and service supplier qualification processes worldwide. The Staff SQE leads risk-based lead audit programs, ensures conformance to applicable global regulatory standards (21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485, EU MDR 2017/745, Good Distribution Practice / GDP), and serves as a subject matter expert (SME) in regulatory body inspections. S/he partners with cross-functional global operations, logistics, and regional RAQA organizations to drive critical process improvement projects, resolve systemic quality issues, ensure CAPA effectiveness, and advance 3PL supply chain compliance maturity.

Essential Job Duties

·         3PL Quality Management & Worldwide Oversight

·         Design, own, and continuously improve a global 3PL Quality Management Program encompassing third-party logistics providers, global distribution hubs, forward stocking locations, cold chain/temperature-controlled storage facilities, and fulfillment partners across all global regions.

·         Establish and maintain qualification frameworks, quality agreements (QAs), and re-evaluation controls specific to 3PL providers and logistics vendors supporting GxP-regulated distribution processes in alignment with 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485 (Clause 7.5.5), EU MDR, and GDP requirements.

·         Drive global harmonization of 3PL quality controls, distribution oversight, and logistics quality standards across regional entities: ISJ, ISK, IS India, IS Aubonne, ISE, ISB, and IST.

·         Maintain quality oversight of 3PL operational execution, including ambient/cold-chain storage validation, environmental monitoring, product handling, serialized inventory controls, localized labeling/repackaging, and transportation controls.

·         Lead Audits & Supplier / Service Qualification

·         Lead and execute comprehensive risk-based audits as Lead Auditor for worldwide 3PL providers, distribution hubs, and service suppliers (sterilization, calibration, test laboratories, software/IT GxP service vendors).

·         Design, own, and update 3PL audit master schedules, audit risk models, protocols, checklists, and reporting templates tailored to third-party logistics and service supplier activities.

·         Conduct Lead Audits against applicable global regulatory standards including Good Distribution Practice (GDP), ISO 13485, ISO 17025, ISO 11135/11137, and 21 CFR Part 820 subpart requirements.

·         Evaluate audit findings, issue formal audit reports, drive root cause analysis rigor with 3PL leadership, and manage SCAR / CAPA phase gate reviews and effectiveness verifications.

·         Projects & Process Improvements

·         Lead strategic quality engineering projects and continuous process improvement initiatives to optimize supply chain workflows, streamline 3PL quality oversight, and elevate supplier scorecards.

·         Partner with IT and Supply Chain teams to drive continuous improvement of QMS software platforms (Trackwise, SAP, Agile) supporting 3PL quality workflows, audit scheduling, and SCAR tracking.

·         Establish and analyze quality metrics, trends, and KPIs regarding 3PL performance, supplier corrective actions, and audit program effectiveness.

·         Own Process Nonconformances (NCs) and CAPAs related to 3PL, logistics, and supply chain audit processes, ensuring root cause rigor (6M / 5-Why) and sustainable corrective actions.

·         Supplier Controls & QMS Administration

·         Manage 3PL Supplier Corrective Action Requests (SCARs) end-to-end: issuance, aging tracking, phase gate reviews, effectiveness verification, and closure.

·         Support Approved Supplier List (ASL) governance regarding 3PL status maintenance, including promotions, conditional approvals, and demotions.

·         Administer and maintain 3PL and service supplier records in Trackwise, SAP, and Agile, including audit files, ISO/GDP certifications, quality agreements, and ARFs.

·         Regulatory Audit Support & Leadership

·         Serve as SME during FDA inspections, Notified Body audits (e.g., BSI, TÜV), and internal QMS audits for all matters related to 3PL Controls, GDP compliance, Service Supplier qualification, and Supply Chain Audits.

·         Operate independently to determine methods and procedures on new, complex, or special assignments with minimal supervision.

·         Mentor, coach, and guide junior compliance and supplier quality engineering staff.

·         May supervise or mentor the activities of junior compliance and supplier quality staff.

Required Skills and Experience

• ISO 13485 Lead Auditor with demonstrated experience leading multi-site external audits worldwide.
• Expert-level knowledge of 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485:2016, EU MDR 2017/745, and Good Distribution Practice (GDP / GMP) requirements applicable to 3PL, logistics, and service supplier controls.
• Proven experience leading quality oversight and audits of global 3PLs, cold chain storage, distribution networks, and service suppliers.
• Expert proficiency with QMS platforms including Trackwise, SAP, and Agile for supplier file management, SCAR tracking, and audit scheduling.
• Strong understanding of risk management principles (ISO 14971) as applied to 3PL risk stratification, logistics risk assessments, and audit frequency determination.

Required Education and Training

• Education: BS/BA degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, Supply Chain Management, or a related technical discipline preferred.
• Experience Level: Typically requires a minimum of 12 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree; or 8 years with a Master's degree; or a PhD with 5 years of experience; or equivalent demonstrated experience.
• Industry Experience: Significant experience in a high-volume, globally distributed medical device or GxP-regulated company is required.

Working Conditions

• Travel 50% Internationally

Preferred Skills and Experience

·         Direct experience auditing and managing worldwide 3PL providers, temperature-controlled distribution, and global supply chain logistics in a regulated medical device environment.

·         Exposure to auditing service suppliers and distributors in a regulated medical device environment.

jobs.title: Office of Children and Families (OCF) - Data Service Coordinator
jobs.description:
The Data Services Coordinator is responsible for coordinating projects involving the collection, analysis, interpretation, and reporting of large volumes of quantitative and qualitative data. The Data Services Coordinator will also support evaluation and data-related activities associated with inquiries from the Office of the Youth Ombudsperson (OYO) and PMT Service Concerns, including data wrangling, structured review of inquiry materials, review of Service Concern reports and supporting documentation, and development of analytic summaries to support timely, accurate evaluation responses, in alignment with PMT processes for service concerns and system oversight.

The Data Services Coordinator will work collaboratively with internal teams, stakeholders, leadership, and external partners to monitor project progress, identify issues, support informed decision-making, and ensure projects are delivered effectively and in accordance with established requirements.

In addition, the Data Services Coordinator will support evaluation, monitoring, and data collection activities related to DHS contracted residential providers including compliance monitoring, fidelity to policy and practice standards, and data collection associated with youth safety, rights, and service quality. This position will require periodic local travel, including quarterly on-site visits to the Philadelphia Juvenile Justice Services Center (PJJSC) and other DHS contracted facilities to support evaluation and monitoring activities. This role supports project planning and execution while ensuring that project activities align with defined scopes, organizational policies, regulatory requirements, and applicable standards.

Essential Functions

• Support data collection, monitoring, and evaluation activities related to PJJSC operations, including review of incident data, policy-aligned monitoring tools, and structured documentation, and conduct best practice research to inform tool updates, workflow improvements, and practical guidance materials used in internal oversight work.
• Assist with qualitative and quantitative data collection efforts related to youth experiences, staff practices, and program conditions, including surveys, observations, and document reviews as assigned, in coordination with PMT team members and site stakeholders to support strong working relationships and effective data collection.
• Contribute to preparation of data summaries, monitoring outputs, and evaluation materials used to inform PMT leadership, DHS leadership, and external oversight entities as appropriate.
• Support continuous quality improvement efforts by identifying data gaps, trends, and implementation challenges related to PJJSC compliance and service quality.
• Support evaluation-related review of Office of the Youth Ombudsperson (OYO) inquiries and Service Concerns by organizing, reviewing, and synthesizing relevant qualitative and quantitative data, including incident documentation, timelines, program records, and Service Concern reports.
• Assist with data cleaning, validation and data management activities related to OYO inquiries and Service Concerns, ensuring data accuracy, version control, and alignment with PMT data standards.
• Support structured review processes which include preparation of analytic summaries, data tables, and documentation to inform PMT leadership review.
• Coordinate with PMT staff to track Service Concern-related data, themes, and trends over time to support continuous quality improvement and system learning.

Required Competencies, Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

• Data Collection, Analysis & Reporting: Collect, organize, validate, and maintain large quantitative and qualitative datasets from multiple sources. Analyze data to identify trends, patterns, gaps, risks, and opportunities.
• Report Writing: Ability to produce accurate, concise, well-structured reports for diverse audiences.
• Knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite, including data analysis tools like Excel and/or open-source tools, Tableau or other data visualization software. Proficiency in producing high-quality written products using Microsoft Word (or similar), including editing for clarity, structure, tone, and audience.
• Attention to Detail: Ability to identify discrepancies, maintain data integrity, and ensure accuracy.
• Regulatory & Policy Awareness: Ability to understand and apply applicable policies, procedures, standards, and regulations.
• Problem Solving: Ability to identify issues, evaluate alternatives, and develop practical solutions.
• Stakeholder Engagement: Ability to work effectively with diverse teams, stakeholders, and leadership. Serve as a central point of coordination among project teams, management, stakeholders, and external partners. Communicate project status, findings, risks, and recommendations clearly and professionally. Adapt written and verbal communication to technical and non-technical audiences. Facilitate information sharing and collaboration across departments and project teams. Build effective working relationships with stakeholders at varying levels of the organization.
• Project Coordination & Management: Ability to coordinate timelines, deliverables, resources, risks, and competing priorities. Coordinate multiple projects, workstreams, activities, and deliverables simultaneously. Develop and maintain project schedules, work plans, timelines, task assignments, and tracking mechanisms. Monitor project milestones, deliverables, dependencies, risks, issues, and resource requirements. Coordinate meetings, prepare agendas and materials, document decisions and action items, and follow up on outstanding tasks. Work with project teams and stakeholders to ensure deliverables are completed on time and within established scope. Identify project challenges and escalate issues when appropriate. Support continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to improve processes, workflows, and project outcomes.
• Scope, Policy & Regulatory Compliance: Develop a strong understanding of project scopes, objectives, requirements, policies, procedures, contracts, and applicable regulations. Ensure project activities and deliverables remain consistent with approved scope and organizational requirements. Review project information and documentation for alignment with policies, standards, and regulatory obligations. Identify potential compliance, operational, or project risks and communicate them to appropriate stakeholders. Maintain accurate records to support accountability, transparency, audits, and reporting requirements.
• Data Analysis & Interpretation: Ability to evaluate complex quantitative and qualitative information and derive meaningful insights. Interpret qualitative information, stakeholder feedback, interviews, surveys, and other non-numerical data.
• Decision-Making: Ability to evaluate information objectively and make well-reasoned recommendations. Apply appropriate analytical methods to support project objectives and decision-making. Use data, project findings, policies, and established criteria to assess options and make recommendations. Exercise sound judgment when addressing project issues, competing priorities, and unexpected challenges. Clearly communicate the rationale, supporting evidence, risks, and potential impacts associated with recommendations.
• Demonstrated ability to understand and apply policies, procedures, project scopes, and regulatory requirements.
• Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office or comparable productivity and data-analysis tools.

Bachelor’s degree in data analytics, business administration, public administration, statistics, social sciences, or a related field. An equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant experience may be considered.

•    At least 1-2 years of experience working with tool development and data collection related to program monitoring, quality improvement, and/or evaluation systems. Experience should include qualitative data collection and analysis (e.g., interviews, focus groups, observations, document review) and translating findings into clear written products.

•    Project management experience and/or applicable business experience. Demonstrated experience independently managing qualitative evaluation or monitoring workstreams, including planning, data collection, synthesis, and deliverables, strongly preferred.

•    Demonstrated ability to draft, edit, and finalize reports with minimal supervision—including organizing complex information, synthesizing qualitative findings, and producing clear, accurate, and publication-ready written materials for leadership and external stakeholders—strongly preferred.

•    Strong writing and editing skills are essential, including the ability to apply consistent style, ensure accuracy, and tailor content for different audiences (e.g., practitioners, leadership, and external reviewers).

Ability to exercise independent judgment and make sound decisions based on available information.

TO APPLY: Interested candidates must submit a cover letter, resume, and references.

Salary Range: $60,000 - $75,000

About the role:

As a Software Engineer II on the storeLink engineering team, you will design, develop, and support key features for our cloud-native retail management platform. storeLink empowers grocery and drug retailers across three core operational capabilities: in-store price tag printing, Electronic Shelf Label (ESL) device management, and digital video screen display management. Operating within an Azure-hosted microservices architecture, you will work closely with dedicated feature sprint teams, our Principal Architect, and L2 Technical Support Engineers to deliver reliable, high-performance web applications and API integrations.

This is a hybrid position that requires 2 days/week in-office. Currently we are only considering candidates within a commutable distance to our offices in Little Rock, AR; Dallas, TX; Mentor, OH; Miamisburg, OH; and New Century, KS.

Key Responsibilities:

• Full-Stack Feature Development: Design, build, test, and maintain scalable microservices using .NET Core for backend web APIs and modern Angular for front-end web interfaces.
• Database & Cloud Infrastructure: Maintain and optimize MS SQL data structures, leverage Azure AI Search, and support applications hosted on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), Azure Service Bus, Blob Storage, Azure Front Door, and Application Insights.
• API Integration & Services: Integrate storeLink microservices with external systems via REST APIs, including custom rendering engines (such as UE2) for PDF and PNG media generation.
• CI/CD & Production Support: Manage GitHub version control, build/release pipelines using GitHub Actions, and partner with L2 support to triage and resolve escalated production issues.
• Quality, Compliance & Agile Methods: Implement unit/automated integration tests, adhere to internal security and SOX 404 controls, and participate in Agile code reviews and task estimation.

• BS in Computer Science, Engineering, or related technical field with 4+ years of software development experience (or MS with 1+ years).
• Proven experience building enterprise web applications using .NET Core, C#, Angular, and RESTful Web APIs within a microservices architecture.
• Strong proficiency in MS SQL / T-SQL development, schema design, query optimization, and working with managed database instances.
• Practical experience with Azure cloud components (AKS, Azure Service Bus, Blob Storage, Application Insights) and continuous integration/deployment using GitHub Actions.
• Strong debugging, analytical, and communication skills to resolve complex technical issues escalated from support teams and articulate designs to engineering leadership.

jobs.title: Senior AI web software Engineer
jobs.description:
Experian Partner Solutions is looking for Senior Web Engineers to build the products our partners white label as their own – embedded components that run inside partner applications, and hosted sites that carry a partner's brand. When a partner puts our software in front of their customers, our code runs under their brand, in their environment, with their reputation attached. There is no margin for "it works on my machine."

Predominantly ReactJS and Typescript across the browser and the server – on the front end, Node in our services and tooling.

We are building this team around AI-assisted development. That is not a perk in the job description – it is the operating model. You will spend a significant share of your time directing AI coding agents, reviewing what those agents produce, and being personally accountable for code you did not type character by character. You will report to the director of web development.

• Manage web software end-to-end – develop, and support it in production. Ownership does not stop at the merge.
• Direct AI coding agents as your primary implementation method rather than hand-writing every line.
• Decompose features into work an agent can build reliably, and write the prompts and specs that make that possible.
• Make the architecture calls AI cannot make for you: interface and Api design, state and service boundaries, versioning, and backward compatibility for consumers who depend on your releases.
• Design for environments you do not control, whether that is a hostile host page, an unfamiliar partner configuration, or an unexpected client of your Api.
• Use AI to create test suites and regression coverage, then look for what the generator missed: adversarial inputs, integration conflicts, and configuration edge cases.

Agentic Responsibilities

• Break complex features into AI-manageable tasks.
• Review AI-generated code for bugs, security, and architecture issues.
• Write prompts that produce quality code.
• Use AI for testing while recognizing its limitations.
• Demonstrate architecture and system-design judgment.
• Understand where AI performs well and where it fall short.

• 5+ years experience building and shipping production web software, with ownership of what you built after it went live.
• Bachelor's degree in a relevant field or equivalent experience.
• You will have experience in ReactJS and Typescript, applied across the browser and the server. We work in React and Node; expertise in a comparable ecosystem plus evidence you pick up new stacks quickly is equally welcome.
• Component libraries, design systems, or SDKs consumed by teams outside your own — where breaking changes carry cost.
• Server-side or full-stack web work — Node services, APIs, and the integrations that connect a customer-facing product to the systems behind it.
• Practical web security awareness: injection and XSS vectors, authentication and session handling, dependency risk, and safe handling of sensitive data.
• Experience with DevOps and CI/CD, automated test and build tooling.

Our uniqueness is that we celebrate yours. Experian's people first, driven culture is multi award-winning; World's Best Workplaces™ 2025 (Fortune Global Top 25), Great Place To Work™ in 26 countries to name a few. Check out Experian Life on social or explore our Careers Site to understand why.

If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know at the earliest opportunity.

jobs.title: Staff Engineer
jobs.description:
Every day, ePayPolicy helps over 10,000 insurance companies speed up incoming and outgoing payments. By helping them move from manual, outdated forms of payment collection to modern payment tools, we help their companies work faster and more efficiently. (Check out our almost 5-star customer reviews https://www.g2.com/products/epaypolicy/reviews.)


How do we do it? With powerful payment tools that just work. Our secure, online ACH and credit card payment page is the core product for many of our companies. But we also provide an integrated suite of helpful features for insurance companies of all sizes, including point-of-sale financing, payables network tools, and check reconciliation, all within a single dashboard.


Our expert, live support team helps deliver exceptional care every day, with an industry-leading 97% customer retention rate. Our customers love us. We love them.


Founded in 2014, our growing team is based in Austin, TX, and has clients in all 50 US states. We’ve grown over 300% in the last three years - with big plans for the future.


The Challenge You'll Own

Insurance runs on legacy rails—paper checks, PDF invoices, and fragmented accounting systems. As our Staff Engineer, you will own the architectural blueprint for modernizing this industry through flagship initiatives like Connected AR/AP and Total Recon. These projects eliminate manual invoice entry and automate bank statement reconciliation, saving our customers thousands of hours of manual tracking and false policy cancellations.



Beyond shipping features, you will define how our engineering org builds in the AI era. You’ll bridge our battle-tested C#/.NET core with modern Azure AI infrastructure, establish our spec-driven development standards, and solve real-world latency and indexing bottlenecks at scale. Your architectural judgment will directly dictate how fast and safely we move AI agents into production.



Insurance or fintech background helps, but successful candidates will have a history of proven architectural judgment.


REQUIREMENTS

 - Proven experience designing and deploying scalable Microsoft enterprise stack solutions with C#, ASP.NET http://ASP.NET Core, SQL Server, and React.

 - Hands-on track record building production AI systems using Azure AI Foundry, Azure AI Search, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures.

 - Deep understanding of AI agent architectures, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and custom indexing strategies to optimize slow agent requests.

 - Familiarity with spec-driven development frameworks like spec-kit or Open Spec.

 - Solid background in Azure cloud architecture, containerization, and Azure cost management.

 - Strong technical leadership skills with experience mentoring engineers, running code reviews, and enforcing high engineering standards.


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Architect and execute technical exploration for complex initiatives like Connected AR/AP and Total Recon.

 - Refine and expand our proprietary Azure AI Search tools to empower internal business stakeholders.

 - Establish spec-driven workflows and guide team adoption of AI coding assistants.

 - Serve as a hands-on technical mentor across the engineering department, raising the bar for code quality and systemic design.

 - Collaborate closely with product leaders to translate complex business problems into modular technical execution plans.

 - Drive end-to-end technical execution across the entire stack, ensuring seamless integration between traditional C#/.NET services and modern Azure AI architectures.

 - Establish rigorous coding standards and architectural oversight, ensuring teams maintain high code quality across legacy and AI-driven systems alike.


THIS ROLE MAY NOT BE FOR YOU IF...

 - You prefer purely theoretical architecture work without writing code or building prototypes.

 - You dislike working in dynamic environments with technical ambiguity and evolving AI capabilities.

 - You favor isolated research over cross-functional team collaboration and mentorship.


Why ePayPolicy

 - Competitive salary

 - Comprehensive benefits package with employer-paid basic life and disability premiums

 - 401K

 - Flexible Paid Time Off Policy (FTO)

 - Company-sponsored quarterly “ePayItForward” initiatives 

 - Supportive and inclusive company culture with a focus on work/life balance

 - Fully-stocked kitchen

 - Lunch stipend when working onsite

 - Open communication (We won’t box you in! If you have a cool idea for a product improvement or a suggestion on how to improve the customer experience, let’s talk about it. We value everyone’s ideas and opinions.)

 - Huge opportunity for growth


We operate on a hybrid schedule for in-office employees. Standard schedules are three days per week in the office, however, the cadence and days are determined by each team and manager. 



Embracing AI at ePayPolicy - At ePayPolicy, AI is a company-wide initiative essential to how we work and innovate. All employees are expected to proactively leverage approved enterprise AI tools to drive operational productivity. While leaning into these capabilities, team members must maintain our ethical standards: thoroughly verifying AI-generated outputs, safeguarding sensitive data, and strictly prohibiting the generation of synthetic media or the use of another individual’s likeness without explicit consent.



We value diversity here at ePayPolicy and understand the importance of creating a safe and comfortable work environment, encouraging individualism and authenticity in every member of our team. We strive to create an accessible and inclusive experience for all candidates. If you need an accommodation during the application or recruiting process, please submit a request to our team via this Interview Accommodation form: https://forms.gle/xKppyKTSqfTUi7hz5

Bachelor's degree and four years related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience. Aerospace background and aircraft interior industry experience preferred.

Employees working on programs subject to International Traffic in Arms Regulations must qualify as a US Person which is defined as a US Citizen, a Permanent Resident who does not work for a foreign company/foreign government/foreign governmental agency or organization, or a political asylee for legal compliance purposes.

Greenpoint delivers nose-to-tail VIP Jet aircraft interiors for private clients and Heads-of-State.  We are proud to be known in the aerospace industry for our design and engineering innovation, award-winning company culture, and on-time delivery of our beautiful products. jobs.description:
About Dutchie

Founded in 2017, Dutchie is an all-in-one technology platform powering the cannabis industry with Point of Sale, E-commerce, Payments, and Loyalty & Marketing. Through our technology, we’re helping cannabis businesses start, operate, and grow with confidence.

With software that simplifies their operations, our customers can focus on what matters most—bringing the benefits of cannabis safely to consumers.

Powering thousands of dispensaries across 40+ markets throughout the United States and Canada, Dutchie is the leading technology company in the cannabis space and was named in Fast Company’s 10 Most Innovative Companies in North America and listed two years in a row on LinkedIn’s Top 50 Startups.

Dutchie has raised over $600M in funding to date, backed by D1 Capital Partners, Tiger Global, Dragoneer, DFJ Growth, Thrive Capital, Howard Schultz, Snoop Dogg’s Casa Verde Capital, Gron Ventures, members of the founding team at DoorDash, Kevin Durant’s Thirty Five Ventures, and other notable angel investors.

About This Role

Dutchie is looking for a Collections Analyst Intern to join our Finance team and support our Collections function. You’ll help reduce bad debt exposure and lower DSO by supporting outreach on past-due accounts, assisting customers with payment arrangements, and keeping accurate records of every interaction. With guidance from experienced team members, you’ll gain hands-on exposure to the full order-to-cash and B2B collections process while building customer service and accounts receivable skills you can use throughout your career.

What You'll Do

• Support the Collections team by contacting customers with past-due balances (primarily 1–30 days past due) via email, phone, and SMS

• Work from the weekly Aging Report and prioritize outreach by highest balance owed and most days past due

• Review subscription and billing details with customers to help resolve questions and discrepancies using Salesforce and Lockstep

• Assist with payment arrangement requests by capturing the customer’s selected plan, payment method, and first payment date and routing the details to the Collections team

• Submit Salesforce cases for escalated billing or collections issues and escalate customer concerns appropriately

• Provide invoices and payment documentation to customers as needed, and keep customer contact information current in Salesforce

• Document all customer and third-party interactions thoroughly in the customer’s account

• Collaborate with Customer Success, Billing, cash application, and account management teams to resolve account inquiries

• Provide excellent, empathetic customer service and demonstrate a positive attitude, good work ethic, and promptness

• Assist with special projects and perform other duties as assigned

• Leverage AI tools to enhance productivity and streamline workflows

What You Bring

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills with a professional, empathetic customer service tone

• Strong attention to detail and organizational skills; comfortable working in spreadsheets (Google Sheets / Excel)

• Interest in accounts receivable, collections, or finance operations (no prior collections experience required)

• Ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams to meet deadlines and common goals

• Flexibility to prioritize and multi-task in a fast-paced environment at a high growth company, with a willingness to learn

• Proficiency in leveraging and navigating AI tools

It’s a Bonus If You

• Prior internship, coursework, or work experience in accounting, accounts receivable, or customer service

• Experience with Salesforce, Sage, Zendesk, or similar CRM / ticketing tools

• Experience or interest in the Cannabis Industry

Compensation and Benefits

The hourly rate for this internship is $18–$25/hour.

This is a temporary, hourly internship position and is not eligible for the full-time employee benefits package. Interns will receive company-provided technology needed to perform their work.

The PLM Analyst (Polarizing Light Microscope) prepares and analyzes environmental samples according to scientific methodology in compliance with company Quality Assurance programs and SOP’s. Sample analyses include but are not limited to air/bulk asbestos samples. The analyst will validate and review data for accuracy and will upload laboratory data into the LIMS that ultimately generates required reports to clients. Schedules sample workload according to due dates and sample hold times. Analysts will be trained according to current methodologies using job specific testing and equipment.

Analyst responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

• Login, prepare, and analyze environmental samples for asbestos.
• Accurately enters and reports sample descriptions and analytical data using LIMS.
• Performs independent QC analysis for other analysts’ work.
• Performs analysis of reference materials, proficiency samples. And other quality control samples as needed.
• Maintains client service and provides technical support as needed.
• Assists the QA manager in development, implementation and collection of QA processes for the different analytical tests.
• Performs and completes all analytical testing QA related tasks as needed.
• Assists in pursuing, receiving and maintaining necessary laboratory accreditations.
• Co-ordinates projects according to their rush status and due time for timely delivery.
• Assists co-workers on analytical questions, as necessary.
• Follows company policies and procedures and ensures that coworkers are doing the same.
• Manages and disposes analyzed samples as needed.
• Trains new asbestos or other analytical testing Analysts as needed.
• Performs root cause analysis and determines and implements corrective actions for errors and issues as necessary.
• Maintains all equipment properly and co-ordinates services of all equipment used in the laboratory, as needed.
• Communicates available capacity to Lab Manager.
• Supports departments within the lab (login, asbestos, metals, pollen/spores) when appropriate and as needed.
• Other responsibilities as deemed necessary by the Supervisor/Manager
• Preparation/Analysis of bulk samples by Polarized Light Microscopy (PLM) in accordance with the laboratory's Standard Operating Procedures
• Perform all analyses and quality control measures in accordance with the laboratory's Standard Operating Procedures
• Perform equipment maintenance and calibration in accordance with the laboratory's Standard Operating Procedures
• Maintain a clean and safe work area
• Enter data into the LIMS as specified and report data to the client, verbally and electronically
• Store and dispose of client samples in accordance with the laboratory's Standard Operating Procedures

• Degree in Geology or similar is preferred
• At least 1-3 Years Laboratory Experience
• Computer and software proficient
• Ability to multitask
• In order to perform analysis, candidate must be able to distinguish colors
• Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship
• Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English.

This role is full-time and the candidate must be able to work, Tuesday - Saturday 1:00pm - 9:00pm,  Training will be conducted Monday - Friday.

Compensation Range: $20 - $27 per hour, based on experience.

We support your development! Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

Sustainability matters to us! At Eurofins, we believe sustainability is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our vision to be the Global Leader in “Testing for Life,” our mission to contribute to a healthier and safer world, and our core values, we are building a strong foundation for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives. Eurofins’ commitment to sustainability begins within our own companies through a shared responsibility to people and the planet. With climate change posing an imminent threat, Eurofins and its many companies recognize their duty to proactively reduce or offset the environmental impact of essential operations while also helping our clients do the same—serving as a true ESG Enabler.

Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/

Company description: Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure :40 the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate. The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and agroscience contract research services. In 2025, Eurofins generated total revenues of EUR 7.296 billion, and has been among the best performing stocks in Europe over the past 20 years.

Our AI prepares clinicians before the visit, documents the conversation during it, codes the encounter after, writes structured data back to the EHR, and supports nurses across the full shift. All so clinicians spend more time with patients and less on their screens.

We are looking for a PM who wants to own a product surface end to end and drive deep impact. You'll work with dedicated engineering, design, clinical, ops, and GTM partners, and be accountable for how the whole product succeeds.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Set the strategy for a major product surface and drive it from vision through discovery, spec, launch, adoption, and iteration. What you ship this year shapes how care gets delivered across the country.

 - Work full stack across the whole product motion. Craft intuitive UIs clinicians actually want to use, set the bar on backend reliability and model quality, and shape the GTM strategy and operational playbooks that drive adoption across clinics and hospitals. You do this alongside dedicated engineering, design, clinical, ops, and GTM partners.

 - Sit shoulder to shoulder with providers. Spend real time onsite in clinics, hospitals, and on nursing floors. Watch how care actually gets delivered, feel the friction, and carry that back into every prioritization decision.

 - Build direct relationships with clinical and executive customers at some of the largest health systems in the country. Understand their world, ship into their environments, and partner with GTM to drive adoption and expansion.

 - Own the metrics that matter. Define the OKRs, use quantitative and qualitative signal to prioritize, and stay accountable to the outcomes.

 - Define what best-in-class AI-native healthcare software should feel like. The category is being invented right now, and the products that win will be the ones providers actually love to use.

 - Choose your path as the team grows. Build toward managing PMs if you want to become a people leader, or stay hands-on and take on increasingly broad and strategic product surfaces as an IC. Both tracks are real, and both are valued.
   




WHAT YOU HAVE

We are hiring at both levels and calibrate scope to experience.

 - Senior PM: 3+ years of product management experience, with strong generalist fundamentals and a track record of owning products end to end.

 - Staff PM: A track record of setting strategy, driving complex product areas across multiple teams, and influencing senior cross-functional stakeholders.

Across both levels, we're looking for:

 - Familiarity with AI. You have used and reasoned about LLMs, agents, and evals. You keep up with the frontier and get excited about what's shipping this month, not last year.

 - Technical fluency to read documentation, understand APIs and integrations, and hold substantive conversations with engineers.

 - A structured approach to user research and a real track record of turning insight into shipped product.

 - Sharp written and verbal communication. You can write a PRD that aligns cross-functional teams across engineering, clinical, ops, and sales without a meeting, and hold the room when you do present, whether it's a design review, an exec update, or a customer pitch.

 - Curiosity and drive. You are the kind of person who studies the domain, not just the product.

 - Comfort with ambiguity and excitement about shaping what your role becomes.

 - Consumer product instincts. A sense for building things end users actually love, not just products that clear procurement.

 - Genuine passion for healthcare. Clinical experience, time at a healthtech company, or meaningful work alongside providers is a plus, but what matters most is that you care deeply about the space and want to spend your time changing how care gets delivered.
   
   


THE TEAM

We are a large and fast-growing team. High trust, low ego, and a strong bias toward jumping in to help. Product, engineering, design, clinical, and ops sit close and move as one team.



WHY THIS MATTERS

Every product decision you make either gives a provider back time with a patient or takes it away. Not many jobs let you feel that on a weekly basis. This one does. You are raising the quality of healthcare in the US, one shipped decision at a time.



WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT

 - Location: 3+ days in Mountain View

 - Travel: Light, mostly for onsite hospital and provider shadowing

 - Ownership: A real product surface end to end from day one

 - Growth: Clear path toward PM leadership as the team scales

 - Impact: Your work reaches tens of thousands of clinicians and the patients they serve every day

jobs.description:
About Axiom:

Axiom is where legal teams go to find the right talent for everything from routine in-house tasks to complex outside counsel work. Too many legal departments are stuck having to choose between paying the high fees of their law firm, hiring full-time employees they don’t need, or turning to a low-cost agency that can’t meet their quality standards. At the same time, top lawyers want to work on challenging legal matters, but they want more control over how, when, and where they practice. Both are forced compromises that no one should have to make. Axiom shares and meets the higher standards of its clients and lawyers, with our “work smarter, adapt faster, go further” approach – connecting growing mid-market and Fortune 500 companies with the world’s deepest bench of experienced, specialized legal talent.

About the Role:

Axiom is hiring for a highly motivated, thoughtful Director, Talent Success to lead a team of Talent Success professionals who support Axiom’s talent experience for our ever-growing population of legal talent, matching them to client opportunities. The Director, Talent Success will be aligned to a specific group of Axiom’s legal practice areas, managing the team who cover those practice areas. This is an exciting opportunity for a strong problem solver with exceptional operational and people management skills to be part of an exciting and innovative team, driving change both within Axiom and the wider legal community.

Responsibilities:

• Lead and manage a team of Talent Success associates, managers, and senior managers providing oversight and guidance on day-to-day priorities while ensuring a consistently high-quality experience for Axiom talent and the delivery of strong, well-aligned client submissions.Collaborate with Talent Success Leaders cross-functionally to refine the processes and procedures of the Talent Success role, ensuring the successful launch and continuous development of the function.

• Work directly with sales leaders and sellers to ensure the Talent Success team effectively manages opportunities and quickly develops high quality submissions that match client needs, helping close client deals and reduce supply losses

• Collaborate with Sales leadership and Talent Acquisition through regular supply and demand meetings to align on bench needs, share market insights that equip TSPs and sellers to set informed client expectations, and provide stakeholders with visibility into current bench health relative to market demand.Coaching and developing team members to success, including sharing best practice and working with enablement to ensure the team is set up to provide next level client and lawyer service.

• Support the successful training and onboarding of new Talent Success Team Members, using the Talent Success playbook and training tools.

• Accountability for the culture of the team and responsibility to ensure that the team is enabled to perform to the highest standards.

• Act as escalation point for the Talent Success Team as required when complex talent issues arise.

• Drive data-informed execution and continuous operational improvement by identifying opportunities for innovation, enhancing efficiency, and partnering with the Global Head of Talent, Talent leadership, and cross-functional stakeholders to develop and implement solutions.Keeping ahead of industry trends in the legal and talent sector to enable better client service and empower team.

• Meet key Talent Success metrics and KPIs

• Direct contribution to company revenue and growth with an expectation to be strategic and think ahead to the growth and development of the team over a longer-term horizon.

• Oversee and ensure accountability for the ongoing development and performance management of the talent population, ensuring the team proactively coaches talent, identifies emerging performance concerns, and effectively manages performance-related roll-offs. Partner closely with Sales, HQ, clients, and PAX to ensure performance issues are surfaced, addressed, and resolved in a timely and effective manner.

Desired Experience, Skills & Abilities:

• 7 + years of experience within a professional services firm, law firm, recruitment agency, or corporate in-house environment.

• Demonstrated ability of leading, managing, and inspiring others.

• Relentless focus on the business needs and consistently raises the bar on service excellence.

• Significant project management experience and meticulous attention to detail

• Demonstrated ability to work in a collaborative, highly matrixed work environment.

• Highly persuasive verbal communication skills, strong written communication skills

• Deep sense of urgency, pace, and drive.

• Critical thinking and creative problem-solving skills

• Legally eligible to work in the country in which the position is located

• Legal experience is preferred, but is not required

Axiom’s total rewards philosophy is to be transparent and equitable with all job candidates. The annual base salary for this U.S.-based remote role is $127,000. You will also be eligible to participate in our Quarterly Bonus Plan which on target would be 50% of your base salary for a Director-level role in our Talent Success business unit. You can also participate in our benefits programs, which include healthcare, life and disability coverage, a 401(k) with company match, paid sick and personal time off, paid parental leave, and more. jobs.description:
Human Interest is on a mission to ensure that people in all lines of work have access to retirement benefits.

More than half of all working Americans are not saving enough for their future. Too often, it’s because they are employed by a company that doesn’t offer a retirement plan. Human Interest is changing that by making it affordable and accessible for small and medium-sized businesses to offer employees a path to financial independence through retirement savings.

We’re a high-growth fintech company changing the retirement industry. We are backed by a number of investors. This includes funding from Marshall Wace and Baillie Gifford, as well as top investors such as BlackRock, TPG (The Rise Fund), SoftBank, Glynn Capital, NewView Capital, USVP, Wing, Uncork, and more.

About the role

Our Partnership Program is a key initiative for the company. The Partner Account Manager’s primary duty is to engage, build and develop Human Interest’s key accounts and growth opportunities. We're looking for a forward-thinking, meticulously organized, and self-motivated sales professional who can thrive in a fast-paced environment.  You'll accelerate our partner relationships to help us exponentially reach more small and medium businesses across the United States, which is essential to our growth. This role requires someone who is proactive, creative, and can exercise their own discretion and judgment to create their own solutions when needed.

What you get to do every day

• Develop, build, and amplify referral relationships with tech partners, human capital management partners, benefit brokers, CPA's and financial advisors in the SMB space

• Create and build strategic referral networks and partnerships focused on lead generation and new partnership opportunities

• Proactively identify and resolve emerging issues and offer solutions by working cross-functionally with Sales, Product, Marketing, Legal and Finance

• Work with partners to establish business goals and performance metrics (e.g, depth of sales pipeline and revenue generation) to develop and execute effective go-to-market strategies and demand-generation activities

What you bring to the role

• 2+ years of experience building, developing, and maintaining relationships with tech and human capital management (HCM) partners, benefit brokers, CPA's and financial advisors in the SMB space (including territory sales and business development)

• Successful - Proven track record of success in a quota driven sales environment

• Passionate - You are a highly motivated individual contributor and relationship builder that can operate independently

• Dynamic - You can thrive in a fast-paced, and ever-changing environment

• Resilient—You bounce back from setbacks quickly, are resourceful, and find creative ways to get things done.

• Solutions-oriented - Willingness to get your hands dirty while managing and solving operational partnership issues

• Extraordinary communication and interpersonal skills — people trust you and sense that you are advocating for something you believe.

• Tech-savvy - familiarity using Salesforce to manage sales cycles is preferred

• Travel - Ability to be In the field 3 days/week. Must be located in Houston, valid Drivers License required

Why you will love working at Human Interest

Human Interest is tackling one of our country's biggest challenges - closing the retirement gap. You'll be instrumental in architecting and scaling solutions that bring financial security to employees at small and medium-sized businesses nationwide. We’ve made significant progress, but there is still growth ahead, offering you a unique opportunity to solve complex problems, drive innovation, and advance your career alongside a dedicated, mission-driven team. We value hard work and recognize that our team's contributions are key to our continued success.

Join Human Interest and make a lasting impact by shaping the future of retirement.

Our operating principles define how we work together as a team. They reflect Human Interest’s unique view on what’s important and what’s right. Documenting this core aspect of our culture helps employees make good decisions on their own. It also helps candidates considering career opportunities critically evaluate whether they will thrive at Human Interest.

• Long-Term Orientation: We're not just playing for today; we're building a legacy. We think big, plan strategically, and invest in our future.
