jobs.title: Senior Program Director, Delivery  (US)
jobs.location: New York, New York, United States
jobs.description:
As a Senior Program Director at Code and Theory, you will lead the Delivery capability for a portfolio of clients and/or a major account, setting the strategic direction for delivery and ensuring the overall health, growth, and performance of your assigned delivery portfolio. You will manage and mentor team members at all levels within Delivery (Associates up to Directors), cultivate deep product and digital transformation expertise across your team, and serve as a senior escalation point for clients and internal leadership alike.

A great Senior Program Director operates at both the strategic and operational altitude: you drive excellence in delivery, own scope and budget integrity across your group, and represent Delivery as part of your portfolio leadership team. Given the growing complexity of our client engagements, we're especially looking for someone with strong grounding in enterprise-scale business and digital transformation — ideally with experience delivering within marketing technology (martech) and digital experience platform (DXP) ecosystems — who can bring that expertise to bear across a broader portfolio.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Oversee the overall health and performance of delivery portfolios, driving the team to excellence across a portfolio of clients and/or a major account.

• Serve as an expert in estimation and scope development; lead and delegate business reviews of scopes, and serve as the delivery reviewer of budgets and contracts.

• Act as an escalation point for accounts and projects, both internally and externally; define and drive resolution paths, mitigating issues in collaboration with discipline leads.

• In partnership with Client Engagement, connect with clients in a steering and escalation capacity, acting as a senior point of contact for issue resolution and account growth.

• Partner with Resource Management and Recruiting to staff projects, ensure account needs are covered, and plan for future staffing needs.

• Partner with Client Engagement and Business Development on organic and new business needs, ensuring growth targets are met; provide recommendations on growth and investment opportunities.

• Evaluate project health weekly, collaborating with portfolio leadership peers and account/project leads on health concerns.

• Manage, mentor, and cultivate team members at all levels within Delivery (Associates up to Senior Directors), including ownership of performance reviews and growth plans.

• Where portfolio work touches enterprise transformation or martech/DXP initiatives, bring credibility and informed POVs across those ecosystems (e.g., Adobe AEM, Workfront, Adobe Experience Cloud, CMS/DXP, content supply chain, analytics/measurement, AI-enabled capabilities) and help orchestrate multi-workstream, dependency-heavy programs.

• Identify and drive change-related processes and tools — including AI-driven approaches — that enable the team to work more effectively and efficiently.

• Act as a lead champion for the Delivery discipline, driving process improvements directly or through Senior Directors and Directors.

• Actively participate in new business pitches, ensuring staffing, delegation, and budget/scope plans are rationalized against client needs.

• Foster a spirit of commitment, collaboration, and positivity that builds trust with internal teams and clients.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

• 10–15+ years of program/delivery management experience, with deep expertise in product and digital transformation delivery.

• Strong preference for experience delivering enterprise-scale transformation programs within marketing technology and digital experience platforms; familiarity with ecosystems like Adobe (AEM, Workfront, Adobe Experience Cloud) is a strong plus.

• Proven experience owning scope, estimation, and budget integrity for complex, high-value engagements.

• Proven people leadership managing, mentoring, and developing team members at all levels within Delivery (Associates up to Senior Directors), including performance reviews and growth planning.

• A track record of serving as a trusted escalation point for clients and senior stakeholders, with the judgment to know when to resolve directly versus mobilize others.

• Strong financial acumen, including comfort partnering with Finance on revenue planning, investment decisions, and account health.

• A change-agent mindset, with a history of driving process and tooling improvements at a department or agency level, leveraging AI to accelerate work.

• Strong technical acumen to drive work forward in partnership with cross-discipline leads, translating technical complexity into clear, actionable delivery plans.

• Understanding of different project management methodologies, with the ability to adapt approach to client, account, and agency needs.

• Exceptional interpersonal skills — clear communication, emotional intelligence, and the ability to influence and align diverse stakeholders.

• Experience contributing to new business pitches, in a senior oversight or hands-on capacity.

ABOUT US

Born in 2001, Code and Theory is a digital-first creative agency that sits at the center of creativity and technology. We pride ourselves on not only solving consumer and business problems, but also helping to establish new capabilities for our clients. With a global client roster of Fortune 100s and start-ups alike, we crave the hardest problems to solve. We have teams distributed across North America, South America, Europe, and Asia. The Code and Theory global network of agencies is growing and includes Kettle, Instrument, Left Field Labs, Create Group, Current, and TrueLogic.

Striving never to be pigeonholed, we work across every major category: from tech to CPG, financial services to travel & hospitality, government and education to media and publishing. We value the collaboration with our client partners, including but not limited to Adidas, Amazon, Con Edison, Diageo, EY, J.P. Morgan Chase, Lenovo, Marriott, Mars, Microsoft, Thomson Reuters, and TikTok.

The Code and Theory network is comprised of nearly 2,000 people with 50% engineers and 50% creative talent. We’re always on the lookout for smart, driven, and forward-thinking people to join our team.

The compensation range for this role is $200,000 – $235,000. Actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, budget, and location.

jobs.title: Information Systems Security Officer
jobs.location: Remote; Washington, District of Columbia, United States
jobs.description:
Vannevar builds AI systems for the Department of War's most consequential missions. We have 125 deployments across every branch and combatant command spanning our core platform and five distinct products. An an example of how we work, when major combat operations started with Iran, we fielded a new product supporting 24/7 operations and 9,000+ users in three months.

How we build is our advantage: we deploy forward with the people who own the mission. Our engineers, product team, and CTO deploy forward to the point of friction, including visiting units in Ukraine. We focus on embedding directly with operational units supporting great power competition with China, combat operations with Iran, and counter-narcotics missions.

About the role

As an Information Systems Security Officer (ISSO), you will help get our products authorized and keep them authorized. Supporting our ISSM and government ISSMs, you will own day-to-day security and authorization work across multiple systems, spanning cloud (FedRAMP, DoD IL5) and classified (IL6, Secret, TS/SCI) systems. You will partner with engineering, AppSec, and DevOps to keep packages current, keep controls verifiable, and move our systems toward continuous ATO (cATO). This is a hands-on technical role that directly shapes how quickly our software reaches the mission.

What you'll do

• Build and maintain ATO and IATT packages (SSPs, FIPS 199 / CNSSI 1253 categorization, CRMs, POA&Ms) under NIST SP 800-37, NIST SP 800-53, FedRAMP, the DoD Cloud Computing SRG, and JSIG.

• Assess security controls across cloud and on-prem classified systems (IAM, logging, encryption, network segmentation) and document inheritance from cloud and hosting providers.

• Complete DISA STIG checklists and run vulnerability scans, then drive remediation with engineering.

• Support cATO and continuous monitoring (NIST SP 800-137): automate evidence collection, review changes for security impact, track POA&Ms, and keep eMASS and Xacta current.

• Respond to customer security questionnaires and coordinate with government customers and third-party assessors.

• Monitor deployed systems for unauthorized changes and suspicious activity, and support incident response, audits, and media sanitization.

• Maintain security policies and procedures aligned to customer and authorization requirements.

What you should have

• Active TS/SCI clearance

• 4+ years in cybersecurity, including 2+ years as an ISSO, ISSE or in a similar authorization role on DoD, IC, or federal systems

• Hands-on ATO experience under NIST SP 800-37 and 800-53 in cloud and classified environments

• Working knowledge of cloud security (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and on-prem classified systems, plus familiarity with containers and microservices (e.g., Kubernetes) and Git-based change management (e.g., GitHub)

• Experience with eMASS or Xacta, DISA STIGs, and SCAP/SCC or ACAS scans

• DoD 8140 compliant certification (Security+ CE or higher)

• Clear, concise writer who can explain controls to engineers and authorizing officials

Nice to have

• DoD IL5/IL6, FedRAMP High, or cATO experience

• AWS GovCloud and cloud security tooling such as Wiz, CrowdStrike, or Splunk

• Scripting in Python, Bash, or PowerShell

• CISSP, CCSP, or AWS Certified Security Specialty

Benefits:

• Health, dental, and vision insurance

• 100% remote - work from anywhere in the US

• 401k matching

• Mental benefits

• Flexible work environment - you manage your workday

• Pet and child care reimbursement during travel

• Unlimited PTO

Compensation
The salary range for this position is $120,000 - $160,000 + equity + 401K match.

We hire across multiple levels based on experience, technical capabilities, and scope of responsibility. This range reflects the base salaries we typically expect to offer for this role, with individual offers determined by the candidate's qualifications and level.

Equity is offered in addition to base salary.

We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply, even if you don't feel like you're a perfect fit. If you're passionate about contributing to our mission, we'd love to hear from you!

IMPORTANT NOTICE

Under no circumstances will a legitimate representative from our company contact you to request passwords, financial information, or other sensitive personal data. jobs.title: Senior Corporate FP&A Analyst
jobs.description:
Come Join Us!

From apartments in New York to hospitals and stadiums in Dallas, libraries at prestigious universities to creating modern retail experiences, our teams contribute architectural glass and building products to projects that shape the way people live, work, heal, learn, and play. At OBE, the work of our employees truly matters. With over 6,500 employees, we operate more than 80 manufacturing and distribution facilities in five countries. You can see some of our favorite projects here.

Start your journey with OBE and help us build the future.

Position Summary

The Senior Corporate FP&A Analyst supports enterprise-wide financial planning, forecasting, reporting, and decision-making across manufacturing and distribution operations. This role is responsible for consolidating financial results and forecasts, developing driver-based financial models, and delivering actionable financial insights to business leaders. The position partners closely with Accounting, Operations, Sales, Supply Chain, Procurement, and Finance teams to improve business performance and support strategic objectives.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Financial Reporting & Consolidation

• Consolidate monthly actual results, forecasts, annual budgets, and long-range plans across business units, operating locations, and corporate functions.

• Validate business unit submissions and reconcile consolidated reporting with Accounting results, researching discrepancies and maintaining reporting consistency.

• Prepare assigned portions of monthly operating review packages, including variance analysis, commentary, and supporting schedules.

• Develop monthly and quarterly management reporting highlighting performance against budget, forecast, and prior-year results, including identification of key business drivers, risks, and opportunities.

• Create and maintain executive reports, KPI dashboards, financial presentations, and supporting analyses.

Planning, Forecasting & Analysis

• Support annual budgeting, recurring forecasting, and long-range planning processes.

• Build and maintain driver-based financial models covering revenue, pricing, volume, mix, material costs, labor, overhead, operating expenses, capital expenditures, and cash flow.

• Conduct scenario planning, sensitivity analysis, profitability assessments, and investment evaluations to support business initiatives and operational decisions.

• Analyze financial and operational performance to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for improved profitability and resource allocation.

Business Partnership

• Partner with Operations, Sales, Supply Chain, Procurement, and functional leaders to understand performance drivers and translate operating plans into financial expectations.

• Evaluate site, product, customer, and channel performance, including revenue, margins, material costs, labor, overhead, inventory, logistics, productivity, and capital investment returns.

• Provide recommendations to improve financial performance, cost management, and operational efficiency.

• Support process improvement initiatives focused on reporting automation, data quality, and FP&A effectiveness.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related discipline.

• 3-5 years of experience in Financial Planning & Analysis, Corporate Finance, Financial Reporting, Business Finance, or a similar analytical role.

• Manufacturing, distribution, industrial, or building products industry experience preferred.

• Strong background in budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, management reporting, and financial modeling.

• Understanding of financial statements and key manufacturing financial drivers, including revenue, margins, material costs, labor, overhead, inventory, and capital spending.

• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.

• Experience working with ERP systems and financial planning platforms such as SAP, Planful, or similar tools.

• Experience with Power BI or other business intelligence platforms preferred.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and presentation skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail.

• Demonstrated business acumen, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to convert complex financial data into actionable business recommendations.

Preferred Competencies

• Financial modeling and forecasting

• Strategic and operational analysis

• Executive reporting and presentations

• Data analytics and visualization

• Cross-functional collaboration

• Process improvement and automation

• Business partnership and stakeholder management

• Decision support and performance management

jobs.title: 3rd Shift Maintenance Technician( Facilities III).
jobs.description:
At SanMar, the work you do makes a difference.

Position: 3rd Shift Maintenance Technician( Facilities III).

Shift: 10:00PM-6:30AM.

Salary Range: $21.50-$28.94.

SanMar is widely known for its friendly, family-oriented culture and its diverse workforce. The company values creating a welcoming and inclusive environment where employees from different backgrounds can feel respected, supported, and part of a team.

This position is responsible for maintaining and repairing buildings, mechanical equipment, conveyor systems, and facility systems to ensure they operate safely and efficiently. Duties include performing preventive and corrective maintenance, inspecting and replacing equipment components, responding to emergency maintenance requests, coordinating with contractors and vendors, maintaining equipment records and HAZMAT documentation, and using a CMMS to monitor and schedule maintenance. The role may also involve basic electrical and security-system repairs, building renovations such as drywall repair and painting, outdoor custodial duties, ordering parts and supplies, operating powered lift equipment, and recommending improvements to maintenance operations while following all safety policies, laws, and regulatory requirements. Previous experience working with conveyor systems is highly appreciated and considered a strong advantage for this position.

What's the Short Version?

The Facilities III, DC is responsible for performing highly diversified duties to install, troubleshoot, repair, and maintain production and facility equipment. They also perform general maintenance and janitorial duties as needed.

What Will You Be Doing?

• Perform minor and major repair of all buildings and equipment.

• Perform preventive maintenance procedures on building mechanical equipment on a scheduled basis; inspect belts, check fluid levels, replace filters, grease bearings, seals, etc.; repair or replace broken parts.

• Coordinate external contractors/vendors involved in the installation, commissioning, and maintenance of building systems.

• Complete daily, weekly, and monthly checklists on building equipment maintenance procedures and maintains records of scheduled maintenance procedures.

• Comply with all applicable laws and regulatory requirements; maintain all required HAZMAT records including maintenance.

• Respond in a professional and timely manner to management and internal customer inquiries and researches and resolves problems related to a facility’s operational issues.

• May operate a computer which controls and monitors mechanical equipment and utility systems.

• May repair electrical locks and control panels to maintain building security.

• Respond to emergency maintenance requests as required.

• Assist with the renovation/remodeling of buildings; repair plaster and drywall; paint building structures.

• Perform outside custodial duties such as snow removal as required.

• May obtain estimates for supplies, repair parts; order parts as needed.

• Make recommendations to programs or ideas to improve Maintenance.

• May be required to operate powered lift equipment.

• Perform other duties as assigned

• Comply with all policies and standards

What Are We Looking For?

• High School Diploma or equivalent

• 4-6 years of facility maintenance experience is required to include most of the duties and responsibilities as listed above and use of hand and power tools.

• Experience operating warehouse equipment is preferred

• Excellent organization, ability to prioritize daily responsibilities.

• Knowledge of facilities maintenance and custodial principles, procedures, and standards.

• May be required to complete and maintain SanMar’s Lift Operator Certification in compliance with OSHA guidelines.

• Self-motivator; needs to take initiative.

• Able to work both independently and within a team.

• Demonstrates ability to follow directions and change priorities or job duties as business needs require; support or rotate to other production functions as needed.

• Ability to work efficiently with minimal supervision.

• Responsible for checking out equipment and returning in same condition.

• Responsive to staff needs, demonstrating professionalism, respect, and consideration of others always

• Comprehend verbal and written instructions.

• Demonstrated verbal and written communication skills.

• Strong attention to detail.

• Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals. Ability to compute rate, ratio, and percent and to interpret miscellaneous drawings and schematics.

• Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out detailed but uninvolved written or oral instructions.

• Ability to deal with problems involving a few concrete variables in standardized situations.

• Regular and prompt attendance.

• Overtime as required, which may include weekends.

What Should You Expect?

DC Warehouse (Equipment): While performing the duties of this job, the employee is constantly required to stand, walk, talk and hear. The employee frequently lifts and/or moves up to 60 pounds. The employee operates powered equipment requiring use of both hands as well as full range of motion of the neck, head and back. The employee is frequently required to reach with hands and arms, grasp and perform repetitive hand, wrist and arm motions. The employee is frequently required to climb stairs, kneel/squat, bend and carry. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus. Employee may be required to wear a headset covering one or both ears. Employee will be required to wear Personal protective equipment such as a Protective harness while operating equipment. Basic English literacy is required for operation of machines and necessary daily paperwork. Work environment is moderately noisy. The employee is occasionally required to work near conveyor systems. There is exposure to dust and changes in weather conditions. Work is performed under typical warehouse conditions. Potential hazards exist with regard to machinery such as forklifts, pallet jacks, mechanized systems, etc. Work environment is hectic and fast-paced.The employee is regularly exposed to ambient lighting and can be exposed to extreme heat and extreme cold including climates consistent with outside weather conditions.

Why Work at SanMar?

Our people are at the heart of everything we do. They bring their talent, passion and dedication to work with them every day. Their hard work inspires us and gives us purpose. We love working here together.

Whether you work in our headquarters, from your home or in one of our distribution centers across North America, we believe that investing in you is just the right thing to do. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to support your health and well-being, life balance, career growth and (eventually) retirement.

SanMar works with brands you already know, like Nike, The North Face and Brooks Brothers, as well as providing industry-leading private label apparel and accessories. Our people come to work excited to do their part, providing clothing that helps people feel that they’re a part of something special.

Here’s your chance to be a part of this story. If you’re ready to work in a place where your participation matters and your growth is a priority, we’re ready for you.

SanMar is an Equal Opportunity Employer

Whoever you are, wherever you’re from, whoever you love or follow in faith, whatever your disability or superpower status, whichever ethnicity or gender you identify with, you are welcome at SanMar.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Field Medical
jobs.description:
About This Role:

The Executive Director, Field Medical is a strategic Medical Affairs leader responsible for overseeing and optimizing ITF Therapeutics' field medical organization across neuromuscular and neurometabolic disease areas. This highly visible leadership role will provide strategic guidance, operational oversight, and people leadership to two Field Medical Directors responsible for leading disease-specific Medical Science Liaison (MSL) teams.

The Executive Director will play a critical role in shaping field medical strategy, ensuring execution excellence, and aligning field medical activities with broader Medical Affairs and corporate objectives. This individual will serve as a key member of the Medical Affairs leadership team, partnering closely with Clinical Development, Medical Strategy, Patient Advocacy, Commercial, Market Access, Regulatory Affairs, and External Experts to support the ongoing growth of ITF's rare disease portfolio.

The ideal candidate brings significant field medical leadership experience, deep knowledge of the rare disease landscape, and a demonstrated ability to build, scale, and lead high-performing teams in fast-paced and evolving environments. Experience in neuromuscular disorders, neurometabolic disorders, or other ultra-rare disease settings is strongly preferred.

What You'll Do:

Field Medical Leadership & Team Development

• Provide direct leadership, coaching, and development for two Field Medical Directors overseeing ITF's Neuromuscular Disorders and Inherited Metabolic Disorders field medical teams.

• Foster a culture of scientific excellence, accountability, collaboration, and patient-centered focus across the field medical organization.

• Lead talent planning, succession planning, performance management, and professional development initiatives for field medical leadership and broader MSL teams.

• Establish organizational structures, processes, and capabilities that support current and future portfolio expansion.

Field Medical Strategy

• Partner with the Vice President, Medical Affairs and Patient Advocacy to develop and execute integrated field medical strategies aligned with corporate and therapeutic area objectives.

• Ensure consistent execution of field medical plans across therapeutic areas while enabling appropriate customization based on disease-specific stakeholder needs.

• Translate scientific, clinical, and healthcare ecosystem insights into actionable strategies that inform Medical Affairs planning and decision making.

• Establish annual objectives, strategic priorities, and performance metrics for the field medical organization.

KOL & External Engagement Excellence

• Ensure strategic engagement with key opinion leaders (KOLs), investigators, treatment centers, advocacy organizations, and other external stakeholders across the rare disease community.

• Guide field medical teams in identifying emerging scientific trends, evidence gaps, and unmet patient needs.

• Support congress planning, advisory boards, investigator engagement activities, and external scientific collaborations.

• Ensure field medical activities generate meaningful insights that inform lifecycle planning and evidence generation strategies.

Operational Excellence

• Develop and oversee field medical operating models, processes, systems, and governance frameworks.

• Establish field medical KPIs, dashboards, and performance reporting to measure organizational effectiveness and impact.

• Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance operational efficiency, stakeholder engagement, and execution quality.

• Collaborate with Medical Operations to optimize CRM utilization, field activity reporting, territory alignment, and scientific engagement planning.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Serve as a strategic partner to Clinical Development, Commercial, Market Access, HEOR, Regulatory Affairs, and Patient Advocacy colleagues.

• Provide field perspectives to support launch readiness, lifecycle management, evidence generation, and disease state education initiatives.

• Partner with Clinical Operations and Development teams to support study feasibility assessments, investigator relationships, and trial awareness activities.

• Ensure field medical activities remain compliant and appropriately differentiated from commercial activities.

Insights & Medical Governance

• Lead the collection, synthesis, and communication of actionable field insights to Medical Affairs leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.

• Identify opportunities to address evidence gaps through investigator-sponsored studies, real-world evidence initiatives, publications, and medical education programs.

• Maintain the highest standards of scientific integrity, compliance, and execution excellence.

• Ensure adherence to all corporate policies, industry regulations, and applicable healthcare compliance requirements.

Required Skills:

• Advanced scientific or clinical degree required (PharmD, PhD, MD, DO, DNP, or equivalent).

• Minimum of 15 years of pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or life sciences industry experience, with significant Medical Affairs leadership responsibility.

• Minimum of 8 years of field medical experience, including leadership of MSL teams and/or field medical organizations.

• Prior experience directly managing leaders of field medical teams, including Directors, Senior Directors, or equivalent field leadership roles.

• Demonstrated success building, leading, and scaling field medical organizations within rare disease, orphan disease, or specialty pharmaceutical environments.

• Deep understanding of Medical Affairs strategy, field medical execution, KOL engagement, medical governance, and insight generation.

• Experience supporting commercial launches and post-launch Medical Affairs initiatives preferred.

• Strong understanding of compliance standards governing Medical Affairs interactions with healthcare professionals and patient communities.

• Proven ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence executive stakeholders in complex matrix organizations.

• Demonstrated ability to thrive in entrepreneurial, high-growth, and evolving organizational environments.

• Prior experience working within startup or emerging biotechnology companies strongly preferred.

• Experience in neuromuscular disorders, neurometabolic disorders, genetic diseases, or other ultra-rare disease therapeutic areas strongly preferred.

• Excellent leadership, communication, presentation, and strategic planning skills.

• Ability to travel approximately 35-50%.

Preferred Skills:

• Experience supporting therapies for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), inherited neuromuscular disorders, metabolic disorders, lysosomal storage disorders, or other genetically defined rare diseases.

• Launch experience within rare disease Medical Affairs organizations.

• Experience managing field organizations across multiple therapeutic areas or franchises.

• Demonstrated success leading teams through periods of organizational growth, transformation, or portfolio expansion.

• Existing relationships within the rare disease, neuromuscular, or neurometabolic healthcare community are highly desirable.

Additional Information:

The base compensation range for this role is: $310,000 - $340,000. Compensation is determined through an analytical approach utilizing a combination of factors including, but not limited to, relevant skills & experience, job location, and internal equity.

jobs.title: Senior Scientist I/II - Solid Sate Characterization
jobs.description:
AbbVie Analytical Research & Development (Analytical R&D) is a global analytical scientific organization responsible for all CMC analytical activities related to the development of AbbVie's pharmaceutical products.  Our scope includes AbbVie's diverse pipeline of innovative small molecule medicines and spans from the selection of Discovery candidate molecules to Late Stage Clinical.  We are building a world-class team of scientists and leaders who will drive the advancement of industry-leading analytical capabilities and make meaningful contributions to advance AbbVie's pipeline of innovative medicines.  Careers in AbbVie Analytical R&D provide unique opportunities to work with global and cross-functional teams to drive exceptional science and innovative product development strategies.  We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.

Position Description:

This Senior Scientist – Solid State Characterization position will be in a technical specialty group - Physical Analytical Chemistry (PAC) withing Analytical R&D.  The PAC group is a global team of experienced and innovative scientists which utilize a diverse set of physical analytical tools to advance CMC development programs by providing insights and driving the understanding of materials, processes, and products.  Additionally, the group contributes to development and justification of control strategies and authors relevant sections of regulatory submissions across all development phases.

We are looking for a subject matter expert in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of drug substances (DS) and drug products (DP), from early form discovery through regulatory filing. The role focuses on single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), electron diffraction (3D ED/MicroED), Rietveld refinement, quantitative phase analysis (QPA), and phase-appropriate polymorph quantitation methods both in drug substance and drug products. The scientist will work closely with Molecular Profiling Drug Development, Process Chemistry, Formulation, Process Engineering, Analytical, Operations, Quality Assurance and CMC-Regulatory.

Key Responsibilities:

• Support new product development with advanced methods development and validations, technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements.
• Serve as technical SME in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of DS and DP; Responsible for PXRD method development for DS and DP, validation/technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements
• Serve as the PXRD expert for supporting solid form screening, identification, crystallinity, and stability studies; perform indexing, Pawley/Le Bail fitting, Rietveld refinement, and structure determination from powder data.
• Perform quantitative phase analysis: Quantify polymorphic and amorphous content in DS and DP using Rietveld, whole-pattern, and multivariate approaches, addressing low drug load, excipient interference, preferred orientation, and micro absorption.
• Apply advanced diffraction such as VT/VH-XRPD, in situ, synchrotron, and PDF analysis to study phase transformations and poorly crystalline/amorphous materials.
• Apply SCXRD and 3D ED/MicroED structure determination, including absolute configuration and crystal packing of APIs, salts, cocrystals, hydrates, and solvates; generate calculated powder patterns and CIF reports.
• Conduct orthogonal solid-state characterization including X-ray diffraction, thermal analysis, moisture sorption, microscopy, spectroscopy as applicable for solid form, impurity and stability studies
• Support solid form control strategies per ICH Q6A, author Module 3 sections and health authority responses, and ensure GMP and data integrity compliance.
• Highly autonomous and productive in performing laboratory work, method development and troubleshoot; processing, interpreting, and visualizing data to facilitate project team decisions
• Represent PAC on CMC teams, lead form-change investigations, mentor scientists, and implement new diffraction technologies.
• Build strong relationships with peers and cross functionally with partners outside of team to enable higher performance.
• Routinely demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in research or development activities and maintain a high level of productivity in the lab.
• Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, appropriate handling of materials, controlled drug and radioactive compounds, and GxP compliance, where applicable.

Qualifications:

• Bachelors, Masters, or Ph.D. in Chemistry, Material Science, Physics, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field typically with minimum 10 (BS), 8 (MS), or 0 – 2 (Ph.D.) years related industry experience.
• Strong technical background in solid state characterization, excellent analytical problem-solving, communication, presentation, and cross-functional collaboration skills. Capable of independently developing and troubleshoot analytical methods.
• Extensive hands-on PXRD experience, including indexing, Rietveld refinement, QPA, and polymorph and amorphous quantitation.
• Track record of developing and validating PXRD methods for DS and DP in a GMP environment, with knowledge of ICH Q2(R2), Q6A, Q14, and USP <941>.
• Expertise in small molecule SCXRD structure solution and refinement, including disorder modeling and absolute structure; and knowledge of 3D ED/MicroED approaches.
• Proficiency with tools such as Olex2, SHELX, CrysAlisPro, TOPAS, Diffrac Eva and DQuant, GSAS-II, HighScore, Mercury, and the CSD.
• Hands-on experience with DSC, TGA, hot-stage and polarized light microscopy, DVS, and strong data analysis and interpretation skills.
• Experience with Raman/FTIR/NIR, solid-state NMR, SEM, SAXS, micro-CT, and crystal structure prediction, and particle characterization is preferred.
• Experience with AI/ML and data science for automation of phase identification and Rietveld/QPA workflows, chemometrics, and Python or R scripting is preferred.
• Experience with biophysical characterization tools of nanoDSC, DLS, SEC-MALS, CD, AUC, nanoDSF in peptide, LNP and biologic materials, formulations and process characterization is preferred.
• Strong pharmaceutical industry experience in solid state characterization is preferred
• Ability to coordinate activities and work simultaneously on multiple projects, in a global, fast-paced setting where priorities may change quickly.
• High attention to detail and creative problem solving while exhibiting strong interpersonal skills and proven ability to work independently as well as part of cross functional teams
• Knowledge of instrument set-up, troubleshooting, management and maintenance.
• Experience extracting insights from multidimensional data sets, along with other physical analytical characterizations, and connecting to pharmaceutical materials, processes, and products
• Practical knowledge of organic structure, functional groups, chemistry, and modern spectroscopic techniques as applied to small-molecule analytical analysis.
• Create a learning environment, open to suggestions and experimentation for improvement.
• Embrace the ideas of others, nurture innovation and manage innovation to reality.

Applicable only to applicants applying to a position in any location with pay disclosure requirements under state or local law: ​

• The compensation range described below is the range of possible base pay compensation that the Company believes in good faith it will pay for this role at the time of this posting based on the job grade for this position. Individual compensation paid within this range will depend on many factors including geographic location, and we may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range. This range may be modified in the future. ​

Priority Focus: Executive administrative support is the primary responsibility; reservations support is provided on designated tasks. The General Manager sets overall priorities and resolves competing requests in consultation with the Director of Finance and Director of Revenue Management.

Key Responsibilities

Executive Office & Leadership Support

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Lifecycle
jobs.description:
About Life360

Life360’s mission is to keep people close to the ones they love. Our category-leading mobile app, Tile tracking devices, and Pet GPS tracker empower members to protect the people, pets, and things they care about most with a range of services, including location sharing, safe driver reports, and crash detection with emergency dispatch. Life360 serves approximately 107.7 million monthly active users (MAU), as of September 30, 2026, across more than 180 countries.

Life360 delivers peace of mind and enhances everyday family life with seamless coordination for all the moments that matter, big and small. By continuing to innovate and deliver for our customers, we have become a household name and the must-have mobile-based membership for families (and those friends who are basically family).

Life360 has more than 500 (and growing!) remote-first employees. For more information, please visit life360.com.

Life360 is a Remote First company, which means a remote work environment will be the primary experience for all employees. All positions, unless otherwise specified, can be performed remotely (within the US and Canada) regardless of any specified location above.

We are AI Native

We are building an AI native company where AI is an integral part of how we build and operate. AI tool usage during interviews varies by role. You may be asked to demonstrate proficiency with AI tools, discuss how you leverage AI, or complete interview exercises without AI assistance. Your Recruiter will provide clear guidance as you move through the interview process.

Undisclosed use of AI not previously discussed with or approved by your Recruiter may impact your candidacy.

About The Team

The Lifecycle team at Life360 owns the moments that decide whether a new member sticks. From the first app open through account creation, permissions, and the first seven days of habit-building, we shape the experience that gets families set up and on the map. Beyond onboarding, we run rapid, full-funnel experimentation, from store impression through activation, engagement, and reactivation, across in-app, push, and email. We own the experimentation platform and standards, so we can test anywhere in the product and scale what works. Our mission is to turn curiosity into connection, and connection into a habit that families rely on.

We are a product-minded, AI-Native engineering team. That means AI isn’t just a tool we use — it’s how we work. We’ve redesigned our team workflows around AI, treating it as a first-class collaborator at every stage: ideation, coding, testing, review, and iteration. We ship faster and go deeper because of it, and we’re looking for someone who wants to help define what that looks like at scale.

About the Job

Life360 is hiring an AI-Native Senior Software Engineer II for the Lifecycles team with full-stack (mobile & cloud)  experience who doesn’t just use AI tools, but thinks natively in them. You’ll be central to how the Lifecycles team builds products, where AI has reshaped how the entire team designs, builds, and ships.

You’ll design and build the moments that decide whether a new member sticks: the first app open, account creation and recovery, permission grants, the first seven days of habit-building, and the re-engagement touchpoints that bring people back. You’ll also run high-velocity experiments across the full funnel, from store impression through activation, engagement, and reactivation, across in-app, push, and email, to find the growth wins and scale them.

You’ll build and evolve our modern AI-Native engineering workflows — from how we write code, to how we run standups, to how we think about team velocity. You’ll publish AI-native engineering playbooks the broader Lifecycles org adopts.

Android experience is strongly preferred, though exceptional iOS, full-stack or backend engineers are also encouraged to apply.

For candidates based in the US, the salary range for this position is $148,000 to $216,000 USD. For candidates based out of Canada, the salary range for this position is 171,500 to 201,000 CAD. Note: Please be aware that the job title for positions in Canada will be "Developer" in lieu of "Engineer." We take into consideration an individual's background, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience in determining final salary. Base pay may also vary based on geographic location, with US work locations falling into one of three geographic tiers.

Total compensation is inclusive of equity compensation in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), as well as a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, financial, and other benefits.

What You’ll Do

• Design and build high-quality member features, including onboarding that gets them set up and on the map, the lifecycle experiences that keep them engaged, and reactivation moments that bring them back after they’ve churned.

• You design and implement high velocity experiments that find and scale what grows Life360.

• Work with AI (Claude Code) as a first-class collaborator — your primary workflow involves orchestrating agents to create specs, generate code and tests, verify results, and perform reviews.

• Help define and codify AI-Native engineering practices for the Lifecycles team, establishing playbooks the broader org can adopt.

• Build across the full stack as needed — shipping polished, performant, and reliable experiences to tens of millions of users.

• Collaborate closely with product managers and designers to turn complex user problems into elegant, scalable engineering solutions.

• Contribute to architectural decisions, code reviews, and a culture of craft and continuous improvement.

• Participate in on-call rotation and incident response.

• Use agentic workflows to dramatically increase the delivery of strong outcomes — moving faster without sacrificing quality.

• Mentor team members and contribute to team processes, technical standards, and help evolve the team's AI-native engineering practices.

• Support performance, reliability, and accessibility across the features you own.

• Develop our product with empathy for the humans using it: a new member stuck in a login flow, an existing member activating a new feature, or a parent unsure why the app is asking for their location. You see the product through their eyes, and you treat every drop-off as a person who needed something we didn’t give them.

What We’re Looking For

• 7+ years of experience building high-quality, consumer-scale software products.

• At least 1 year of hands-on experience prompting, evaluating, and building with LLMs.

• Strong proficiency in mobile development (Android preferred) — you know what great mobile UX feels like and how to build it. Web and backend experience (Java, Kubernetes, AWS) are valued alternatives.

• Proven ability to ship full stack experiences to production, including mobile apps and their supporting cloud backends.

• Deep experience with agentic workflows, prompt engineering, context window management, and MCP/function calling.

• A track record of using AI tooling to multiply your own output — not just as autocomplete, but as a genuine development partner.

• Strong communication and collaboration skills — you work well with product, design, and platform engineers.

• A genuine excitement for defining what it means to be AI-Native — you’re not waiting for the playbook, you want to write it.

• Bachelor’s Degree in a Technical field, or equivalent experience.

AI-Native Expectations

We use AI coding tools as a professional standard on this team. Here's what that means in practice:

• Daily use: You use AI coding assistants (we support Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot) for real, substantive tasks: analysis, coding, refactoring, testing, navigating codebases, and documentation. Not just research or autocomplete.

• Judgment and ownership: AI-generated code gets the same review you'd give any PR. You are accountable for everything you ship.

• Velocity: We expect senior engineers who use AI well to operate with meaningful leverage — doing more with the same time, taking on problems that would otherwise require a larger team.

• Team leadership: You share what works. You automate prompting strategies that others can build on and help teammates earlier in their AI workflow adoption get up to speed.

• Continuous learning: The tooling is changing fast. You stay current and bring recommendations to the team when something would meaningfully improve how we work.

Our Benefits

• Medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance plans (100% paid for US employees). We offer life and disability as well as supplemental plans for medical and dental for Canadian employees.

• 401(k) plan with company matching program in the US and RRSP with DPSP plan for Canadian employees.

• Paid parental leave.

• Mental Wellness Program & Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for mental well-being.

• Generous time off: flexible PTO, companywide holidays throughout the year plus summer and winter shutdowns.

• Learning & Development programs.

• Equipment, tools, and reimbursement support for a productive remote environment.

• Free Life360 Platinum Membership and Tile trackers.

AI Usage: We use AI to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Life360 hiring teams

Life360 Values

Our company’s mission-driven culture is guided by our shared values to create a trusted work environment where you can bring your authentic self to work and make a positive difference

• Be a Good Person - We have a team of high integrity people you can trust.

• Be Direct With Respect - We communicate directly, even when it’s hard.

• Members Before Metrics - We focus on building an exceptional experience for families.

• High Intensity, High Impact - We do whatever it takes to get the job done.

Our Commitment to Belonging

Life360 is an equal opportunity employer. We don’t discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or any other legally protected status. We believe diverse perspectives make us better, and we’re building a workplace that reflects the communities we serve. Don’t meet every qualification? Apply anyway.

jobs.title: Senior AI Developer Experience Engineer
jobs.description:
About Scribe

Scribe https://scribe.com is where exceptional people come to do the best work of their careers. More than 94% of the Fortune 500 use Scribe to own their specialized intelligence: the unique way their teams work, decide, and get things done. Our Specialized Intelligence platform automatically captures how work happens and turns it into a living asset for people and AI agents.

We're growing fast. Since our founding in 2019, we've reached 7 million users across 600,000 businesses. Based in San Francisco, we're a LinkedIn Top Startup, valued at over $1B, and backed by leading investors. Join us in our mission to transform how people work.



About the role

Scribe is hiring a Senior AI Developer Experience Engineer to own CI and test infrastructure, define observability standards, and build internal tooling. Our engineers already use Cursor, Codex, and Claude, with AI reviewers on every PR. You'll make that workflow faster, more dependable, and measurable, with clear human oversight.

This hands-on Senior IC role combines strong software and systems engineering with substantial autonomy and room to grow into Staff. You'll report to Rishabh Sharma and partner with Infrastructure, which owns continuous deployment and the production observability platform.



A note from your hiring manager

I lead AI-Native Engineering at Scribe, and DevEx is the team that makes every other engineer here faster and more confident: the path from an engineer's intent to production code they trust. That path runs through CI, feedback loops, shared standards, and the agentic workflows that increasingly write and review our code. Our engineers already work agent-first; the hard problem now is making the system underneath them fast, trustworthy, and measurable as traffic, headcount, and agent-generated code all grow by an order of magnitude. You'd own real parts of that system from day one, on a team that publishes its numbers and shuts down its own experiments when they don't work.

— Rishabh https://www.linkedin.com/in/rishabhsharma09/



Why This Role Matters

AI-assisted development depends on fast feedback, trustworthy validation, and useful context. When CI is slow or flaky, agents wait on it too, and they wait badly. When instrumentation is inconsistent, nobody can tell why something failed. This role improves software quality and developer experience while maintaining delivery velocity, using evidence from engineering workflows and developer feedback to decide what to improve and how to scale adoption.

You will tackle practical engineering challenges:

 - Workflow Reliability: How do we make CI and agent workflows fast, recoverable, and easy to diagnose?

 - Standards as Defaults: How do we turn shared engineering conventions into checks, libraries, and agent instructions, so the right way is the easiest way?

 - Evidence & Impact: How do we use telemetry and developer feedback to understand failures and evaluate whether our tools are actually useful?

What You'll Own

 - CI & Test Infrastructure. Own the speed and trustworthiness of CI on our main monorepo, from first push to deploy handoff: shard balancing, caching and fixtures, flake detection and quarantine, test discovery, and runner economics. Infrastructure owns continuous deployment; you're their most demanding partner.

 - Observability Standards. Define how Scribe instruments its software, and make the right way the default way: what goes to error tracking versus tracing, the context every event carries, and how errors join to traces. You turn these conventions into shared libraries, automated checks, and agent instructions so humans and agents follow them without having to remember, and you guard against cost and noise so the tooling stays within budget and useful. Owning teams run their own alerts and service targets; you make sure they're built on a consistent foundation.

 - Agent Workflows & Guardrails (shared with the DevEx team). Co-own our engineering bots (ReviewBot, BugTriage) and the deterministic checks that catch problems before human review. Make sure every system we run has a second operator, a runbook, and an adoption number reported alongside its quality number.

 - Developer Environment. Make the first ten minutes of any task cheap: local setup, worktrees, seeded databases, onboarding. When an engineer's environment breaks, you're who they want to hear from.

What Success Looks Like

Within 6 months:

 - CI: You've set baselines and delivered measured improvements: a sharply lower main-branch failure rate, faster required checks, and every test file either running in CI or explicitly waived.

 - Observability standards: A written standard is in place and enforced in code, not just documented. Errors join to traces, events carry consistent context, and error-tracking spend alerts before it hits a cap.

 - Shared ownership: Every system DevEx operates has at least two people who can run it.

Within 12 months:

 - Developer experience: Engineers rate build-and-test as a strength, not the weakest part of their workflow.

 - Standards by default: New services and agent-written code meet the observability standard by default, and compliance is measurable per team, never per person.

 - Evidence-driven delivery: You've taken at least one project from a written proposal with pre-set success and stopping criteria to a published result, whether it shipped or was shut down. Delivery velocity held steady or improved throughout.

The Ideal Profile

You combine strong engineering judgment with a practical understanding of how engineers work. You build useful tools, evaluate them with evidence, and help teams adopt and maintain them.

 - Earn Adoption: Understand engineers' needs and build tools teams choose to use because they improve daily work.

 - Work from Evidence: Establish baselines, combine operational data with developer feedback, and change direction when results warrant it. Define and defend useful metrics.

 - Measure Systems Responsibly: Use DevEx metrics to improve tooling, workflows, and team outcomes, without scoring or ranking individual engineers.

 - Experiment with Clear Boundaries: Define success measures and stopping criteria before trials, and be willing to stop approaches that do not deliver value.

 - Standards as Code: You'd rather ship a check, a wrapper, or a default than a policy doc, and you measure whether conventions are actually followed.

 - Internal Product Judgment: Take tooling from design through rollout, and turn recurring needs into documentation, templates, and reusable agent skills teams can maintain.

 - Build for Shared Ownership: Create understandable, documented systems that other engineers can operate, maintain, and improve.

 - Enjoy the Support Side: You like helping engineers get unstuck, and you treat recurring support requests as product signals rather than interruptions.

Must-Have Skills

 - Build & Test Systems Depth: Deep, hands-on experience owning test, lint, build, or CI infrastructure in a substantial codebase, in at least one ecosystem (TypeScript, Go, Python/Django, or similar), and enough systems judgment to learn the others. You can diagnose slow pipelines, flaky tests, and broken development environments.

 - Systems Engineering & Instrumentation: You design, build, and maintain dependable internal tools and integrations, and have hands-on experience instrumenting production systems with error tracking, tracing, and logs (e.g., Sentry, Honeycomb, OpenTelemetry), deep enough to set conventions others follow.

 - Practical AI Engineering: You use agentic coding tools daily and critically, and have built or adapted at least one AI development workflow that other engineers adopted, including context management, validation, and failure handling.

 - Evidence & Measurement: You can define a metric, defend it under pushback, and tell when it's being gamed. You're comfortable with SQL and analyzing operational data.

Bonus

 - Experience with Temporal or similar workflow orchestration engines for AI/agentic pipelines.

 - Deep experience with GitHub Actions internals or optimizing large test suites through sharding, caching, and test isolation.

 - Experience customizing agent harnesses or building reusable integrations for AI development workflows.

 - Experience designing developer experience measurement frameworks that combine operational data with developer feedback.

 - Experience in Series B–D startups or core platform/infrastructure teams in growing technology companies.

How We Interview

 - Our loop is a set of work samples, not puzzles.

 - In the agentic round and the take-home, you'll use AI tools, and we look at how you delegate, verify, and explain.

 - One round is a short paid take-home: a maintainer-facing analysis of a public repository, which you then defend live.

 - Every round is scored against the same five areas: engineering systems depth, agentic systems judgment, evidence and measurement, developer empathy and adoption, and platform stewardship.

Remote within the U.S., with two in-person team gatherings per year.

jobs.description:

ROLE DESCRIPTION

The Production Coordinator is responsible for supporting production planning, scheduling, and reporting across multiple production lines at our facility in Weirton, WV. WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

   - Proficient in Oracle Fusion reporting tools, analytics dashboards, and Excel..

   - Knowledge of Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP functionality
   
   - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
   
   - Attention to detail and data accuracy
   
   - Effective communicator across technical and operational teams
   
   - Process improvement and systems-thinking mindset

WHERE YOU'LL WORK:


This role is based at Form Factory 1 in Weirton, WV—an easy commute from the city of Pittsburgh, PA. This 550,000-square-foot facility is our hub for high-volume battery production and a leader in the new era of American energy manufacturing. Relocation assistance is available.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Quality Inspector
jobs.description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.


About the role

Robots only work if every part is exactly what it claims to be — and you're the one who makes sure of it. You'll be the final word on mechanical quality in our QC lab, using GD&T to catch what others miss and confirming that the parts going into our robots match the drawings they came from. Get it right, and every arm we ship starts on solid ground.


What you'll do

- Inspect mechanical parts and assemblies in the QC lab using GD&T (ASME Y14.5), catching deviations before they turn into downstream problems.

- Program and run CMMs and other advanced measurement equipment to verify parts against spec.

- Lead First Article Inspections for mechanical parts at launch and after any process change.

- Run process audits on production mechanical operations so quality holds steady as we scale.

- Mentor Receiving Inspectors on mechanical inspection techniques and GD&T fundamentals.

- Keep inspection records and traceability tight and audit-ready for all mechanical work.

- Take a seat on the Material Review Board and help resolve mechanical nonconformances.

- Review mechanical drawings for inspectability, and flag GD&T issues to NPI and Engineering before they cause rework.

- Support our 6S and FOD programs to keep the QC lab clean, organized, and safe.


What you'll bring

- 5+ years of mechanical inspection experience in a QC lab environment.

- Strong working knowledge of GD&T per ASME Y14.5.

- Hands-on skill with measurement equipment — CMM preferred, plus height gauges, optical comparators, and surface plates.

- Sharp drawing interpretation skills.

- The patience and precision to work through complex measurements without cutting corners.


Nice to have

- CMM programming experience with PC-DMIS, Calypso, or similar software.

- Experience inspecting industrial robotics or precision mechanical assemblies.


Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this role is $34-40/hour, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.
