jobs.title: Head of Community Relations, Compute
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic is building data center capacity across many sites at once, and for every site we own or lease we have committed to invest significantly in the host community, on terms we can stand behind publicly.

We're looking for someone to own our community benefits program end to end, across an international portfolio of many sites, so that every commitment is tracked, funded, paid on schedule and publicly reported. You'll negotiate the community-benefit terms with developers and other counterparties, from the term sheet through the lease, then manage those developers after signature, run the payouts and publish each site's yearly reports.

You'll work closely with our data center deal team, Finance, Legal and Policy. Our Community Engagement Managers own on-the-ground community relationships and community benefits agreements with local governments; this role owns the program end to end, including the deal terms behind it.

Responsibilities

Program management

• Own the commitments ledger: every community commitment, budget and payout at every site, and who holds the money
• Track payment schedules and rent recovery against each site's construction milestones, with Finance
• Manage developers after lease signature: make sure they actually hold and pay out community funds at our direction, send their data on time, and troubleshoot issues when they arise
• Run payouts: check who receives the money, run select programs, such as the electricity credit, through an outside partner, and publish who got what each year
• Own each site's yearly environmental and jobs reports: get the data from developers and utilities, have an outside firm check it, and publish it
• Track what is committed, signed, funded and paid, and where a deal is stuck
• Keep the terms we sign consistent with our public commitments
• Build and hire the team that runs this function on an ongoing basis

Deals

• Negotiate the community-benefit terms in developer leases and capacity agreements: who funds the community commitment, whether it sits on the developer's books or is recovered through rent, and when payments are made during construction
• Work the term sheets with developers and other counterparties, and partner with our data center deal team so these terms are in every new deal and expansion from the start
• Time each site's community commitments to its schedule: as early as the day after lease execution, and no later than substantial completion
• Build and maintain standard form templates for the community commitments and leases, so each new deal starts from an agreed position

You may be a good fit if you

• Have owned a program or portfolio end to end across many sites or deals, and kept named owners to dates
• Have negotiated incentive, tax and community commitments with state and local governments for new sites, and closed them as signed agreements
• Have worked with state and local officials across many markets, and know what it takes to get an agreement approved
• Know how data center sites come together: site selection, leases with developers, power and local approvals
• Have worked in economic development for a data center operator or other large infrastructure developer, on the company's side of the table
• Are fluent in the financial side: funds, payment schedules, how a cost is recovered through rent, and what sits on whose books
• Write clear term sheets and clear updates for executives
• Are comfortable building a function from scratch, quickly and with ambiguity
• Care about Anthropic's mission and about doing right by the communities that host our infrastructure

Strong candidates may also have

• Experience negotiating community benefits agreements
• A legal, tax or incentives-advisory background
• Experience in government relations or public affairs
• Deal experience outside the US (for example, Canada or Australia)

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$1—$2 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Lunar Engineer
jobs.description:
Vast is developing next-generation space stations and space infrastructure using an incremental, hardware-rich, and capital-efficient approach. Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to support a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and supporting a growing space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to design, build, and operate its own spacecraft in orbit. Next, Haven-1 is targeted to become the world’s first commercial space station, with launch anticipated in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced two new offerings leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo: Vast Satellite, a high-power satellite product line; and Vast Lunar Systems, power, communications, and habitats for the Moon.

Headquartered in Long Beach, California, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities capable of manufacturing America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for Mars, dedicated modules for government partners, and other crewed systems designed to unlock the expanding long-term space economy.

Vast is looking for Lunar Engineers, reporting to the Senior Vice President, Lunar Programs, to help develop the systems for Vast’s Lunar ecosystem. We are building on the technology, infrastructure, and knowledge from our Haven Demo, Haven-1, Haven Station, and Vast Satellite programs to take Vast to the Moon, giving this founding team an extraordinary running start. As one of the earliest engineers on the Lunar team, you’ll own your work end-to-end and help set the technical standards our lunar hardware will be built on.

This will be a full-time, exempt position located in our Long Beach, CA location.

Responsibilities:

• Serve as the responsible engineer for lunar hardware, systems, or analysis in your discipline, owning requirements, design, build, test, and flight readiness

• Design for the lunar environment, including vacuum, regolith and dust, extreme thermal swings and long lunar nights, radiation, and micrometeoroid impacts

• Lead trade studies and make architecture and design decisions in close partnership with power, thermal, avionics, structures, life support, and test teams

• Write and manage requirements and interface control documents, and close interfaces across subsystems

• Develop the analyses, models, and simulations needed to demonstrate performance against requirements

• Plan and execute development, qualification, and acceptance test campaigns, and drive issues to resolution

• Present technical trades, analyses, and risks at design reviews, and work with NASA, partners, suppliers, and customers as the program grows

• Adapt proven Haven and Vast Satellite technologies to lunar applications, and apply lessons learned from prior builds

• Help establish the design standards, processes, and practices the Lunar team will inherit as it scales

Minimum Qualifications:

• B.S. in mechanical, aerospace, electrical, systems, or materials engineering, physics, planetary science, mathematics, or a related technical field

• 4+ years of professional experience in spacecraft, aerospace, or similarly demanding hardware, systems, or test environments. Some roles require more experience, as noted in the posting for that role

• Demonstrated ownership of a hardware product, subsystem, system architecture, test campaign, or technical analysis from concept through design review, test, or flight

• Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal skills, and the ability to communicate technical information to cross-functional partners and customers

Preferred Skills & Experience:

• Experience on lunar engineering programs, or on hardware designed for other extreme environments beyond low Earth orbit

• Experience serving as responsible engineer on spaceflight hardware through qualification and flight

• Familiarity with NASA’s Artemis program, human-rating standards, and commercial partnership models

• Experience leading design reviews (PDR, CDR) and verification campaigns

• Experience in a fast-paced, hardware-rich startup environment with rapid design-build-test cycles and high ownership

• Experience standing up new capabilities, standards, or teams from the ground up

Discipline-specific experience we are looking for:

• Senior Mechanical Engineer, Lunar: Mechanical design for space applications with end-to-end hardware ownership; NX or equivalent CAD; mechanical, power, fluid, mechanism, and materials design; deployable structures such as solar arrays, booms, or masts; battery system design, sizing, or qualification; and leading hardware through functional, vibration, and thermal-vacuum testing

• Senior Systems Architect, Lunar: Design ownership, systems integration, and test, including systems engineering work; ownership of system-level architecture, requirements, and interfaces; working knowledge of power, thermal, life support, avionics, communications, and structures; architecture trade studies; work with NASA or other government customers; and requirements and project management tools

• Senior Power Electronics Engineer, Lunar: Developing power electronics, with at least one product taken from architecture through hardware bring-up and validation; converters, distribution, and switching; radiation-tolerant part selection, derating, and screening; environmental testing; and vehicle and instrumentation buses such as Ethernet, CAN, SPI, I2C, and RS-422

• Senior Thermal Engineer, Lunar: Spacecraft thermal engineering, including thermal model build and correlation for flight hardware; Thermal Desktop, SINDA/FLUINT, ESATAN, or equivalent; radiators, heat pipes, MLI, coatings, and heaters; lunar diurnal and survival design; pumped fluid loops; crewed cabin thermal control and airlock or EVA thermal experience; and TVAC and thermal balance testing

• Senior Test Engineer: Operation, design, and development of test systems, fluid systems, or hardware testing, with ownership of large test campaigns; experience across fluids and propulsion, structures and mechanisms, thermal vacuum, and avionics and power testing; standing up new test stands or labs; reading P&IDs and schematics; Python or MATLAB for test automation; and serving as test conductor for hazardous operations

• Senior Avionics Engineer: Designing and testing avionics or electrical hardware, with ownership from design through test and integration; flight computers, embedded systems, and data buses such as RS-422, CAN, SpaceWire, Ethernet, and MIL-STD-1553; radiation effects mitigation; Altium or similar PCB tools; and EMI/EMC and environmental testing

Additional Requirements:

• Willingness to work evenings and/or weekends to support critical mission milestones

• Ability to travel up to 20% of the time, depending on the role, to support customer meetings, suppliers, and test facilities

Pay Range: California

$147,000—$249,000 USD

We calibrate level and compensation to the selected candidate's experience and demonstrated capability. We welcome applicants across a range of experience levels to apply.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

Base salary will vary depending on job-related knowledge, education, skills, experience, business needs, and market demand. Salary is just one component of our comprehensive compensation package. Full-time employees also receive company equity, as well as access to a full suite of compelling benefits and perks, including: medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents, generous paid time off; up to 20+ days of vacation for exempt staff and up to 10+ days of vacation for non-exempt staff with the ability to cash-out unused vacation annually, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, ClassPass credits, personalized mental healthcare through Spring Health, and other discounts and perks. We also take pride in offering exceptional food perks, with snacks, drip coffee & onsite barista, cold drinks, and dinner meals remaining free of charge, and lunch subsidized as part of Vast’s ongoing commitment to providing high-quality meals for employees.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Vast is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with Vast is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Chief Credit Officer
jobs.description:
Taekus is a profitable fintech and travel company building a next-generation premium banking and rewards ecosystem for affluent customers. With more than $130M in annualized revenue and billions in annual transaction volume, we're entering a new stage of growth focused on scaling our banking platform, credit products, rewards infrastructure, and partner integrations.

As we prepare for the next phase of the business, including the development of our own bank, we're looking for an experienced Chief Credit Officer to lead our credit organization and establish the policies, governance, and risk management infrastructure necessary to support a regulated banking institution.




THE ROLE

The Chief Credit Officer will provide executive leadership over Taekus's credit function, overseeing credit strategy, portfolio management, underwriting governance, and credit risk management.

This is a senior leadership role focused on building and managing the credit organization, establishing sound banking practices, and ensuring the company is prepared to operate within a regulated banking environment.

A major component of the role will be supporting Taekus's new bank charter application and working directly with banking regulators, advisors, and internal leadership to develop the credit policies, procedures, governance frameworks, and supporting documentation required for regulatory approval.

The ideal candidate has at least 10 years of experience leading credit functions within an established bank and understands how to operate within a regulated banking environment. They should be comfortable working with regulators, presenting to senior leadership and boards, and building a credit organization that can scale alongside a growing financial institution.




RESPONSIBILITIES

Credit Leadership & Strategy

 - Own Taekus's credit strategy, policies, and risk management framework.

 - Establish risk appetite, underwriting standards, approval authorities, and concentration limits.

 - Oversee credit performance across existing and future products.

 - Balance portfolio quality, profitability, growth, and regulatory expectations.

 - Build and lead the credit organization, including hiring and developing senior personnel.

 - Establish credit governance, reporting, and escalation processes.

Bank Charter & Regulatory Engagement

 - Lead credit-related workstreams for Taekus's new bank charter application.

 - Develop credit policies, procedures, and documentation required for regulatory approval.

 - Work directly with banking regulators, including the OCC, throughout the application process.

 - Manage regulatory inquiries, examinations, and supervisory requirements.

 - Ensure credit operations meet applicable banking regulations and supervisory expectations.

 - Partner with Legal, Compliance, and Finance to address regulatory feedback.

 - Support ongoing examinations, audits, and regulatory reporting.

Credit Risk & Portfolio Oversight

 - Oversee portfolio performance, including delinquencies, losses, charge-offs, and concentrations.

 - Establish monitoring and reporting frameworks to identify emerging risks.

 - Review and approve material changes to underwriting policies and credit strategies.

 - Oversee credit loss forecasting, reserves, stress testing, and risk assessments.

 - Ensure appropriate model governance, validation, and documentation.

 - Maintain credit quality as the business scales and expands its products.

Executive & Cross-Functional Leadership

 - Serve as a senior leader and strategic partner to Taekus's founders.

 - Partner with Finance, Compliance, Legal, Operations, Product, and Technology.

 - Present credit performance and risk recommendations to executives, boards, and committees.

 - Build relationships with regulators, banking partners, auditors, and advisors.

 - Provide leadership, direction, and accountability across the credit organization.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Required Experience

 - 10+ years leading credit functions within a regulated banking institution.

 - Deep experience in credit governance, policy development, underwriting, and portfolio risk.

 - Proven ability to manage credit teams and senior risk professionals.

 - Direct experience with bank regulators, examinations, and supervisory reviews.

 - Strong understanding of banking regulations and credit risk management standards.

 - Experience presenting credit strategy and risk assessments to executives, boards, or committees.

 - Ability to oversee credit analytics and modeling without serving as the primary individual contributor.

Preferred Experience

 - Experience supporting bank formation.

 - Experience working with the OCC and FDIC.

 - Previous experience as the chief credit officer of a regulated bank.

 - Experience running credit policies and governance frameworks for a new or growing financial institution.

 - Experience overseeing consumer credit card or unsecured lending portfolios.

Join the Carvana team by applying on this page, or call one of our recruiters by phone at (888) 690-7853, Monday through Friday, between 6 AM and 4 PM PT (9AM to 7PM ET).

jobs.location: San Francisco, New York, Seattle, Chicago, Atlanta, Remote in the US
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Marketing Strategy & Operations team is responsible for driving organizational effectiveness and leading transformational programs across Marketing, Self-serve, Startup and Sales Development. We create the processes and conditions that enable high performance across teams and help Stripe scale with focus and discipline.

We partner closely with the CMO, Marketing and Sales Development leadership team to define strategy, lead operational planning, and steward execution across global programs. This role partners directly with the head of Global Demand, Campaigns, and Field Marketing.

Our work spans cross-functional efforts that are critical to Stripe’s growth. From delivering strategic insights and frameworks to leading complex initiatives, we focus on what moves the needle most for the business. We care about results, not activity, and we have fun doing it. If you like hard problems, are analytical, and are an amazing teammate, we want to hear from you.

What you’ll do

Responsibilities

• Drive our annual strategic plan and operating plan, working in partnership with the Global Demand, Campaigns, and Field Marketing leadership team to define our must-wins, build plans to win, and allocate our resources to deliver on the plan.

• Define and manage our most critical OKRs that instill transparent, data-driven accountability for delivering our strategy to Stripe leadership.

• Run the core rhythms of the business and reporting to focus attention, inspection, and strategic steers in the right places at the right time.

• Drive critical leadership and team-wide communication forums (e.g. leadership onsites, all hands) to effectively cascade strategy and comms

• Leverage an AI-first approach to aggressively automate marketing reporting.

• Bring clarity to ambiguity; navigate complexity, distill insight from noise, resolve issues quickly, and empower teams to make smart, confident decisions.

• Work directly with senior leaders across the company and with cross-functional partners to accelerate progress, solve hard scaling initiatives, and incubate new programs.

• Own and improve the campaign operations process end-to-end across digital campaigns and events - from planning and briefing through asset production, regional activation, and performance measurement - with a focus on efficiency and collaboration.

• Build tooling and automation to integrate marketing workflows and automate global calendars of marketing activity and impact

• Define how we should effectively measure the success of our marketing efforts and align with Data, MarTech, and Eng teams to build the infrastructure to support our reporting goals

• Use data to tell a compelling story and drive alignment on where we’re winning and where we need to focus.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

• 10 years of experience in consulting, strategy and operations, business operations, product strategy, product management, or similar roles with exposure to both business and technical skills

• Proven people management experience leading a team in strategy and operations, marketing operations, or a similar function, with a track record of hiring, developing, and retaining high-performing talent

• Background in B2B marketing, and core capabilities of Campaign and Field Marketing (e.g. digital campaigns, events)

• Experience working in highly cross-functional settings, and in a role that spans strategy, analysis, and operations in a fast-paced environment

• Critical and first-principles thinking, with the ability to zoom out to the most important questions

• Passion for digging deep into data to diagnose business issues and solve problems

• Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to speak to leaders across teams including product, engineering, analytics, sales, and partnerships

• An ability to execute with minimal guidance and with a high degree of ambiguity

Preferred qualifications

• Prior experience in payments, finance, fintech, or high-growth technology companies

• Prior experience working directly with C-level executives and their direct reports

• Experience navigating large data sets and/or SQL

jobs.title: Revenue - Director of Special Projects and Continuous Improvement
jobs.description:
The Continuous Improvement Director leads the Continuous Improvement pillar within the Revenue Strategic Transformation division. This role identifies, prioritizes, and delivers process improvement initiatives that increase operational efficiency, reduce waste, and improve the experience of both employees and the residents and businesses the department serves.

The CI Director brings a disciplined improvement practice to a large public organization: mapping how work actually flows, finding where it breaks down, and redesigning it in partnership with the units that own it. Success depends on facilitation, analytical rigor, and the ability to see how decisions in one part of the department create consequences in another.

The CI Director owns the improvement methodology, process mapping and redesign discipline, customer satisfaction measurement, documentation standards, and the training that builds continuous improvement capability across the department. The role leads a small team and is expected to develop that team, not simply directing its work.

The CI Director works in close partnership with the Executive Director, who provides strategic direction, and coordinates with the division's other pillars: Operations, Project Management, Change Management, and Innovation and Advanced Analytics.

Essential Functions

Continuous Improvement of Methodology and Execution

• Design and maintain the department's continuous improvement framework, applying Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, root cause analysis, and process redesign methods as appropriate to each initiative.

• Lead current-state process mapping across business units, documenting workflows, identifying waste, rework, and handoff failures, and designing future-state processes in partnership with the relevant unit.

• Lead improvement initiatives from intake through implementation, ensuring changes are measurable, sustainable, and owned by the business unit responsible for execution.

• Design and maintain controls and monitoring mechanisms so improvements are sustained and do not revert to prior practice.

• Apply design thinking to identify where a local improvement would create downstream burden elsewhere, and design accordingly.

2. Intake and Prioritization

• Capture improvement opportunities from business unit requests, performance data, customer feedback, staff suggestions, and strategic priorities.

• Apply a structured prioritization framework covering feasibility screening, scoring, and portfolio balancing to select initiatives that deliver the highest value relative to effort and risk.

• Operate the shared intake and routing protocol with the Project Management Office and the Innovation and Advanced Analytics unit, so that improvement requests, project requests, and pilot concepts follow one clear path.

• Maintain a portfolio tracker providing visibility into active, pipeline, and completed initiatives with documented outcomes.

3. Customer Satisfaction Measurement

• Own design, distribution, and analysis of customer satisfaction surveys, including the external survey of residents and businesses and the internal business unit survey.

• Produce and distribute monthly reports with trend analysis and actionable insight.

• Route improvement opportunities identified through customer feedback into the intake process.

• Coordinate with Communications on distribution and messaging, and with Innovation and Advanced Analytics on data integration and reporting.

4. Standards, Procedures, and Process Documentation

• Establish departmental standards for processing documentation so procedures, workflows, and operational guides are created and maintained consistently across units.

• Provide templates, frameworks, and guidance to business units documenting their own processes, with Continuous Improvement serving as the quality standard-setter.

• Maintain a central repository of documented processes accessible to leadership and business units.

5. Training, Culture, and Team Development

• Develop and deliver a continuous improvement education plan tailored to three audiences: executive leadership for strategic awareness, managers and supervisors for application skills, and frontline staff for mindset and participation.

• Integrate a continuous improvement introduction into departmental onboarding in partnership with Human Resources.

• Identify and develop improvement champions within business units who sustain the practice beyond individual initiatives.

• Directly develop the Continuous Improvement Specialist and Project Coordinator, building their capability in process mapping, intake discipline, and initiative support.

6. Reporting and Impact Measurement

• Track and report measurable outcomes for each initiative: time saved, errors reduced, cost avoided, satisfaction improved, or other relevant metrics.

• Produce quarterly impact reports for the Executive Director documenting portfolio progress, results achieved, and lessons learned.

• Use outcome data to support the case for continued investment in staffing, tools, and initiative scope.

Competencies, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

• Proven leadership in strategic planning, organizational development, and change management.

• Expertise in Lean Six Sigma, process mapping, and performance benchmarking.

• Strong ability to lead cross-functional teams and foster collaboration.

• Excellent communication, facilitation, and presentation skills.

• Advanced analytical and data-driven decision-making capabilities.

Required

• Bachelor's degree in Public Administration, Business Administration, Organizational Development, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.

• Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in continuous improvement, process improvement, or operational excellence.

• Lean Six Sigma certification at Green Belt or higher, or equivalent recognized process improvement certification.

• Demonstrated command of improvement methodologies and the judgment to select the right approach for a given problem.

• Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional improvement initiatives from intake through measurable results.

• The ability to see how processes connect across an organization and how a change in one area affects others.

• Strong facilitation, analytical, and stakeholder engagement skills.

• Experience supervising, mentoring, or developing staff.

Preferred

• Master's degree in a related field.

• Experience in government, public sector, or nonprofit organizations.

• Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or equivalent advanced certification.

• Change management certification such as Prosci.

• Project management certification such as PMP.

• Experience designing and analyzing customer satisfaction surveys and Net Promoter Score programs.

• Experience building an improvement function where none previously existed.

More than half of all working Americans are not saving enough for their future. Too often, it’s because they are employed by a company that doesn’t offer a retirement plan. Human Interest is changing that by making it affordable and accessible for small and medium-sized businesses to offer employees a path to financial independence through retirement savings.

About the role

jobs.title: Store Associate (Part-Time)
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

At Copperstate Farms and Sol Flower, we’re creating a better kind of cannabis company. Where we know happy plants begin with happy people. We aspire to high standards, take pride in our work, and drive for better results every day. At the greenhouse, our roots are growing flower, but we’ve branched out to offer an extensive range of cannabis products like edibles, topicals, and concentrates for retail dispensary locations. From farm to market, we are committed to the quality of our products and are always testing for patient and customer safety. By bringing together best practices from big agriculture, consumer packaged goods, and pharmaceutical and retail industries, Copperstate is becoming one of the top cannabis companies to work for.

What We’re Growing:

As one of the largest greenhouse cannabis producers in North America, Copperstate Farms ranges over 1.7 million square feet of canopy and 40 acres under glass. It’s here where we have been growing a house of cannabis brands that our patients and customers can trust, each addressing a different needs state and demographic. From the greenhouse to corporate to multiple Sol Flower dispensaries, we’re an inclusive cannabis community empowering wellness for all. Most of all, we strive for a culture where our employees view us as one of the best places to work.

Job Description:

The Store Associate provides necessary support for dispensary operations either in Front of House (FOH) or Back of House (BOH) as needed.  In FOH, the Store Associate will provide outstanding customer service while assessing the needs of each customer to fit them with the best product. In BOH, the Store Associate will be responsible for all aspects of physical and digital inventory maintenance within the company and the processes associated with inventory control such as packaging, stocking, intake of all products, and inventory compliance. The Store Associate is a lifelong learner who is passionate about Cannabis and dedicated to providing an exceptional customer experience.

Core Responsibilities:

Duties of this job include, but are not limited to:

Front of House

• Greet all customers in a positive and professional manner.

• Provide exceptional customer service while accurately entering and processing customer information/transactions.

• Quickly and precisely handle cash and debit transactions while maintaining a balanced cash drawer.

jobs.title: Intern - Software Development Engineer
jobs.description:
About Amperity—Why This, Why Now

Most customer data is a lie by omission.

Every consumer brand wants to know its customers. Unfortunately, almost none actually do. Data is scattered across a dozen systems, half of it contradicts the other half, and "insights" teams are forced to act on incomplete guesses. We started Amperity ten years ago because that gap—between what a brand believes about its customers and what is true—is the most expensive problem in the industry, and nobody had solved it.

With a lot of hard work and a little bit of luck, we did. Our patented identity resolution takes billions of messy, conflicting records and resolves them into an accurate picture of a real human being—in hours, not months. That’s not a feature; it’s the foundation everything else stands on. It’s why more than 400 brands—like Alaska Airlines, Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, DICK’S Sporting Goods, Virgin Atlantic, and Brooks Running—trust us with the one thing they can’t afford to get wrong, and why IDC named us a Leader in the category in 2026.

Now we’re doing something harder. We’re rebuilding Amperity as an AI-first company—not bolting a chatbot onto old software, but putting agents at the center of how customer data actually gets used. We shipped the industry’s first identity resolution agent, then the first enterprise Customer Data Agent that turns a plain-language question into a live segment without waiting on an engineering queue. The bet underneath all of it is simple, and we think it’s correct: The potential of AI will not be realized for a brand until it’s grounded and activated against a true, unified view of the customer. The market at-large is focused on intelligence, and we are focused on being  the ones who can make it trustworthy.

So here’s the honest pitch. If you want a tour of a category that’s already been figured out, this isn’t it. If you want to help decide what the next version of an entire industry looks like—alongside people who are remarkably exceptional at what they do, solving a problem that requires deep, sustained focus—this is one of the few places that work exists. Our goal is to build a highly impactful, generational business.

We measure our success by one standard: whether what we build moves the business. Return on cognition, not return on hype. If that’s how you want to be measured, we would love to speak with you.

The Role

We’re looking for an intern to help design, build, and launch new features for Pér. In this role, you’ll help shape how the platform serves marketing, analytics, and IT professionals. You’ll roll up your sleeves to help build the inner workings of our products as we continue our accelerated growth.  We’re looking for someone who has a passion for making complex distributed systems operate and scale seamlessly while balancing cost efficiency, velocity, and customer experience. Our ideal candidate is eager to gain hands-on experience with how we’re applying AI across the platform and is excited about the opportunity to contribute to new, innovative product ideas in a rapidly evolving space.

Amperity internships are full-time (40 hours/week) for 14 consecutive weeks, starting June 14th and ending September 17th, 2027. By applying for this position, you will be considered for an in-person Seattle-based internship in summer 2027, at the previously mentioned dates.

Interesting Problems

• Building agentic systems to help marketing, business analyst teams, and executives make more accurate decisions at a faster rate.

• Build agentic systems that plan strategically, incorporating every learning from past experiments into future recommendations for marketers

• Build agentic systems that learn their users – their organization structures, business rhythms and systems, and adapts as their needs change

• Ingesting and cleaning large amounts of data daily and blending it with real-time events.

• Automatically stitching data together across disparate systems by training machine-learning models to build a probabilistic knowledge graph.

About You

• You are excited about using or learning AI-Assisted Development and working on products & features that will ship to real customers. You’re not just building internal tools for internal consumption.

• You are excited about software in general, ideally an active hobbyist with projects of your own outside of schoolwork.

• Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's degree program, preferably in a technical field (Computer Science, Engineering), Business, or a related discipline, with an expected graduation date between June 2027 and June 2028.

• You are excited about using or learning to use functional languages in a production environment

• You are excited about software in general, ideally an active hobbyist with projects of your own outside of schoolwork

• You have experience operating in production software environments, likely at a previous internship

• Strong desire to learn and investigate new technologies

Location

Seattle, WA

Amperity’s work model operates on four in-office days each week and one designated remote workday on Wednesdays. We value the collaboration, connection, and learning that come from working together in person.

Compensation

$55/hour

Benefits

Commuter Benefit FSA (Seattle-based employees), free gym access, on-site lunches, snacks and refreshments

Amperity is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, and reproductive health choices), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as someone with a disability, political views or activity, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law.

jobs.title: Manager, Autonomy Engineering
jobs.description:
May Mobility is transforming cities through autonomous technology to create a safer, greener, more accessible world. Based in Ann Arbor, Michigan, May develops and deploys autonomous vehicles (AVs) powered by our innovative Multi-Policy Decision Making (MPDM) technology that literally reimagines the way AVs think.

Our vehicles do more than just drive themselves - they provide value to communities, bridge public transit gaps and move people where they need to go safely, easily and with a lot more fun. We’re building the world’s best autonomy system to reimagine transit by minimizing congestion, expanding access and encouraging better land use in order to foster more green, vibrant and livable spaces. Since our founding in 2017, we’ve given more than 500,000 autonomous rides to real people around the globe. And we’re just getting started. We’re hiring people who share our passion for building the future, today, solving real-world problems and seeing the impact of their work. Join us.

This Manager will be responsible for leading the vision, strategy, and technical roadmap for ML Engineering functions at May Mobility.  This position plays a key role in advancing May’s core autonomy software stack, applying Autonomy Models to ML challenges across the organization, and charting the path for the supporting ML Platform and Operations infrastructure to maintain velocity.

• Ability to direct the architecture and maintenance of training, data, evaluation and optimization/release pipelines at enterprise scale.

• Mastery of the process for training and deploying Perception and/or Planning models for Robotics and/or Physical AI applications.

• Demonstrable success in directing groups of 3+ Engineers in cross-functional, physical and ML-related projects.

Qualifications and Experience

Candidates most successful in this role typically hold the following qualifications or comparable knowledge or experience:

Required

• Bachelor's degree in Robotics, Computer Vision, Machine Learning, Computer Science, Engineering, or a field that requires a strong mathematical and/or engineering foundation.

• A minimum of 5+ years of industry experience leading, deploying, or managing technical development for real-world robot systems related to perception, prediction, planning or equivalent technical fields.

• A minimum of 2 years in a technical lead or management role.

• Exceptional verbal and written communication skills for cross-team collaboration.

• Ability to travel approximately 4-6 times per year.

Desirable

• Master's or PhD in a related field

• Experience working within ML Ops and/or ML Platform teams

• Familiarity with real-time productization (compilation, quantization etc) of models for edge devices

Physical Requirements

• Standard office working conditions, which includes but are not limited to:

• Prolonged sitting

• Prolonged standing

• Prolonged computer use

• Travel required? - Moderate: Up to 30%

Benefits and Perks

• Comprehensive healthcare suite including medical, dental, vision, life, and disability plans. Domestic partners who have been residing together at least one year are also eligible to participate.

• Health Savings and Flexible Spending Healthcare and Dependent Care Accounts available.

• Rich retirement benefits, including an immediately vested employer safe harbor match.

• Generous paid parental leave as well as a phased return to work.

• Flexible vacation policy in addition to paid company holidays.

Don’t meet every single requirement? Studies have shown that women and/or people of color are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every qualification. At May Mobility, we’re committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workforce, so if you’re excited about this role but your previous experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway! You may be the perfect candidate for this or another role at May.

Join the Carvana team by applying on this page, or call one of our recruiters by phone at (888) 690-7853, Monday through Friday, between 6 AM and 4 PM PT (9AM to 7PM ET).

jobs.title: Data Center Engineer - Critical Faciliites
jobs.description:
Verisign helps enable the security, stability, and resiliency of the internet. We are a trusted provider of internet infrastructure services for the networked world and deliver unmatched performance in domain name system (DNS) services.

We are a mission focused, values driven company where each individual can contribute to building a stronger, more secure internet.  We offer a dynamic and flexible work environment with competitive benefits and the ability to grow your career.

We are seeking a Senior Critical Facilities Engineer (Data Center Operations) to serve as a technical resource and leader within the Global Data Center Operations Team. This onsite role at our Ashburn Data Center will play a crucial role in the day-to-day operations & capacity planning of mission critical systems.

The ideal candidate will have technical and program management expertise in the maintenance and operation of electrical, mechanical, and fire life safety data center systems as well as applicable base building support systems.  You will support the Director – Data Center & Facilities Operations as a technical lead.  While this is an individual contributor role, you must be able to direct and inspire highly skilled engineers, deliver on project timelines and be the technical point of contact for on-call escalations.  Clear and concise written and verbal communication skills along with experience developing Standard Operating Procedures, Emergency Operating Procedures and Method of Procedures utilizing technical writing standards are a must.

Mechanical responsibilities include chilled water systems and components, HVAC systems such as roof top units, CRAC/CRAH units, and humidification systems.  Electrical responsibilities will include electrical/critical power distribution from the Utility/Generator main switchgear through the UPS, STS, and PDU system to the power on the data center floor.  Fire Life Safety responsibilities will include wet sprinkler systems, pre-action sprinkler systems, clean agent fire suppression systems and fire alarm systems as well as their associated detection devices.

The candidate will:

• operate independently with limited direct management

• act as an escalation point for all facilities-related issues within the data center, escalating to the Director – Data Center & Facilities Operations as needed

• ensure all electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety equipment supporting the data centers are operating at peak efficiency and are highly available

• identify Single Points of Failures (SPoF) and End of Life (EOL) equipment within existing design/architecture and drive prioritization/remediation efforts within the facility

• drive preventative maintenance best practices and oversight using Method of Procedures (MOP) and Emergency Operating Procedures (EOP) for the facility

• identify root cause of system failures and present those findings to Senior Leadership

• oversee multi-year capacity/growth critical facilities projects within the facility and build business cases to support the projects

• be open to a continuous improvement culture

The ideal candidate will have:

• a deep understanding of chiller, chilled water and air handler technologies and electrical switchgear, generators, load banks, UPS, STS, PDU, RPP, and batteries

• 7+ years’ relevant experience operating data centers in a technical lead individual contributor role

• a Mechanical, Electrical, or other related Engineering degree or equivalent job experience

• strong verbal and written communication skills

• direct experience with design, engineering, commissioning, and operations of data center electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment

• demonstrated expertise of the data center tier rating systems and design risk factors for resiliency and availability

• experience reviewing technical drawings to ensure installations and designs conform to industry best practices and standards

• experience in operations of large-scale data center environments

• existing data center service vendor relationships

• experience with Electrical Power Management Systems (EPMS) and Building Management Software (BMS)

• relevant industry certifications (NFPA, ATS, ATO, AOS, DCDC, etc)

This job is on-site and based in our Ashburn, Virginia area location. This is a first shift, Monday-Friday position.

The annualized pay range is $108,900 - $147,300.

jobs.title: Admissions Coordinator
jobs.description:
Guidelight Health is a cutting-edge behavioral healthcare company dedicated to transforming lives through high-quality PHP (Partial Hospitalization Program) and IOP (Intensive Outpatient Program) services. As a newly launched organization, we are on a mission to redefine the behavioral health industry by delivering exceptional care, utilizing state-of-the-art facilities, and prioritizing the well-being of those we serve. At Guidelight Health, we are building a team of passionate, forward-thinking professionals who are eager to be part of this exciting journey to reshape mental health care. Join us in making a lasting impact!

Title: Admissions Coordinator

Reports to: Central Intake Supervisor

Department/Location: Remote (EST)

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt, Hourly

Schedule:  Monday-Friday, 9:00-5:00pm EST  *Must be able to work this schedule.

Role Summary:

The Admissions Coordinator is a critical member of Guidelight’s Central Intake team and serves as one of the first points of contact for prospective clients and referral partners.

This is a high-volume, front-line role for someone who is comfortable engaging people who may be anxious, ambivalent, emotionally dysregulated, or in crisis while keeping the interaction focused and moving forward. The Admissions Coordinator builds rapport quickly, gathers relevant information, completes structured screening and intake activities, educates clients about Guidelight’s PHP and IOP programs, addresses barriers and objections, verifies benefits, and coordinates the next steps toward care.

The ideal candidate brings strong judgment and clinical curiosity without needing to be clinically credentialed. They ask thoughtful follow-up questions, listen for what may not be explicitly stated, recognize potential risk or fit concerns, and understand when to escalate to the appropriate clinical or operational team rather than attempting to interpret or make clinical determinations.

This role combines genuine care with strong sales and operational instincts. The Admissions Coordinator believes in the value of treatment and can help an ambivalent client take the next step toward care while maintaining clinical appropriateness, ethical standards, and a high-quality client experience. The role is accountable not only for completing tasks, but for owning the outcome—ensuring that clients do not fall through the cracks and that each interaction results in a clear next step or accepted handoff.

Role Responsibilities:

Client Engagement & Admissions

• Serve as a primary point of contact for prospective clients and referring providers through phone and web-based channels.

• Engage clients with warmth, confidence, and appropriate directness, including individuals who may be anxious, ambivalent, emotionally dysregulated, or experiencing a behavioral health crisis.

• Build rapport quickly while maintaining structure and control of the conversation.

• Guide clients through demographics, insurance, screening, program education, scheduling, and next steps in a cohesive and efficient interaction.

• Conduct structured initial screenings to gather relevant clinical, demographic, and logistical information while maintaining the appropriate boundary between screening and clinical assessment.

• Recognize potential risk, clinical fit, or other concerns and appropriately escalate to clinical or operational team members.

• Educate prospective clients and referral partners about Guidelight’s PHP and IOP programs, including program structure, expectations, and next steps.

• Help clients navigate barriers to accessing care, including ambivalence, scheduling challenges, technology, insurance questions, and other concerns.

Engagement, Conversion & Client Commitment

• Use active listening, motivational interviewing, and consultative communication techniques to understand client needs and support movement toward treatment.

• Help clients understand the value of treatment and confidently move toward an appropriate next step in care.

• Address questions and objections with empathy, confidence, and sound judgment.

• Ask directly for commitment and help clients take action when appropriate.

• Maintain a conversion-minded approach while protecting client experience, clinical appropriateness, and ethical standards.

• Take ownership of funnel movement and identify opportunities to reduce drop-off and improve conversion.

• Consider an interaction complete only when there is a clear next step, accepted handoff, or documented resolution.

Referral & Pipeline Management

• Proactively manage inbound and outbound referrals and ensure timely movement through the admissions pipeline.

• Maintain ownership of assigned cases across multiple stages of the intake process.

• Reliably complete follow-up activities and close loops with clients, referral partners, clinicians, and internal teams.

• Monitor cases for stalled movement, missing information, or other sources of funnel leakage and take action to resolve them.

• Coordinate with referring providers and community partners to facilitate appropriate access to care.

• Ensure clients and referral partners have a clear understanding of next steps and who is responsible for them.

Insurance & Financial Transparency

• Verify insurance eligibility and benefits for PHP and IOP services.

• Explain coverage, out-of-pocket costs, and payment expectations clearly and accurately.

• Demonstrate a working knowledge of commercial insurance, Medicaid, and Medicare.

• Identify insurance or financial barriers that may affect access and escalate or coordinate resolution as appropriate.

Documentation & Clinical Handoffs

• Capture accurate, concise, and relevant information from client and referral interactions.

• Document information in CRM and EMR systems so that Clinical Reviewers and downstream teams can quickly understand the client, referral context, screening information, and outstanding needs.

• Coordinate the collection and submission of relevant prior medical records and referral documentation.

• Complete clear and effective handoffs to clinical and operational partners.

• Maintain accurate records and ensure required information is complete and accessible to downstream teams.

Workflow, Systems & Operational Excellence

• Manage high call volumes and multiple active cases while maintaining quality, responsiveness, and client experience.

• Balance live client interactions with follow-up work, documentation, SLAs, and other assigned responsibilities.

• Follow established workflows consistently while identifying opportunities to improve processes and reduce friction.

• Learn and effectively navigate CRM, EMR, scheduling, insurance, and other technology platforms.

• Adapt quickly as programs, payer requirements, workflows, and processes evolve.

• Identify process gaps and bring forward practical solutions rather than simply identifying problems.

• Participate in call review, quality audits, calibration, coaching, and other performance improvement activities.

• Be accountable to performance expectations including responsiveness, conversion, throughput, documentation quality, follow-up completion, and other Central Intake metrics.

Virtual Work Environment:

Virtual team members are expected to maintain a private, professional, distraction-free work environment that supports patient confidentiality and HIPAA-compliant care.

Because our roles involve direct patient care and/or access to protected health information, children, family members, household members, or other dependents may not be present in the workspace during patient-facing activities, clinical discussions, documentation, or other work involving confidential information.

Remote work is not a substitute for dependent care. Team members are expected to have appropriate care arrangements in place during scheduled working hours so they can fully perform their responsibilities without simultaneously providing active supervision or caregiving.

Required Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in health, human services, psychology, or a related field (required).

• 2–3+ years of experience in a high-volume, front-line healthcare, behavioral health, substance use, patient access, intake, admissions, triage, or healthcare contact-center environment.

• Working knowledge of insurance coverage, including the ability to verify eligibility and benefits, explain coverage and out-of-pocket costs, and identify potential insurance or financial barriers to care.

• Demonstrated experience interacting with individuals in emotionally sensitive, complex, urgent, or high-pressure situations.

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build rapport while maintaining structure and direction in a conversation.

• Strong judgment and clinical curiosity, with the ability to recognize when additional information or escalation is warranted while maintaining the boundary between screening and clinical assessment.

• Demonstrated ability to manage multiple active cases, competing priorities, follow-up requirements, and time-sensitive workflows.

• Strong organizational skills and exceptional attention to detail.

• Clear, concise written communication and documentation skills.

• Comfort being measured against operational performance metrics such as responsiveness, conversion, throughput, SLAs, and quality.

jobs.title: Electrical & Controls Installation Technician
jobs.description:
AMP is applying AI-powered sortation at scale to modernize the world's recycling infrastructure and maximize the value in waste. AMP gives waste and recycling leaders the power to harness AI to reduce labor costs, increase resource recovery, and deliver more reliable operations. With hundreds of deployments across North America, Asia, and Europe, AMP’s technology offers a transformational solution to waste sortation and changes the fundamental economics of recycling.

Headquartered in Louisville, Colorado, the Denver Post and BuiltIn Colorado have recognized AMP as one of the state's top workplaces. AMP has operations and career opportunities outside of Atlanta, Cleveland, Portsmouth, Virginia, and Europe. We’re fostering an environment where passionate individuals can grow and create impact. We seek unconventional thinkers to join our mission to enable a world without waste; at AMP, your contributions have meaning and can spur change. With backing from top-tier investors and national recognition including North American Cleantech Company of the Year, we’re always seeking ways to better our operations, raising the bar on innovation, and looking to collaborate and improve in what we do. Learn more at AMPSortation.com.

AMP is seeking an Electrical & Controls Installation Technician to execute and support industrial electrical and controls work across new system installations, retrofits, commissioning activities, and operating facilities. The role's primary focus is field installation: ensuring 480V and 120V power distribution, motor controls, safety circuits, instrumentation, and control systems are installed safely, accurately, and ready for startup. Between installations, this technician will provide electrical and controls troubleshooting, repairs, upgrades, and technical support to other AMP facilities.

What You'll Do

• Execute, coordinate, inspect, and document electrical and controls installations for AMP systems, including 480V three-phase and 120V single-phase circuits.

• Install, terminate, label, test, and troubleshoot conductors, control wiring, junction boxes, panels, motor circuits, sensors, actuators, safety devices, remote I/O, networking components, VFDs, servos, and related field devices, as permitted by applicable licensing and site requirements.

• Verify electrical installations against approved drawings, specifications, the National Electrical Code (NEC), local requirements, and AMP standards; identify deficiencies and drive closure with contractors and project teams.

• Perform pre-energization checks, point-to-point verification, continuity and insulation checks, torque verification, phase/rotation checks, and voltage measurements using properly rated test instruments.

• Support energization and commissioning, including I/O checkout, motor rotation, VFD and servo setup, safety-circuit and e-stop validation, device calibration, functional testing, and fault resolution.

• Create and maintain motor lists, I/O lists, cable and termination schedules, panel and device labels, redlines, as-built electrical drawings, test records, punch lists, and turnover documentation.

• Partner with Project Managers, Automation & Controls Engineering, Software Integration, equipment suppliers, electrical contractors, and facility teams to plan work, sequence energization, and resolve field issues.

• Review electrical contractor qualifications, work plans, installation quality, and progress; provide clear technical direction within the role's authority and promptly escalate safety, code, design, and schedule risks.

• Provide remote and on-site electrical and controls support to operating facilities, including troubleshooting, repairs, replacement of failed components, system upgrades, and restoration of equipment to service.

• Troubleshoot electrically controlled conveyor systems, including motor and drive behavior, sensors, safety devices, electro-hydraulic controls, and control-related conditions affecting conveyor tracking and roller operation; coordinate mechanical corrections with the appropriate team.

• Maintain safe work areas, tools, test equipment, documentation, and spare parts; share lessons learned and help standardize installation and troubleshooting practices across facilities.

Electrical Safety and Compliance

• Perform electrical work only when qualified, authorized, and permitted under applicable laws, licenses, site rules, and AMP's electrical-safety program.

• Apply lockout/tagout and establish an electrically safe work condition before work begins whenever feasible.

• Demonstrate training and experience consistent with NFPA 70E Qualified Person requirements, including knowledge of electrical hazards, shock and arc-flash risks, approach boundaries, required PPE, safe work practices, and procedures for work on or near energized electrical equipment.

• Participate in job briefings, energized-work planning and permitting when applicable, and stop work when conditions, documentation, PPE, or authorization are inadequate.

Required Qualifications

• Five or more years of hands-on industrial electrical and controls experience, or an equivalent combination of training and experience.

• Demonstrated experience installing and troubleshooting 480V and 120V industrial electrical systems, motor controls, control panels, and field devices.

• Ability to read, interpret, redline, and troubleshoot electrical schematics, one-lines, panel drawings, wiring diagrams, P&IDs, network diagrams, and equipment documentation.

• Experience selecting appropriate circuit protection, wire and cable, sensors, safety hardware, PLC hardware, remote I/O, VFDs, and servo systems for industrial applications.

• Experience with industrial controls, including valves, sensors, actuators, PLC-based control systems, electro-hydraulic systems, conveyors, conveyor tracking interfaces, and rollers.

• Working knowledge of PLC I/O, ladder logic, industrial networks, VFD and servo configuration, safety circuits, and power/load sizing.

• Proficiency with industrial electrical tools and properly rated diagnostic equipment, including multimeters and related test instruments.

• Ability to work independently in the field, coordinate effectively with contractors and cross-functional teams, document work accurately, and communicate technical issues clearly.

• High school diploma or equivalent and a valid driver's license.

Preferred Qualifications

• Journeyman electrician license, electrical apprenticeship completion, industrial electrician credential, or comparable formal technical training.

• Experience with Allen-Bradley or similar PLC/HMI platforms, industrial Ethernet networks, functional acceptance testing, and integrated system commissioning.

• Experience leading field electrical crews or coordinating electrical contractors on industrial installation projects.

• Proficiency with CAD/electrical drawing tools and standard Google Workspace or Microsoft Office applications; experience in recycling, material handling, robotics, manufacturing, or another automated industrial environment.

Working Conditions and Physical Demands

This is a hands-on field role in active industrial and construction environments. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

• Frequent standing, walking, climbing, bending, kneeling, reaching, and use of hands for tools and terminations; occasional lifting or moving of up to 45 pounds.

• Ability to distinguish wire and indicator colors, read labels and drawings, and work around operating industrial equipment, noise, dust, temperature variation, and construction activity.

• Comfortable using ladders and mobile elevating work platforms and working at heights after required training and authorization.

• Frequent travel, up to 80%, to installation and operating sites. Installation assignments may use a 10-days-on, weekend-off schedule based on project needs.

Compensation and Benefits

Hourly rate: $40.00-$44.00 per hour, with overtime likely during projects. The selected candidate may be recommended for a stock option grant commensurate with the position and qualifications. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, disability and life insurance; eligible HSA contributions; 401(k); paid time off; sick time; and paid holidays, subject to current plan terms and company policy.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Other Duties

jobs.title: Lead Teacher
jobs.description:
Shape a child’s very first learning experiences. At Guidepost Montessori, our Lead Infant and Toddler Guides create calm, nurturing environments where infants and Toddlers are respected as capable individuals from the very beginning.

If you’re passionate about early development and want to lead a thoughtfully designed classroom that supports independence, movement, and discovery, we’d love to meet you.

As a Lead Infant Guide, you’ll lead a mixed-age infant classroom (ages 0–3) in a Montessori environment intentionally designed to support each child’s natural development.

As a Lead Toddler Guide, you’ll lead a mixed-age toddler classroom in a Montessori environment thoughtfully designed to support children during one of the most formative stages of development.

In Montessori, the environment and the guide work together to nurture independence, curiosity, and confidence. You’ll thoughtfully prepare the classroom, observe each child closely, and provide individualized care that honors their unique rhythms and needs.

Most importantly, you’ll help infants develop trust in themselves and the world around them laying the foundation for lifelong learning.

What You’ll Do

• Observe each child to understand and support their physical, emotional, and cognitive development

• Respect and follow each child’s natural rhythms for sleeping, eating, and toileting

• Prepare and maintain a beautiful, orderly environment that fosters trust, movement, and exploration

• Support independence by encouraging children to participate in care activities

• Build warm, meaningful relationships with children and families

• Partner closely with parents to support each child’s growth and development

• Lead and collaborate with classroom team members to create a strong, respectful community

The Montessori Prepared Environment

Every Guidepost infant classroom is fully equipped with high-quality Montessori materials and thoughtfully designed to support movement, exploration, and independence.

Our infant environments include:

• Open floor space for movement and exploration

• Child-sized furniture and materials

• Curriculum that supports independence in feeding, dressing, and toileting

• Scientifically designed materials for fine and gross motor development

• Natural elements like real plants, cozy rugs, and abundant natural light

• Beautiful, breakable materials made from wood and metal rather than plastic

• Opportunities for climbing, crawling, and discovery without restrictive devices

What We’re Looking For

• Interest in pursuing fully sponsored Montessori certification through our Prepared Montessorian Institute, or prior Montessori diploma

• Experience working with children ages 0–3 in a group care setting

• Alignment with child-led educational philosophies (Montessori, Reggio Emilia, or similar)

What We Offer

• Competitive salary

• Health, dental, and vision insurance

Guidepost Montessori is a growing network of over 100 schools across the U.S. and Asia, serving children from 3 months to 6 years old in our Nido, Toddler, and Children’s House programs.

We believe children are capable and we design environments that empower them to explore, grow, and flourish. Our mission is to transform education by nurturing independence, joy, and lifelong learning.

If you’re passionate about early childhood, excited to partner with families, and ready to lead with purpose, we’d love to welcome you to our community.
