jobs.title: Test Technician
jobs.description:
About H3X Technologies

H3X is building America's advanced electric motor company, powering next-generation platforms in aerospace, defense, and marine. Our integrated motor drives deliver 12+ kW/kg, roughly 3x the power density of competing solutions. We're now scaling to megawatt-class systems, with customers working on everything from supersonic aircraft to turbine power generation for AI datacenters.

Our team brings together engineers and operators from aerospace, defense, and motorsports, with deep expertise in electric machines, power electronics, material science, and advanced manufacturing. We're a small, fast-moving team doing hard engineering that matters, and we're looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside us.

 

About the role

H3X is looking to hire an experienced Test Technician who will assist in the testing of prototype electric drive systems and facilitate product performance validation. Candidates should be experienced with testing procedures and data collection. This role will work closely with the product manufacturing and test teams to execute both R&D and production testing on H3X electric machines. This is an onsite role at our headquarters in Louisville, Colorado, on a standard weekday schedule, reporting to the Test Engineering Manager.

 

What you will do:

 - Set up, execute, and tear down dynamometer and environmental tests for motor drive systems

 - Build test setups, including instrumentation, wiring harnesses, and cooling loops

 - Execute test profiles according to written test procedures

 - Run production acceptance tests on units before they ship

 - Interpret live data, monitor for abnormalities, and make decisions during testing accordingly

 - Log anomalies and write up test results for the engineering team

 - Follow lockout/tagout, high-voltage, and rotating-machinery safety procedures (high-voltage safety training is provided)

 - Maintain testing equipment and track calibration status

 - Process, label, and archive test data so results are traceable to the unit and test run

What we are looking for:

 - High School Diploma or equivalent

 - 2+ years of hands-on mechanical and/or electrical assembly and testing experience

 - Some hands-on experience building electrical wiring and harnesses

 - Proficiency in comprehending data and identifying abnormalities in datasets

 - Ability to troubleshoot and debug test equipment

 - Ability to understand test equipment assembly steps from CAD models and work instructions

 - Ability to follow safety procedures closely and identify safety issues

 - High intelligence, high energy, and high integrity

 - Excellent written and verbal communication to document test results and share knowledge with the team

 - Organized and obsessive attention to detail: no room for oversight when testing flight-critical systems

 - Humble and open-minded: willingness to accept feedback and learn, consistently improve upon yourself and the work for which you will be responsible

 - A high degree of emotional intelligence: ability to collaborate closely with coworkers in a respectful and empathetic manner

 - Fundamentally curious and motivated by first principles

Preferred Qualifications:

 - Experience with testing dynamometers

 - Experience working with high voltage test systems

 - Experience with technical assembly work including fastening and component fabrication

 - Associate’s or technical trade degree

 - Experience with testing to DO-160G, MIL-STD-810, or other environmental specifications

Compensation & Benefits

 - Hourly Compensation Range: $25-$33/hr

 - Employee equity incentive plan

 - Health insurance: Medical, Vision, Dental, ST & LT Disability, and Life

 - Gym membership stipend (up to $60/month)

 - Outdoor Recreation Reimbursement ($900 annual maximum)

 - Flexible hours (deliverable-based goals)

 - Non-Exempt PTO Policy - 80 hours per 2000 hours, accrued per hour, PTO can be taken by the hour 

 - Monthly company events

 - 401k program

 - Friday Team Lunches

 

Why H3X

Joining H3X means working on hard, meaningful problems with a skunkworks-style team that's laser-focused on building exceptional products. We're deeply vertically integrated and have a very tight design-build-test loop, which lets us move from concept to hardware at unmatched speed. We've gone from idea to shipping product in less than two months.

We're a small, highly skilled team where everyone carries real responsibility and shares an extreme ownership mentality. We stay focused on the critical path, keep bureaucracy to a minimum, and structure everything around delivering results. You'll learn and grow faster here than you would anywhere else.

You'll work alongside world-class engineers and builders who are pioneering electric motor technology at scale on some of the coolest programs in the industry, from supersonic aircraft to power generation for AI datacenters. If you want your contributions to be visible and your work to directly shape American reindustrialization, you'll feel at home here.

Our team provides robust benefits including medical, vision, dental, disability, & life insurance offerings, employee equity incentive program, & 401k program. Additional benefits include our gym membership stipend and outdoor recreation reimbursement program. We have an execution based culture, with flexible hours, 12 company holidays (including our company ski trip), monthly company events, and weekly catered team lunch on Fridays.

 

Our Values

Be Relentless Never give up, persevere until the job is done. Run toward problems, not away from them. Grit is key.

Gain insight through humility Approach every challenge with a learner’s mindset. Stay open to feedback, listen to others, and deepen your understanding through self-awareness. ****Put your ego aside and seek the truth in every discussion, especially when leading others.

Distill & Simplify Eliminate unjustified complexity and simplify wherever possible, whether in requirements, design, or execution. Use first principles thinking to distill every problem to its essence. Less is more.

Find your flow Engage fully and work with intention. Find the rhythm and deep focus that lets you do your best work. Discover your Ikigai - where your strengths, passions, and purpose meet and drive your personal fulfillment and team success. That is when the magic happens.

SEND (Solve, Evolve, Nail It, Deliver) Devise the best solution with the information at hand, test it, learn from it, and iterate quickly until you nail it. Nothing works perfectly the first time, but you should never hit the same issue twice. Stay laser-focused on solving customer problems and delivering solutions that create real value.

 

Equal Opportunity Employer

H3X is an equal opportunity-affirmative action employer and considers all qualified applicants for employment based on business needs, job requirements and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, past or present military service or any other status protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate.

jobs.title: Care Manager, RN (Youngstown, OH Market / PART-TIME / Field-based)
jobs.description:
About Our Company

FreedomCare is a healthcare company that has been dedicated to revolutionizing the home care industry since 2016. We support our patients by ensuring they have the power to choose a caregiver who will care for them in the comfort of their own homes. Our mission spans coast to coast, supporting patients across the U.S.

We pride ourselves on our values which drive the level of care that we deliver to our patients:

Here For You An attitude of service, empathy, and availability

Own It Drive and ownership

Do the Right Thing High integrity

Be Positive Great attitude and a can-do positive approach to challenges

Join our team and make a positive impact on the lives of others! We are looking for a Case Manager, RN for our Ohio team! New Graduates Welcome!

This is a field-based position that requires frequent travel to patient's homes in across our Youngstown, Ohio market.

Overview

The Case Manager, RN is responsible for conducting initial in-home assessments, orientations for new patients and caregivers, and providing ongoing care management and support. This role combines clinical assessment, care coordination, patient and Personal Care Attendant (PCA) education, and quality assurance to ensure safe, effective, and person-centered care.

The Case Manager, RN collaborates closely with patients, PCAs , and interdisciplinary care teams to assess needs, develop individualized plans of care, and facilitate the seamless initiation and delivery of services. Through regularly scheduled home visits, the RN evaluates patient and caregiver well-being, monitors the quality and effectiveness of care, and identifies opportunities to enhance health outcomes, safety, and regulatory compliance. The Case Manager, RN proactively communicates clinical concerns, changes in condition, and potential barriers to care with the appropriate team members to ensure timely intervention, effective care coordination, and optimal patient outcomes.

Responsibilities

• Conducts initial in-person clinical assessments and coordinates service activation, ensuring that all required forms and standard procedures are followed.

• Develops, implements, manages patient's activity plan(s).

• making revisions and documenting changes as needed.

• Completes all client documentation, to include written records, reports, and notes in accordance with agency policy and procedure following client visits or contacts in an accurate, timely, complete, concise and legible manner.

• Actively coordinates the care of the client through communication and written documentation to the physician, and other disciplines involved in the client’s care and community resources.

• Provide ongoing coaching to drive effective utilization of established best practices, encourage PCA education, and connect families to appropriate resources.

• Reviews the PCA notes and appropriately addresses changes in the consumer’s condition or environment.

• Ensure continuous compliance with all regulatory standards as well as company policies and procedures.

• Performs other job-related duties as may be required or directed by the supervisor.

Education and Experience

• Diploma from an accreditted nursing program. New graduates welcome!

Is a Plus:

• Home care case management

• Care coordination experience

Qualifications

• Valid and Active Registered Nursing License issued by the Ohio Board of Nursing

• Ability to articulate cases through effective summaries.

• Ability and flexibility to travel (usually by car) within assigned geographic area

• Valid driver’s license and car insurance required.

• Proficient in common software and web-based applications (e.g. Case Management Systems, MS Office) with the ability to teach others.

• A passion for providing a high level of customer service, including the ability to show empathy, active listening and patience.

• Is a Plus: Bilingual

Why work at FreedomCare?

We are here for you and committed to providing a best-in-class employee experience. We offer competitive compensation, medical benefits, retirement plans, wellness programs, fun company events and ongoing learning opportunities to grow your career.

This is a place where your voice matters, where we build great relationships, and your work has meaning and a tangible positive impact on others!

At FreedomCare, we celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, citizenship or immigration status, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

At FreedomCare, base pay is one part of our total compensation package and is determined within a range. This provides our employees with the opportunity to professionally grow and develop within a role. The base pay range for this per diem role is between $40.00 and $45.00 per hour at the commencement of your first year of employment. Compensation decisions are dependent upon a variety of factors which may include, but are not limited to: skill set, years of relevant experience, education, location, and licensure/certifications.

jobs.title: Senior Influencer Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
Maven Clinic is the world's largest virtual clinic for women and families on a mission to make healthcare work for all of us. Through Maven Enterprise, the company partners with more than 2,300 employers and health plans to provide end-to-end women's and family health programs spanning fertility and family building, maternity and newborn care, parenting and pediatrics, and menopause and midlife — improving clinical outcomes, reducing healthcare costs, and expanding equitable access to high-quality care at scale. Through its consumer platform, Maven provides direct access to virtual care across 30+ specialties, as well as dedicated hormone and GLP-1 care programs purpose-built for women. Founded in 2014 by CEO Kate Ryder, Maven Clinic has raised more than $425 million from leading healthcare and technology investors including General Catalyst, Sequoia, Dragoneer Investment Group, Oak HC/FT, StepStone Group, Icon Ventures, and Lux Capital. Recognized for innovation and industry leadership, Maven has been named to the TIME100 Most Influential Companies, CNBC Disruptor 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, and FORTUNE Best Places to Work. Learn more at mavenclinic.com

An award-winning culture working towards an important mission –  Maven Clinic is a recipient of over 30 workplace and innovation awards, including:

• TIME 100 Most Influential Companies (2023, 2026)

• Fortune Change the World (2024)

• CNBC Disruptor 50 List (2022, 2023, 2024)

• Fortune Best Workplaces for Millennials (2024)

• Fortune Best Workplaces in Health Care (2024)

• Fast Company Most Innovative Companies (2020, 2023)

• Fortune Best Workplaces NY (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024)

About the Role:

Maven is looking for a performance-driven Senior Manager to own influencer and podcast as acquisition channels for our consumer business. This is a role for someone who treats every creator and every placement as a channel to be measured, tested, and optimized — not a brand or awareness play. You'll bring rigor to a function that's still early: building the testing roadmap, owning attribution, and proving out what actually converts, while also supporting the team's broader partnership strategy.

As a Senior Manager, Influencer & Partnerships at Maven, you will:

• Own influencer as a performance channel end-to-end — strategy, creator sourcing, briefing, contracting, and budget — building the high-level approach needed to hit aggressive growth targets, with every partnership evaluated against clear performance criteria, not reach or sentiment alone.

• Build and run a testing roadmap for influencer: define hypotheses, success criteria, and evaluation plans before committing spend, and use results to decide what scales, what changes, and what stops.

• Own purchase-level CAC and funnel reporting for influencer, from creator exposure through completed purchase, and bring that reporting proactively, not on request.

• Support the team's broader partnership strategy, helping identify and evaluate a small number of high-impact brand partnerships, with clear prioritization given limited resources.

• Partner closely with the paid and organic teams to share wins, losses, and learnings, and ensure what's working in influencer and podcast informs performance across channels.

• Bring a forward-looking read on the influencer and podcast landscape, competitor activity, and emerging opportunities for Maven.

We're looking for you to bring:

• 5+ years of experience running influencer or creator as a performance/acquisition channel, ideally within consumer health, wellness, or a high-growth consumer brand.

• A proven track record of building attribution and measurement for non-click or hard-to-attribute channels.

• Direct experience setting and running a testing roadmap: hypotheses, success criteria, and go/no-go decisions, not just campaign execution.

• Fluency with CAC, LTV, and funnel metrics, and comfort being held to the same performance bar as paid channels.

• A true self-starter who takes full ownership without waiting to be told what to do next, and who's energized rather than daunted by building a function from 0 to 1.

• Experience with partnerships or co-marketing a plus, but not the core of this role.

• A collaborative approach and ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

• A deep passion for women's and family health, and excitement to help shape the next chapter of Maven's brand story.

The base salary range for this role is $150,000 - $175,000 per year. You will also be entitled to receive equity and benefits. Individual pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including qualifications for the role, experience level, and skillset.

This role requires active work authorization in the US.

Maven embraces a flexible hybrid work model. Our teams primarily operate from the New York Metropolitan area, NY, and remotely via San Francisco/Bay Area, CA, Seattle, WA. For those in our New York City office, we encourage in-person collaboration by requiring team members to work onsite three days a week  (Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday). For those based in Boston, DC, Chicago, Seattle, and San Francisco, we encourage in-person collaboration by requiring team members to attend monthly Work Together Days within these cities. This policy aims to balance remote work flexibility with the benefits of face-to-face interaction.

At Maven we believe that a diverse set of backgrounds and experiences enrich our teams and allow us to achieve above and beyond our goals. If you do not have experience in all of the areas detailed above, we hope that you will share your unique background with us in your application and how it can be additive to our teams.

Benefits That Work For You

Our benefits are designed to support your health, well-being and career development, helping you thrive both personally and professionally. We remain focused on providing a competitive benefits package for our employees. On top of standards such as employer-covered health, dental, and insurance plan options, we offer an inclusive approach to benefits:

• Maven for Mavens: access to the full platform and specialists, including care for mental health, reproductive health, family planning and pediatrics.

• Whole-self care through wellness partnerships

• Hybrid work, in office meals, and work together days

• 16 weeks 100% paid parental leave and new parent stipend (for Mavens who've been with us for 1 year+)

• Annual professional development stipend and access to a personal career coach through Maven for Mavens

• 401K matching for US-based employees, with immediate vesting

These benefits are applicable to Maven Clinic Co., US-based, full-time employees only. 1099/Contract Providers are ineligible for these benefits.

Maven is an affirmative action and equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or genetic information. Maven is committed to providing access, equal opportunity and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. Maven Clinic interview requests and job offers only originate from an @mavenclinic.com email address (e.g jsmith@mavenclinic.com). Maven Clinic will never ask for sensitive information to be delivered over email or phone. If you receive a scam issue or a security issue involving Maven Clinic please notify us at: security@mavenclinic.com. For general and additional inquiries, please contact us at careers@mavenclinic.com.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Business Development - Maneuver Dominance (International)
jobs.location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Maneuver Dominance Division’s mission is to reboot Vertical Flight and autonomous systems that operate in the near-earth domain. Our portfolio of UAS and air launched effectors are the cornerstone of these capabilities, and we continually strive to push the boundaries of what's possible in endurance, autonomy, and mission capability. The Maneuver Dominance team develops and maintains core products and payloads, and adapts and applies those products to serve a wide variety of defense, IC, and commercial customers in US and international markets.

ABOUT THE JOB

As our team begins the next stage of hypergrowth and significantly expand our International deal-stack, we are looking for motivated candidates that are inspired to work within an extremely energetic, creative, and innovative team. We work in a highly dynamic environment where collaboration and idea sharing are a way of life. We are seeking an Associate Director, Business Development - MD International to join Anduril. This will support the coordination and execution (in partnership with Global Defense Country teams and group Business Development teams) of the international portfolio for the TRS business line and the MD division.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Work across multi-functional, diverse teams in a highly dynamic and fast paced environment. Business development at Anduril is not just about the rolodex. This role requires a self-starter who can help coordinate and align the enablers that Anduril has to craft, coordinate, and execute GTM Strategies, Government Relations activities, Communications and Marketing strategies, etc.

• Help generate and capture business opportunities. The BD Team is ultimately responsible for growing revenue. This role will support the growth team in identifying, pursuing, and shaping opportunities for existing, in-development, and new platforms and capabilities. You will grow a deep understanding of the existing and prospective client base, know the current and planned programmatic and technical roadmap, and be cognizant of the current and changing competitive landscape in the commercial, defense and international market. You will engage with current clients and prospective customers and monitor buying cycles for opportunities. You will support proposals and new customer efforts, including authoring and reviewing RFI, RFP, RFWP, and other request responses and support the growth and capture teams in closing on new business.

• Grow existing business. You will partner with adjacent business lines and product engineers to identify opportunities for business growth with current clients. This doesn’t just include expanding on current work, but interfacing with existing partners to explore new opportunity areas by sustaining and building on the strong foundation of client relationships.

• Communicate our value to customers. BD Team members represent Anduril to a broad audience: customers, partners, competitors, and the interested public. You must project the company’s ethos, conveying insights that illustrate our approach to building next-generation defense technology and our competitive edges in doing so.

• Inform product development. You will be a liaison between current or prospective customers and the engineering organization, and as such must be able to translate their problem set into an actionable internal plan and product roadmap. You will need to interpret and convey various client needs to the growth and engineering teams, help to inform and manage priorities and execution, keep Business Line stakeholders informed, and make sure that performance stays aligned to key milestones.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• 5-10 years of experience in business development, capture, or program management, including hands-on contribution to international business capture strategies with an emphasis on commercial and defense industries.

• Working familiarity with international defense deal flow: hands-on exposure to FMS and DCS transactions, ITAR/EAR export licensing (e.g., DSP-5, TAA, MLA) and releasability determinations, and support to the partner-nation relationships and MOD procurement cycles.

• An aptitude and appetite to thrive within organizations with nascent structure, high-ownership culture, and a “whatever it takes” environment.

• A knack for knocking out deliverables in an ambiguous environment, while maintaining a level-head, strong interpersonal skills, and a professional presence with senior stakeholders.

• Bachelor’s degree

• High-energy, high-ownership contributor who takes initiative, follows through on commitments, and works well across teams with a high level of emotional intelligence.

• Ability to work in a fast-paced, highly entrepreneurial, and creative environment, and be able to build, adapt, and implement new and innovative approaches to market.

• Excellent writing and communication skills, with experience preparing and delivering briefings for senior executives and customers.

• Working knowledge of relevant DoD / IC / Commercial programs, platforms and payloads, to include enabling technologies, systems integration and software development.

• Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Prior experience with DoD Capture and Sales.

• Familiarity with foreign military sales, including the technical, programmatic, and operational challenges of autonomous systems.

• Experience in defense and commercial industries or complex engineering systems.

• Prior military or contracting experience, or experience in DoD or Government (ground or air maneuver and/or group 1-3 drone experience a plus).

• Experience with government business development, government contract structures, and government proposal processes.

• Ability to travel 30-50%, majority international.

• Currently has and can maintain an active U.S. Secret or Top Secret security clearance.

US Salary Range

$167,000—$222,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

jobs.title: Senior Business Operations Associate
jobs.description:
Rapidly Growing Life Sciences Technology Company

Ultima Genomics is a rapidly growing company that is developing ground-breaking genomics technologies. Our mission is to continuously drive the scale of genomic information to enable unprecedented advances in biology and improvements in human health. Join us to develop and commercialize technologies that unleash the power of genomics at scale and empower the future of human health.

• Employee communications Work with Business Operations leadership to draft and deliver company announcements, company event communications and culture messaging via various channels, such as email, Teams, company intranet and bulletin boards Manage the logistics of company all-hands Support to organize and coordinate company meetings, including internal employee meetings and external customer or partner meetings

• Payroll support Manage the company's biweekly and off-cycle payroll processes Help resolve employee payroll discrepancies and inquiries Help ensure all mandatory payroll-related filings, if any, are completed and submitted prior to deadlines Work with the Business Operations team members to collect and approve timecards and ensure they are submitted accurately and on time Understand company timecard system and be able to step in and support the team as needed

• Other job duties as assigned

Qualifications, Skills, Knowledge & Abilities

jobs.title: Naval Architecture Intern
jobs.description:
Work Arrangement

This is an onsite position.

Job Overview

The Naval Architecture Intern supports vessel design, analysis, modeling, and engineering activities across a diverse portfolio of maritime programs. Working under the guidance of experienced naval architects and marine engineers, this position provides hands-on exposure to vessel design, hydrostatics, hydrodynamics, stability, structures, and marine operations while contributing to real-world engineering projects.

Essential Functions

• Assist with vessel design studies, concept development activities, and engineering analyses.

• Support hydrostatic, stability, resistance and powering, seakeeping, and vessel performance evaluations.

• Develop and modify vessel arrangements, engineering drawings, and 3D models under engineering supervision.

• Assist in preparing technical reports, calculations, engineering documentation, presentations, and design packages.

• Support evaluation of vessel layouts, compartment arrangements, mission payload integration, and equipment installations.

• Assist with structural assessments and engineering analyses using established naval architecture methods and tools.

• Support application of classification society, customer, and regulatory requirements to vessel designs.

• Participate in design reviews, engineering discussions, and multidisciplinary project meetings.

• Collect, organize, and analyze engineering data from vessels, simulations, models, tests, and field activities.

• Support dockside inspections, vessel surveys, sea trials, testing, and verification activities as assigned.

• Document engineering observations, findings, lessons learned, and technical recommendations.

• Collaborate with naval architecture, mechanical, electrical, systems, software, and production personnel on engineering tasks.

• Learn and apply company engineering processes, configuration management practices, documentation standards, and technical procedures.

• Perform other duties as assigned in support of engineering and maritime operations.

Standard Essential Functions

• Regular and reliable attendance on a full time basis [or in accordance with posted schedule].

• Responsible for exhibiting professional behavior with both internal and external business associates that reflects positively on the company and is consistent with the company's policies and practices.

• Embodies AEVEX’s cultural values and aligns daily actions with department goals and company culture.

Qualifications

• Fundamental understanding of naval architecture and marine engineering principles.

• Coursework exposure to hydrostatics, hydrodynamics, fluid mechanics, statics, dynamics, or related engineering disciplines.

• Familiarity with vessel stability, resistance and powering, seakeeping, structures, arrangements, or marine systems.

• Basic understanding of engineering drawing interpretation and technical documentation practices.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Ability to document technical work clearly and effectively.

• Ability to learn new engineering tools, methods, and processes.

• Ability to receive technical guidance and incorporate feedback from experienced engineers.

• Ability to work both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary engineering team.

• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

• Interest in maritime systems, vessel design, and marine operations.

• Ability to safely board and traverse vessels, docks, shipyards, and waterfront facilities.

• Ability and willingness to work in office, laboratory, manufacturing, shipyard, waterfront, and vessel environments.

• Ability to occasionally lift, carry, and transport engineering equipment and materials consistent with job requirements.

• Ability and willingness to travel occasionally in support of testing, inspections, sea trials, and project activities.

• Preferred: Familiarity with vessel arrangements, stability analysis, resistance and powering, seakeeping, or marine structures. Familiarity with marine industry standards and classification society requirements, including ABS, DNV, USCG, or U.S. Navy guidance.

Education / Certifications

• Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Naval Architecture, Ocean Engineering, Marine Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.

• Completion of coursework in engineering fundamentals such as statics, dynamics, fluid mechanics, naval architecture, or related technical subjects.

• Preferred: Completion of junior- or senior-level coursework in Naval Architecture, Ocean Engineering, or Marine Engineering. Relevant academic projects, undergraduate research, engineering competitions, or design-team participation related to maritime systems. Training or coursework involving vessel design, stability analysis, marine structures, hydrodynamics, or marine systems engineering.

Experience

• No professional experience required.

• Academic coursework demonstrating engineering fundamentals applicable to vessel design and marine systems.

• Experience participating in engineering projects, laboratory work, design teams, research activities, or technical extracurricular programs.

• Experience preparing engineering calculations, technical reports, presentations, or design documentation.

• Preferred: Experience using engineering software such as Rhino, SurfaceWorks, GHS, or SolidWorks. Experience participating in student engineering competitions, capstone projects, research efforts, or maritime-related activities. Experience supporting testing, inspections, vessel surveys, model testing, or field engineering activities. Prior shipyard, waterfront, boating, maritime, military, or marine industry experience.

Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties the employee is:

• Occasionally required to lift up to 10 pounds.

For the purpose of this summary, occasionally is used to represent up to 1/3 of the time given to the work day, frequently represents 1/3 to 2/3 of the time and constantly represents 2/3 or more of the time.

Security Clearance

• U.S. Citizenship required.

The Company provides a reasonable range of compensation. Actual compensation is influenced by an array of factors including, but not limited to, skill set, level of experience, and specific location. The range of starting pay for this position is for the listed location only.

Salary Range

$20—$25 USD

About AEVEX

AEVEX, headquartered in Solana Beach, California, supports the U.S. national security mission and partner nation needs around the world by providing full-spectrum aviation, remote sensing, and analysis solutions. The company's capabilities include custom design and engineering; rapid prototyping; sensor integration and sustainment; aircraft modification and certification; flight test instrumentation and support; mission operations service; advanced intelligence data processing, exploitation, and dissemination solutions; and tailored hardware and software mission-system tools. AEVEX uses agile and customized approaches to rapidly define, develop, and deliver specialized solutions for airborne special mission needs for the U.S. Government, partner nations, and commercial businesses. AEVEX has major offices in California, Florida, North Carolina, Ohio, and Virginia.

jobs.title: Buyer
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Gatik is in the business of autonomous freight, and that business is already on the road.

Every day, Gatik’s autonomous trucks move freight for Fortune 50 retailers, grocers and consumer brands across Texas, Arizona, Arkansas and Canada, connecting distribution centers and stores and keeping goods moving. At the heart of it all is the Gatik Driver™, our proprietary Level 4 autonomous driving system, powered by scalable, interpretable AI and engineered to deliver safe, reliable, high-frequency freight operations.

Gatik’s momentum is real. With more than $600 million in contracted revenue and $200 million raised in our August 2026 Series D round, Gatik has taken one of the toughest challenges in autonomous technology and turned it into a proven commercial business.

And the market is paying attention. In 2026, Gatik earned a place on Forbes' America's Best Startup Employers list, and the Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing private companies. The Gatik Driver™ won an Edison Award for Advancements in Autonomous Driving, and Inc. named our Co-founder and Chief Engineer, Apeksha Kumavat, to its Female Founders 500 list.

There's a lot more road ahead, and some of the brightest, most driven minds in autonomous technology are building the next chapter at Gatik. We're taking on hard engineering problems, pushing the limits of what's possible and building on a commercial foundation that's already proven itself in the real world with some of the biggest companies in the world, like PepsiCo and Loblaw. If you're ambitious, love solving problems that matter and want to see your work make a real difference, you'll find plenty to get excited about here.

About the role

Gatik is looking for an experienced, detail-oriented Buyer to support procurement operations across our autonomous vehicle hardware, engineering, manufacturing, and fleet programs. In this role, you will own end-to-end purchase order execution, strategic sourcing and supplier negotiations, material shortage mitigation, and operational vendor management. Partnering closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Logistics, Fleet Operations, and Finance, you will keep critical components and business services moving on schedule. You will be instrumental in maintaining accurate ERP records and cost controls while driving supplier reliability in a fast-paced hardware environment.

This role is onsite 5 days per week in Santa Clara, CA.

What you'll do

• End-to-End Purchase Order Management: Own the full PO lifecycle in NetSuite—from reviewing technical and commercial accuracy on requisitions to issuing orders, managing revisions/change orders, and reconciling invoices through closeout.

• Strategic Sourcing & Negotiations: Source competitive quotes, onboard suppliers, and negotiate pricing, lead times, payment terms, freight, and MOQs to achieve cost savings and vendor accountability.

• Hardware & Production Procurement: Procure mechanical, electrical, and automotive components—including LiDAR, radar, cameras, sensors, compute systems, and harnesses—across prototype, validation, and production builds while coordinating engineering change orders (ECOs).

• Material Planning & Shortage Mitigation: Track open orders, BOM requirements, and supplier lead times; maintain shortage trackers, expedite constrained parts, and resolve receiving discrepancies to prevent build delays.

• Operational Purchasing & Renewals: Manage day-to-day purchasing for Fleet Operations (vehicle maintenance and parts), IT, software subscriptions, and professional services while tracking contract expirations and consolidating recurring spend.

• Financial Controls & Reporting: Partner with Finance and Accounts Payable to resolve invoice mismatches, coordinate prepayments or milestones, and maintain audit-ready ERP data and spend/delivery reporting.

What We're Looking For

• Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Operations, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

• 5+ years of progressive experience in purchasing, procurement, or supply chain operations, ideally within automotive, manufacturing, robotics, or hardware technology.

• Proven track record independently managing the full PO lifecycle, supplier negotiations, commercial terms, and urgent component expediting.

• Hands-on experience with ERP/procurement systems (NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, or Coupa) and strong proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets (lookups, pivot tables, spend/shortage reporting).

• Solid understanding of BOMs, inventory/material planning, receiving workflows, and three-way invoice matching.

Salary Range - $80,000- $120,000

More about Gatik

Founded in 2017, Gatik has grown into a commercial force in autonomous freight, operating trucks daily in live customer networks across the United States and Canada. We're headquartered in Santa Clara, California, but our impact is felt on the roads and in the supply chains that keep essential goods moving for some of the biggest companies in North America.

Our trucks do some of the most demanding work in freight, running high-frequency, time-sensitive routes between distribution centers and stores, where reliability matters every single day. jobs.title: Bolt-On Autonomy Engineering Lead
jobs.description:
Who we are

Picogrid is a leading venture-backed defense technology company founded to bridge the decades-long gap between modern technology and the critical demands of national security. Today, we're building the essential infrastructure to unify sensors, autonomy, and operators with our technology deployed in active operations around the world. Our mission is to deliver an operational advantage to secure the United States and its allies.


ABOUT THE ROLE

A vehicle drives into a valley and loses GPS. It still has to know where it is. The computer bolted onto it must combine its inertial navigation system (INS) with visual-inertial odometry (VIO) to keep its position, track uncertainty and tell the operator who assigned the mission when it can no longer proceed safely. You will make navigation, vehicle control and operator intent work together under those conditions.

You will lead the software that adds autonomy to existing platforms through onboard compute and connected sensors. Your scope spans sensor discovery, navigation, vehicle control and mission assembly across ground vehicles, airframes, turrets and interceptors. It extends to full mission orchestration: automatic takeoff, meshing with other airframes in flight, and terminal flight with target acquisition on intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) missions. That means deciding which interfaces can serve several platforms and which limits belong to a specific installation. You own the path from simulation to a bench with real hardware to an operator-supervised field test, including degraded navigation and communications. This work is funded: the Air Force awarded Picogrid a $3.2M program for unmanned systems integration.

You will own a vertical or customer segment of bolt-on autonomy. As this work grows, you will recruit engineers for navigation, platform integrations and mission execution, and decide how they share responsibility for a vehicle in the field. Expect to write software, set acceptance criteria and work directly with hardware engineers, platform partners and operators. We want to hear about hardware you put into use, what failed and how you corrected it. Apply even if your career has been short and you have already done that work.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Build capability discovery that identifies connected sensors and vehicles, rejects ambiguous membership, and tells the operator which mission functions are available.

 - Define navigation interfaces for an inertial navigation system (INS), including coordinate frames, installation geometry, timestamps, uncertainty and loss of a trustworthy position or heading.

 - Develop vehicle and turret control integrations with explicit command authority, operator takeover, cancellation and safe responses to lost communications.

 - Assemble and orchestrate full missions from navigation, sensing and control capabilities through Legion, from automatic takeoff to terminal flight, keeping platform-specific limits visible to planning software and operators.

 - Create simulation, hardware-in-the-loop tests and field procedures that exercise stale telemetry, sensor loss and GNSS-degraded operation before expanding the operating envelope.

 - Set the technical roadmap, review implementation decisions and hire engineers who can independently own navigation, platform integrations and mission execution.
   
   


YOUR FIRST YEAR

 - Within 30 days, trace a mission from the operator's request through navigation and vehicle control, ship an improvement on real hardware, and document the conditions in which it is safe to use.

 - Lead an operator-supervised field test of an integrated vehicle and sensor package, with measured navigation quality, command latency and takeover behavior.

 - Bring a second platform or sensor configuration onto the shared interfaces and use the differences to remove assumptions tied to the first installation.

 - Recruit the first additional autonomy engineers, give each a defined subsystem to own, and establish how changes pass from simulation through hardware tests to field release.
   
   


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - You have shipped software that controls or coordinates physical hardware and can explain your decisions, failures and test evidence.

 - You can build and debug production software on Linux in Go, Python, C++ or a comparable language, across application and device boundaries.

 - You understand coordinate transforms, timing and navigation uncertainty well enough to diagnose a plausible-looking but incorrect vehicle pose.

 - You have integrated third-party hardware or software from incomplete documentation and verified its actual behavior.

 - You can define and test command authority, failure handling and operator intervention for a system whose outputs cause physical motion.

 - You can turn an unclear mission need into an architecture, a working implementation and acceptance criteria, and help other engineers deliver against them.

 - U.S. citizenship and ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret security clearance.
   
   


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with INS or VIO integration, sensor fusion, GNSS-degraded navigation or installation calibration on moving platforms.

 - Experience with autopilots, ground vehicle controllers, gimbals or turret interfaces and their operating constraints.

 - Experience building simulation, recorded-data replay or hardware-in-the-loop infrastructure that caught problems before a field test.

 - Experience deploying containerized software on constrained edge computers and diagnosing network, compute or sensor timing limits.

 - Experience conducting field trials with operators or growing a small engineering team while remaining a hands-on contributor.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Base salary range: $200,000- $280,000 per year. Base salary is just one part of your total compensation package at Picogrid.

 - Significant stock options with a high potential upside as an early-stage company

 - 401(k) with employer matching

 - Health coverage for you and your family (medical, dental, and vision insurance)

 - Relocation assistance provided (if applicable)

 - Unlimited PTO (two-week minimum) and 13 paid holidays per year

 - Paid parental leave for both parents

 - Lunch provided when working in-office and a fully stocked kitchenette

 - Free EV charging at the HQ

 - Unique office in El Segundo, CA stocked with quality coffee, snacks, and craft beer

 


EXPORT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

Picogrid is committed to providing a professional work environment free from discrimination, harassment, and retaliation. We are an equal opportunity employer and make all employment decisions based on merit, qualifications, and business needs.

Our Hopper consumer booking platforms and HTS (Hopper Technology Solutions), our B2B business, work together to give travelers something the industry has never reliably offered: transparency, flexibility, and real savings on every trip. jobs.description:
This is a part-time, 20 hours per week, afternoon phlebotomy position located at Central DuPage Hospital in Winfield.

Must be able to work 2pm - 6pm with occasional Saturday or Sunday (or both). Responsible for outpatient and inpatient blood draws. When needed, also responsible for driving to nursing homes around the Central DuPage Hospital area for stat blood draws.

The Phlebotomist reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Phlebotomist provides expert phlebotomy services and must demonstrate excellent customer service and communication skills. The phlebotomist must have the ability to function as part of a highly effective team that consistently puts “Patients First”.

The Phlebotomist is responsible for venipuncture collection and specimen processing. Other responsibilities include but are not limited to order entry in multiple systems, verification of test result receipt, patient information retrieval and lab reception/clerical duties and functions

Responsibilities:

· Performs phlebotomy and other lab specimen collections per age related standards and in accordance with departmental policies, protocols and procedures.

· Demonstrates AIDET model and optimizes patient safety to reduce the likelihood of medical/health care errors.

· Receives and reviews physician orders; ensures that all necessary information is included for appropriate lab services. Enters accurate orders for lab tests in accordance with department policies, protocols and procedures.

· Patient communication model and provides appropriate post-phlebotomy patient care.

· Processes specimens in a timely manner to ensure stability and integrity of samples including labeling, centrifuging, aliquoting, freezing and packaging specimens for transport in accordance with established protocols and policies.

· Reviews/Records refrigerator temperature(s) and QC/QA records. Areas of concern are recorded through the Corrective Action Log and reported to maintenance for repair. Findings are reported to supervisor or manager.

· Understands the operation and maintenance of equipment pertinent to the job. Follows up with all outstanding orders on manifest log, and communicates all timed, completed or uncompleted draws/charges/results as appropriate

· Communicates and notifies Laboratory and/or Physician of problems with specimen procurement for optimal care

· Maintains a safe work environment, holds self-accountable for safe work practices; including adhering to biohazard waste procedures and ensuring proper storage and timely pickup of biohazardous waste.

· Performs lab-related clerical duties include but not limited to order entry, verification of test result receipt, patient information retrieval as well as utilization of email, medical record systems, handheld and desktop devices, ordering and maintaining supply inventory, filing and sanitizing equipment as necessary

· Uses department’s resources efficiently; participates in efforts to reduce costs and streamline work processes.

· Adheres to continuing education expectations; completes and signs-off on competency assessments

· Demonstrates the value of teamwork on a consistent basis; interacts with and assists others in a professional manner

· Applies critical thinking, sound decision making and judgment to investigate and resolve challenging situations

· Complies with all organizational policies regarding ethical business practices.

· Performs other duties as assigned

Minimum Requirements:

Education:

• High School diploma or equivalent.

Certification:

• ·Phlebotomy certification through a nationally recognized organization or training from a phlebotomy school or medical institution or one or more years of phlebotomy experience in a healthcare setting or CMA certification.

Preferred:

· Experience performing phlebotomy on a broad range of patient’s types.

· Experience with processing lab specimens, transferring specimens, and handling a centrifuge.

· Familiar with medical EMR systems.

· Knowledge of medical terminology.

jobs.description:
About Lucid

At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience.

We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what’s possible and shape the future of mobility.

Sr. Technical Quality Engineering Specialist

Quality | Arizona | Full-Time

About Lucid

At Lucid, we are creating an electric future without compromise. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. We build world-class vehicles by pushing performance, efficiency, and design beyond industry limits, setting new standards with vehicles like Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity.

The people here—engineers, designers, operators, and builders—came from across industries and around the world because they wanted to work on a harder problem. They care deeply about mastering their craft and delivering work they're proud of. We trust you to take ownership, push beyond what is expected, and help write the playbook for what comes next.

By refusing to settle, you help shape the future of electric mobility and prove what's possible when craft and ambition refuse to compromise each other.

The Role

Assuring the quality of a premium electric vehicle begins long before Start of Production. As a Sr. Technical Quality Engineering Specialist, you will drive quality engineering activities across a broad range of vehicle systems, components, and commodities throughout product development, validation, launch, and production.

This role requires a strong technical foundation and the flexibility to support multiple engineering commodities based on program priorities and business needs. You will apply core quality engineering methodologies, lead complex root-cause investigations, and collaborate with Design Engineering, Manufacturing, Supplier Quality, and cross-functional teams to identify risks, resolve technical issues, and ensure product and process readiness.

Success in the first 12 months means driving early design and manufacturing risk mitigation, leading cross-functional issue resolution, improving component and system quality, and ensuring products meet design intent, performance requirements, and process capability targets ahead of launch.

What You'll Own

Early Engineering & DFM: Evaluate components and systems for manufacturability and assembly feasibility. Provide DFM input during concept, prototype, and design-freeze phases, and participate in engineering design reviews to incorporate quality requirements, lessons learned, and risk mitigation.

Quality Tools & Engineering Analysis: Apply core quality methodologies including APQP, PPAP, FMEA, Control Plans, MSA, and SPC. Lead or support DFMEA and PFMEA reviews and utilize structured problem-solving methodologies such as 8D, 5-Why, and Ishikawa to drive root cause identification and corrective action.

Root Cause Analysis & Issue Closure: Lead cross-functional technical investigations involving design, manufacturing processes, suppliers, and vehicle build issues. Drive containment, corrective action implementation, validation, and issue closure across program phases.

GD&T & Dimensional Engineering: Interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and GD&T requirements. Support tolerance analysis, dimensional investigations, and resolution of component and assembly issues in partnership with Engineering and Metrology teams.

Prototype, DV, and PV Build Support: Provide hands-on quality engineering support throughout prototype, design validation, product validation, and production build phases. Identify and track defects, coordinate technical investigations, validate corrective actions, and ensure component readiness and design intent.

Manufacturing & Supplier Quality Collaboration: Partner with Manufacturing and Supplier Quality teams to assess process capability, production readiness, supplier performance, and component quality. Support PPAP activities, technical reviews, audits, line walks, and containment efforts.

Cross-Commodity Quality Support: Provide technical quality engineering support across various vehicle commodities and systems based on evolving program requirements. Collaborate with engineering teams to address quality challenges involving mechanical, electrical, electromechanical, structural, and integrated vehicle components.

What You Bring

Required

Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

8+ years of automotive engineering, product quality, manufacturing quality, or related technical engineering experience.

Experience supporting automotive components, systems, or commodities through product development, validation, launch, or production.

Strong understanding of engineering drawings, technical specifications, GD&T, and dimensional analysis.

Hands-on experience with APQP, PPAP, FMEA, SPC, and automotive core quality tools.

Experience supporting prototype, DV, PV, or production build activities.

Demonstrated ability to lead complex root-cause investigations, implement corrective actions, and drive technical issue resolution.

Ability to work across multiple engineering disciplines and adapt to different vehicle systems and component technologies.

Strong technical communication, analytical problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

Ability to read, write, speak, and understand English sufficiently to perform the essential duties of the position, including understanding work instructions, safety procedures, and job-related communications.

Preferred

Experience supporting multiple automotive commodities or vehicle systems.

Experience in automotive OEM, Tier 1 supplier, or high-volume manufacturing environments.

Familiarity with automotive quality standards, including IATF 16949 and ISO 9001.

Experience with vehicle integration, system-level validation, and cross-functional engineering investigations.

EV, premium automotive, or advanced vehicle technology experience.

Work Requirement

This role is fully onsite at our Arizona facility.

Floor Leader

jobs.title: Certified Medical Assistant
jobs.description:
The Certified Medical Assistant (CMA) is responsible for the intake of clients and preparing them to be seen by the Medical Practitioners. The CMA performs back-office skills, obtains baseline clinical data, assists the medical staff as necessary, assists in the efficient operation of the Medical Clinic, and collaborates with the maintenance of the laboratory. This position is vital to the provision of support to the providers and patients in the delivery of Patient Centered Medical Home (PCMH) team-based care. The Certified Medical Assistant works under the supervision of the site Practice Manager.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:

• Screens patients, documents findings in the medical information system and alerts the practitioner to special care needs.
• Assists the practitioner and other professional staff in the delivery of patient care; reinforces discharge instructions and deliverables.
• Administers medications and immunizations under the direction of healthcare professionals; documents same in the medical information system.
• Practices Infection Control and Bloodborne Pathogen precautions, procedures and practices.
• Performs medical office administration, monitors inventories and maintains supply levels for patient care activities.
• Performs CLIA-waiver testing and collaborates with the contract laboratory technician.
• Performs all Core Competencies when providing patient-centered care.
• Supports the Native Health mission as needed.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

• Knowledge of the primary care clinic purpose and operations.
• Ability to prioritize duties, perform them efficiently and adjust to unexpected events.
• Knowledge of medical terminology.
• Safe medication administration knowledge and skills.
• Ability to help patients feel welcome.
• Ability to be punctual and dependable.
• Knowledge of infection control and bloodborne pathogen processes.
• Ability to work efficiently and comfortably with other medical clinic employees.
• Knowledge and use of supplies and medical equipment.
• Skills in the use of medical instruments and supplies.
• Willingness to learn new tasks consistent with MA training.
• Culturally competent; able to work with a diverse workforce and client population.
• Evidence of current medication administration knowledge and skills.
• Comprehension of HIPAA regulations, compliance and violation reporting.
• Healthcare information entry and retrieval from the electronic health record skills.

QUALIFICATIONS/EXPERIENCE/REQUIREMENTS:

• High school diploma or equivalent is required.
• Certificate from an accredited Medical Assistant training program is required.
• Must be certified as a Certified Medical Assistant (CMA), Registered Medical Assistant (RMA), National Certified Medical Assistant (NCMA), or Certified Clinical Medical Assistant (CCMA).
• Two years of experience as a Medical Assistant in a direct patient care setting, with experience in pediatric and adult patients preferred.
• Spanish language fluency is preferred.

Standard Employment Requirements:

• Must possess a valid and unrestricted Arizona driver’s license (within 30 days of hire if applicant is from out-of-state) with no DUI/DWI or reckless driving convictions in the last five years. No more than two at-fault accidents in the last three years. Must maintain a valid Arizona driver’s license during employment. Must be insurable under NATIVE HEALTH’s liability auto policy.
• Must pass a criminal background check and obtain a Class I Fingerprint Clearance Card within the initial ninety (90) calendar days of employment and retain a valid card while employed with NATIVE HEALTH.
• Must pass substance abuse testing upon employment and submit to random testing during employment.
• Must provide an updated immunization (IZ) record at the time of employment.
• Must have a current (within 12 months) Tuberculosis (TB) skin report upon employment and provide an annual update.
• Must obtain BLS certification within (90) calendar days of employment and maintain certification during employment.

Native Health complies with all state and federal requirements, including EEOC requirements.
