At onX, we believe that unique perspectives make us stronger. By bringing together people with different experiences, ideas, and viewpoints, we fuel innovation and move closer to our mission of awakening the adventurer in everyone. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to fairness not only in hiring, but also in development, compensation, and promotion. Our goal is to build an inclusive community where every team member can show up authentically and thrive. Together, we win as one team. Come join us!

jobs.title: Senior Engineer - Autonomy Systems Engineering, Vehicle Control
jobs.location: Boston, Massachusetts, United States; Las Vegas, Nevada, United States; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States
jobs.description:
Motional is a leading autonomous driving company on a mission to make driverless vehicles a safe, reliable, and accessible reality. Backed by Hyundai Motor Group, Motional is at the forefront of the physical AI revolution. Motional isn't just building first-of-its-kind technology; we are transforming transportation to create safer streets and more sustainable mobility options.

The Systems Readiness and Performance team is the crucial bridge between software development and real-world deployment. We are responsible for driving system design, for verifying and validating the autonomy stack, and for defining, measuring, and validating system performance targets. We work closely with stakeholders in autonomy, vehicle platform, safety, infrastructure, and operations to build the safety case for our fully driverless IONIQ 5 robotaxis in Las Vegas and to shape the vehicle platform that comes next.

Mission Summary:

The vehicle control interface is where Motional's autonomy software interfaces with the vehicle platform: steering, braking, and propulsion commands go out, and actuator state, faults, and vehicle interventions come back. Gaps in requirements or test coverage at this boundary show up as issues on the road.

As a Senior Systems Engineer embedded with our vehicle control software team, you will own the verification and validation strategy for the vehicle interface software on our current fleet, act as the systems reviewer for changes going into releases, and contribute to the control interface requirements for our next-generation platform.

What you'll be doing:

• Build and own the verification and validation plan for the vehicle interface control software: catalog existing tests across unit, integration, simulation, hardware-in-the-loop, and test track; map them to requirements; and close coverage gaps.

• Establish an impact analysis process so every software change ships with the right regression tests identified and tracked.

• Review and approve changes to vehicle interface and fault handling logic as the systems engineering representative, defining the evidence needed for release.

• Analyze fleet and test data to characterize vehicle behavior (braking, traction and stability interventions, torque response) and turn findings into requirements and test cases.

• Draft and review control interface requirements for the next-generation platform alongside the principal engineer, and prepare technical material for discussions with Hyundai Motor Group.

• Support safety analyses on the vehicle control path and make sure the resulting requirements are testable.

• Build automated analysis and dashboards (Python, SQL) that give fast feedback on vehicle interface performance.

• Support root cause analysis of vehicle interface issues from testing and operations.

What we're looking for:

• BS in Mechanical, Electrical, Aerospace, Robotics, Computer, or equivalent Engineering; MS preferred.

• 5+ years of engineering experience on safety-critical systems, including hands-on work bringing up or integrating a vehicle platform for an ADAS or automated driving system (vehicle interface, actuation, drive-by-wire control, or platform testing).

• End-to-end systems engineering experience: requirements, analysis, and verification and validation, including building test plans and tracking requirement-to-test coverage.

• Software or hardware test development experience.

• Strong analytical skills across vehicle dynamics, data analysis, and systems analysis.

• Python or similar, and SQL, for analyzing test and fleet data; ability to read C++.

• Excellent written and verbal communication; effective working day to day with a software development team.

• In-vehicle networking tools and signal definition with CAN

Bonus points(not required):

• Automotive functional safety or SOTIF experience (ISO 26262, ISO 21448) applied to control software.

• Hardware-in-the-loop test development.

• Requirements management and traceability tools (Jama, DOORS, Polarion, or similar).

• Experience working directly with an automaker or Tier 1 supplier on vehicle interfaces.

Physical Demands:

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit, talk, or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stand and at times for long periods; walk; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms. The employee must occasionally lift and move up to 50 pounds.

Travel Requirements (up to 20%):

Expected to travel to our Las Vegas test site and to Pittsburgh for vehicle testing and integration, roughly 1-2 weeks each quarter, with occasional international travel as needed for the business.

Working Environment:

The work environment characteristics described here represent those a team member encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. The team member is regularly exposed to mechanical and computer parts. The team member is occasionally exposed to fumes and/or airborne particles. The noise level in the environment is low to moderate.

All applicants will receive impartial consideration without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic data, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation or other legally protected status. Motional is a driverless technology company making autonomous vehicles a safe, reliable, and accessible reality. We’re driven by something more.

Our journey is always people first.

We aren't just developing driverless cars; we're creating safer roadways, more equitable transportation options, and making our communities better places to live, work, and connect. Our team is made up of engineers, researchers, innovators, dreamers and doers, who are creating a technology with the potential to transform the way we move.

Higher purpose, greater impact.

We’re creating first-of-its-kind technology that will transform transportation. To do so successfully, we must design for everyone in our cities and on our roads. We believe in building a great place to work through a progressive, global culture that is diverse, inclusive, and ensures people feel valued at every level of the organization. Scale up, not starting up.

Our team is behind some of the industry's largest leaps forward, including the first fully-autonomous cross-country drive in the U.S, the launch of the world's first robotaxi pilot, and operation of the world's longest-standing public robotaxi fleet. We’re driven to scale; we’re moving towards commercialization of our technology, and we need team members who are ready to embrace change and challenges.

Formed as a joint venture between Hyundai Motor Group and Aptiv, Motional is fundamentally changing how people move through their lives. jobs.title: CO2 Quality Lead
jobs.description:
Remora is seeking a Quality Lead to own and continuously improve our CO₂ Quality Program, ensuring the beverage-grade CO₂ produced by our carbon capture systems consistently meets regulatory, customer, and industry standards. This is a hands-on role responsible for maintaining our quality management framework, overseeing product testing and compliance, and establishing the processes necessary to support our growing operations.

We’re building modular carbon capture systems, turning exhaust into beverage-grade CO₂ sold to breweries and greenhouses. We deploy in regions facing severe CO₂ shortages, where prices are highest, allowing us to generate high margins without relying on tax credits or carbon credits.

We’ve raised over $115 million in funding from top investors including Lowercarbon Capital, Union Square Ventures, First Round Capital, Y Combinator, and Valor Equity Partners.

Responsiblities:

• Own and maintain Remora's CO₂ Quality Program, ensuring compliance with FDA regulations, customer specifications, and industry standards.

• Develop, own, and continuously enhance Remora’s food safety and quality programs, establishing and improving scalable processes, procedures, and documentation as operations grow.

• Oversee product sampling, laboratory testing, and quality verification to ensure beverage-grade CO₂ meets required specifications.

• Exercise independent product release and stop-ship authority to prevent distribution of nonconforming products.

• Lead nonconformance investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective actions to prevent recurrence.

• Support customer, regulatory, and third-party audits, maintaining audit readiness and addressing findings.

• Train site operators on quality procedures, compliance requirements, and documentation standards.

• Partner with Operations and Engineering to mitigate quality risks and standardize processes across production sites.

• Develop and eventually own Remora's Corrective Action Program (CAP) and Occurrence Investigation and Reporting Program (OIRP).

Requirements:

• 7+ years of quality assurance, quality control, or quality management experience in regulated manufacturing, or similar experience.

• Strong knowledge of Quality Management Systems (QMS), ISO 9001, document control, and quality compliance.

• Experience with root cause analysis, nonconformance management, corrective actions, and quality audits.

• Ability to interpret technical specifications, regulatory requirements, and laboratory testing results.

• Demonstrated ability to independently make critical quality decisions, including stopping production or shipments when standards are not met.

• Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills, with the ability to train and influence cross-functional teams.

• Comfortable working independently in a fast-paced startup environment, building and improving processes as the organization scales.

Here’s what we value:

• Mission First: We are laser-focused on our mission. We have chosen to take on the defining challenge of our time, and we don’t shy away from the hard decisions required to put our mission first, no matter how tough. The world needs our technology and it won’t happen any time soon if we don’t make it happen. We are a low-ego team, and we prioritize the mission over our self-interest. We think strategically with an eye to the long term, and we clearly separate what must be done well now, and what can be improved later, despite ambiguity.

• Burning Urgency: Our hard-core intensity and work ethic match the crisis we’re in. We have a strong bias toward action, and we execute with focus and speed. In the absence of guidance, we take charge, lead our teammates, and accomplish our goals. We aren’t afraid to change course when something isn’t working, and we find solutions even when it seems like there are none. We are cool under pressure, and our quiet determination and drive are unwavering. We relentlessly push ourselves and each other to improve. We don’t accept adequate performance. Excellence is the expectation. Many would say our standards are unreasonably high, and many would say our goals are unreasonably bold, but we are hungry to be exceptional. We will never give up, no matter what. If we get knocked down, we get back up, every time. We will not fail.

• Uncompromising Honesty: We are always honest with ourselves, our teammates, our customers, our investors, our suppliers, our communities, and all of our partners, especially about what’s not going well and what we don’t know. When we see issues, risks, or challenges, we speak up, and when we make mistakes, we admit them proactively and take full accountability. We challenge others directly when we disagree, even when it’s uncomfortable, and we seek this uncompromising honesty from others.

• Treat People Exceptionally Well: We care intensely about everyone who is on this mission with us, and our standard is exceptional respect for our teammates, partners, and communities. Teammates who bring different perspectives and backgrounds are essential to our success, and we empower everyone to share their voice. We listen to truly understand. We constantly encourage and help our teammates, and inspire each other with our enthusiasm and optimism.

• Joyful Curiosity: We love to learn, and we learn quickly. We explore the unknown with wonder and excitement. We reason from first principles. We generate original ideas with an open mind and test them quickly in the real world. We take risks and adapt as we discover more. We explore many ideas in parallel, and we don’t count on a silver bullet solution. We share our ideas freely with our teammates. We are skeptical about conventional wisdom, and we question every assumption and requirement. We are always looking for ways to simplify. We are rigorous and attentive to detail. We are eager to understand all aspects of our business and technology, and we contribute effectively outside our individual specialties. We never stop learning.

Logistics:

• Location: Wixom, MI (in-person required)

• Start date: ASAP

Compensation and Benefits:

• Salary: $140,000 - $189,000

• Competitive Stock Options

• Healthcare (BCBS)

• Dental + Vision

• Retirement (401k)

• Student loan assistance

• Three weeks of paid time off

• Dependent care assistance (childcare or eldercare)

• Parental leave

• Unlimited Sick leave

• Compassionate leave

• Employee development and coaching

Studies show that many qualified candidates hesitate to apply unless they meet every listed qualification. If you’re enthusiastic about this role—even if you don’t meet every requirement—we encourage you to apply. We’re most excited to work with people who learn quickly and want to tackle the climate crisis.

jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer
jobs.description:
SENIOR DATA ENGINEER

Location: Remote. (Eastern & Central time zones only. Some travel required.)




ABOUT US

Clasp is a mission-driven, venture-backed startup transforming access to education and career pathways. A college education was always meant to lead to economic mobility. But with rising costs and shrinking loan availability, many working-class and first-generation students don’t have the money they need to finish school. That’s where Clasp comes in. We’re the market leader in institutionally funded gap loan programs. We partner with schools to design, launch and manage lending programs that keep students enrolled, graduating and thriving.

Fresh off our Series B, Clasp is entering its next phase of growth. Recent recognition includes:

 - TIME’s Best Inventions of 2026 (Loan-Linked Hiring)

 - Forbes Fintech 50

 - Business Insider: Top 14 Healthcare Startups to Watch in 2026 and 43 Startups to Bet Your Career On in 2025

Our work spans two business lines:

Clasp Talent helps healthcare employers attract and retain critical talent by connecting them with diverse candidates and using student loan repayment as a powerful recruiting and retention tool. We meaningfully connect employers, educational institutions, and learners to drive mutual benefit.

Clasp Student Finance equips colleges and universities with lending technology to launch and operate their own private student loan programs, enabling schools to step in and support their students directly with financial aid. Recent federal financial aid changes are reshaping how institutions think about supporting their students, and Clasp Student Finance is poised to meet this moment. 




WHO WE NEED

Clasp is hiring a Senior Data Engineer to be a technical owner of our data platform. You'll design, scale, and evolve the pipelines and architecture that deliver reliable data on student loans, educational enrollment, and employment to teams across Clasp Student Finance and Clasp Talent, and to our partners. You'll take on complex, ambiguous problems on your own, make sound architectural tradeoffs, and think ahead to how those decisions affect downstream teams, systems, and the business. You'll also mentor teammates and build the patterns, tooling, and AI-supported workflows that raise the bar for the whole data team. The payoff for Clasp is a data platform that scales with the business: fewer outages, faster answers, and higher-quality data behind better decisions.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the reliability, scalability, and long-term direction of Clasp's data pipeline end to end

 - Design, build, and maintain DAGs and dbt models, and set the modeling standards and patterns the team follows

 - Architect ETL/ELT pipelines that integrate data from third-party APIs, databases, and flat files, with monitoring, testing, and failure handling built in

 - Lead design for new data sources and models, and evolve our cloud data architecture so data stays secure, accessible, cost-efficient, and well-governed

 - Diagnose complex pipeline failures across upstream sources, transformation logic, and infrastructure, then put systemic fixes, alerting, and runbooks in place so issues don't recur

 - Partner with stakeholders to anticipate their data needs, navigate competing priorities, and deliver reliable, well-documented data products

 - Identify business continuity risks and single points of failure in the platform, and lead improvements to developer experience and platform architecture

 - Raise the quality bar through thorough design and code reviews, and mentor teammates formally and informally

 - Take an AI-first approach to documentation, tooling, and workflows so the team's knowledge of the codebase scales beyond any one person


WHAT YOU’LL NEED

 - Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

 - 5+ years of hands-on data engineering experience, including ownership of production pipelines and architecture decisions

 - Deep expertise designing, building, and maintaining DAGs and dbt models, including setting the modeling standards and patterns others follow

 - Proven experience architecting ETL/ELT pipelines that integrate data from third-party APIs, databases, and flat files, with monitoring, testing, and failure handling built in

 - Experience designing cloud-based data architecture and making explicit tradeoffs between security, accessibility, cost efficiency, and governance

 - Strong judgment in ambiguous situations: you make pragmatic architectural decisions that balance speed, quality, and long-term impact, and you set new patterns when existing ones fall short

 - A track record of owning relationships with non-technical stakeholders and turning their needs into reliable, well-documented data products

 - Clear, early communication, both synchronous and asynchronous, especially around risks, tradeoffs, and technical decisions

 - Experience mentoring engineers and giving thorough design and code reviews

 - Comfort with high autonomy on a fast-paced, high-performing team, with the ownership and follow-through to set the pace for others

 - Experience leveraging AI tools to improve documentation, tooling, and engineering workflows


WHAT WE GIVE IN RETURN

 - Competitive cash and equity compensation

 - Health benefits (health, dental, & vision)

 - 401k + match

 - Flexible PTO policy

 - Opportunities to grow and perform in a fast-paced environment alongside a stellar team


SALARY

The salary range for this position is competitive and will be commensurate with the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and industry knowledge, ranging between $135,000 to $165,000 annually. In addition to the base salary, we offer an attractive equity component as part of our compensation package, providing an opportunity for eligible employees to share in the success and growth of our company. We are committed to offering competitive compensation and benefits packages to attract and retain top talent.

Working at Clasp
Clasp is moving to a remote-first model in 2027. We've built our tools and norms to support flexible, focused work wherever you do your best thinking. To keep collaboration real-time, we hire team members based in the Eastern and Central time zones. Remote-first doesn't mean remote-only. We invest in intentional in-person time to strengthen relationships and stay connected to our mission. Team members should expect company-paid travel up to seven times per year, typically two to four days at a time, for team and company-wide gatherings, in addition to any role-specific travel.

Work authorization
This role is not eligible for immigration sponsorship, now or in the future. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States for any employer.

How we use AI in hiring
Clasp uses AI-assisted tools in parts of our hiring process, such as AI notetakers transcribing or summarizing interviews, scheduling, and supporting evaluation in technical assessments. Humans review applications and make every hiring decision. AI tools don't make final decisions about any candidate. You're welcome to use AI to research Clasp and prepare, but during live interviews and assessments we want to hear your own thinking, so please don't use AI tools that generate or feed you responses in real time. If you'd like to be evaluated without AI tools, need an accommodation, or have questions about how we use these tools, email recruiting@clasp.com and we'll arrange another process where we can.

Equal opportunity
Clasp is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We don't discriminate based on race, color, religion, creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, and related conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran or military status, citizenship status (except as required by law), or any other status protected by federal, state, or local law. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered in line with applicable fair chance laws. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the hiring process, email recruiting@clasp.com.

Datavant is the data collaboration platform trusted for healthcare. Guided by our mission to make the world’s health data secure, accessible and actionable, we provide critical data solutions for organizations across the healthcare ecosystem - including providers, health plans, researchers, and life sciences companies. From fulfilling a single patient’s request for their medical records to powering the AI revolution in healthcare, Datavanters are building the future of how data is connected and used to improve health.

By joining Datavant today, you’re stepping onto a driven and highly collaborative team that is passionate about creating transformative change in healthcare.

What We’re Looking For:

The Senior Manager of Coding Operations leads the internal audit leadership and auditor team responsible for vendor quality oversight, client audit reviews, and audit activities supporting risk adjustment client projects. This role sets priorities, establishes performance expectations, and ensures that audit findings are accurate, consistent, and translated into measurable improvements in coding quality.

The Senior Manager serves as a primary point of contact for internal leadership and external vendor leadership on overall accuracy performance. This role reviews the qualifications and performance of vendor users assigned to coding and audit projects and partners with vendor leaders on coaching, corrective actions, and assignment decisions. Through leadership of the internal management team, the Senior Manager ensures audit resources are aligned to client needs, vendor risks. This individual will be responsible for strategic initiatives as it relates to vendor quality performance and internal resource alignment.

What You Will Do:

• Lead and develop the managers, supervisors, and auditors responsible for internal audit operations, vendor oversight, and client audit support; establish clear ownership, goals, and accountability.

• Set the internal team’s audit priorities, staffing plans, and quality and productivity expectations; balance routine oversight with client audits, targeted reviews, escalations, and time-sensitive project needs.

• Own communication of overall coding and audit accuracy performance to internal stakeholders and onshore and offshore vendor leadership, including trends, risks, corrective actions, and progress against expectations.

• Lead recurring vendor quality reviews and business review discussions, using findings to establish action owners, timelines, and measurable improvement goals.

• Review vendor users assigned to coding, first-level quality assurance (QA1), and second-level quality assurance (QA2) projects; evaluate qualifications, audit history, and sustained performance to assess suitability for each assignment.

• Partner with vendor leadership to address individual user performance through documented feedback, coaching, retraining, increased monitoring, and recommendations for reassignment or removal when expectations are not met; verify improvement before recommending a return to prior responsibilities.

• Oversee review and validation of client audit findings, including agreement and rebuttal assessments, root cause analysis, and timely preparation of supporting documentation and response recommendations.

• Ensure the internal audit team completes vendor oversight reviews, targeted audits, validation of corrective actions, and other audit tasks needed to support client projects; perform complex or urgent reviews as needed.

• Oversee resolution of coding and audit disagreements, including escalated QA1 and QA2 findings, and coordinate calibration to support consistent application of coding and client-specific guidelines.

• Establish consistent standards for audit selection, feedback documentation, performance tracking, escalation, and follow-up; monitor the reliability of audit results used to evaluate vendor and user performance.

• Analyze performance at the vendor, project, and individual user levels to identify recurring errors and emerging risks; present findings and recommendations clearly to leadership.

• Partner with Coding Operations, Client Success, Training, and other stakeholders to translate audit findings into education, workflow improvements, and corrective action plans; evaluate whether interventions produce sustained improvement.

• Maintain audit policies and procedures aligned with applicable coding requirements and client guidelines; promote consistent, compliant use of coding platforms and AI-assisted workflows.

• Manage internal team performance, hiring, onboarding, development, and capacity through the reporting management team; escalate barriers to quality, service commitments, or project completion.

• Business-related travel up to 20%.

What You Need to Succeed:

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and progressively responsible experience in coding operations, auditing, or quality management.

• A minimum of five years of risk adjustment coding and/or auditing experience, including oversight of coding quality and client audit processes.

• Five or more years of people leadership experience, including experience leading managers or supervisors and developing remote teams.

• Experience managing vendor quality performance and working directly with vendor leadership on corrective actions and individual user performance concerns.

• Strong knowledge of ICD-10-CM coding, risk adjustment methodologies, medical terminology, disease processes, and the application of client-specific coding guidelines.

• Ability to evaluate auditor performance, resolve complex coding disagreements, and lead effective calibration and root cause discussions.

• Demonstrated ability to interpret vendor, project, and user-level performance data and turn findings into clear priorities and measurable improvements.

• Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex findings and performance expectations to internal and external leaders.

• Strong judgment, organization, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to prioritize competing demands and meet deadlines across multiple projects.

• Proficiency with Excel and other Microsoft applications; experience with coding platforms, quality dashboards, and AI-assisted coding workflows preferred.

• Active AHIMA credential (RHIA, RHIT, or CCS) or AAPC credential (CPC, COC, CIC, or CRC).

• Ability to work effectively in a remote environment and adjust work schedules to support departmental needs and vendor collaboration.

What We Offer:

• Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance

• Retirement savings plan

• Opportunities for career growth and development

• Employee wellness programs

• Additional benefits based on location and role

We are committed to building a diverse team of Datavanters who are all responsible for stewarding a high-performance culture in which all Datavanters belong and thrive. jobs.title: Manager, Food Innovation and Commercialization
jobs.description:
The Manager, Food Innovation Commercialization is responsible for translating innovation strategy into scalable business results, overseeing the commercialization of new menu items, platforms, equipment, packaging and operational capabilities from concept approval through network-wide deployment. This role partners closely with culinary development, category management, operations, procurement, marketing and finance teams to ensure innovations are operationally viable, financially sound and ready for successful launch. This role leads the commercialization function, drives cross-functional alignment, manages commercialization priorities and ensures execution readiness across the innovation pipeline.

• Lead the commercialization strategy for all food and beverage innovation initiatives
• Develop launch roadmaps that align innovation priorities with business objectives and operational capabilities
• Establish commercialization standards, tools and best practices across the innovation portfolio
• Prioritize projects and allocate resources across multiple workstreams
• Partner with Director of Food Innovation to translate innovation priorities into executable commercialization plans
• Assess operational feasibility, risks, dependencies and resource requirements for new initiatives
• Ensure concepts progress through development milestones with appropriate business rigor and governance
• Recommend launch timing and market readiness decisions
• Develop and lead a team of commercialization talent, aligning resources and capabilities to support the innovation strategy
• Build commercialization capabilities and processes that support a growing innovation pipeline
• Serve as the primary commercialization lead across food operations, procurement, marketing, finance and technology
• Facilitate alignment on launch requirements, timelines, and success metrics
• Resolve cross-functional barriers and escalate critical issues when necessary
• Ensure launch readiness activities are completed on time and within scope
• Oversee pilot planning, market tests and post-launch evaluations
• Define commercialization success measures including financial metrics, operational performance, guest feedback and scalability
• Identify learnings and recommend adjustments prior to broader deployment
• Lead launch readiness reviews and commercialization approval processes

• Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Operations, Supply Chain or related field
• 7+ years of experience in foodservice, retail, CPG, restaurant operations, commercialization, category management, innovation or project leadership
• Ability to follow instructions and work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
• Basic understanding of food safety and sanitation practices.
• Experience leading cross-functional teams and influencing stakeholders without direct authority
• Strong financial, operational and analytical capabilities
• Exceptional project leadership and communication skills
• Ability to translate strategy into executable market launches, balancing guest, operational and financial considerations
• Cross-functional leadership and ability to influence diverse stakeholder groups
• Proactively designs for operational success by understanding how innovations impact field execution
• Leads multiple initiatives simultaneously while maintaining quality, speed and accountability
• Strong financial and business acumen

• Overnight travel required up to 10%
• General office work requires sitting or standing for long periods of time
• Able to lift up to 50 lbs.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Product Development & Production
jobs.description:
Studs is a category-defining ear piercing and earring brand named one of “the 10 most innovative companies in retail for 2023” by Fast Company. Studs connects ear piercing with aftercare and earring shopping to create an end-to-end Earscaping® experience. We offer a better retail and digital experience that prioritizes safety and expertise in a cool, fun and welcoming environment, along with a wide earring assortment—all at an accessible price point.

The Senior Manager of Product Development & Production is responsible for execution of proposed product and design. They will take the product from the proposed design state to commercialization including physical product development and final production. They will also be responsible for building out a team org structure and training new team members

Salary Range: $130,000

Key Responsibilities:

Product Development

• Establish strategic partnerships with suppliers, manufacturers, and other vendors in order to develop new products or improve existing products

• Oversee the product life cycle of new products from concept to commercialization

• Develop and manage the development calendar with milestones that aligns with the organization’s strategic objective

• Manage all vendor WIPs, sample requests and inbound samples

• Price negotiation to achieve margin goals

• Work with external partners on brand collaboration products and key initiatives

Production

• Oversee production process from PO placement through ex-factory including vendor payment and credits

• Ensure bulk goods produced conform with approved designs and standards

• Set factory allocation to ensure they align with factories’ capacity supporting the businesses growth and key initiatives

• Negotiate bulk inventory costs, lead times and deliveries

• Manage and resolve any manufacturing issues including delivery delays with factories

• Communicate delivery timelines and collaborate with cross functional partners on product launches

Testing & Relations

• Foster and maintain vendor relationships

• Lead on boarding process ensuring factory and vendor adherence to Stud's processes and standards, and that clear understanding of processes and nuances between vendors is maintained

• Develop and monitor, and continually improve quality assurance procedures and processes with external testing vendors

• Ensure all products manufactured that will be commercially sold are tested to STUDS standards prior to shipment

• Evaluate, improve, and define processes and policies, process implementation, and identify errors and areas of improvement

• Address the root causes of quality issues, create corrective action plans and implement long term solutions in partnership with external vendors

Requirements:

• 5+ years of experience in product development and/or production, with hands-on ownership of products from concept through bulk delivery.

• Jewelry experience strongly preferred, but not required. Experience in accessories or another consumer product category is a plus.

• Retail or DTC brand experience a plus, especially in a multi-channel business (physical retail and ecommerce).

• 2+ years of people management experience, or a demonstrated record of training and developing team members. Interest in building a team structure from the ground up.

• Proven track record managing overseas and domestic factory partners, including vendor onboarding, factory allocation, and capacity planning.

• Highly organized, with the ability to run a development calendar across many SKUs, vendors, and launches at once in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

• Clear, direct communicator who works well across functions, including Merchandising, Finance, Retail, and Marketing.

• Advanced Excel/Google Sheets skills. AI fluency preferred: comfortable using AI tools in daily work to move faster.

• Based in New York, NY and able to work from the HQ office on a hybrid schedule.

• Driven, creative problem solver that consistently acts with integrity and speaks up

• Owner’s mindset, with the ability to approach feedback and problems with a positive attitude.

Benefits & Perks

• Flexible Work Environment (3 days in office, 2 days work from home)

• Comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance (including a plan option with $0 in-network mental health visits)

• Access to Mental Health and Work/Life Resources including Online Therapy, Gender Affirmation Support Services, and Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

• Voluntary Life Insurance

• Health and Commuter Tax-Advantaged Accounts

• Stock Options in connection with the Company’s Equity Incentive Plan

• 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan

• Paid Time Off, Paid Safe & Sick Leave, and Paid Parental Leave

• Paid Sabbatical After 4 Years of Service

• Exclusive Employee Discounts on Piercings and Jewelry (we’ve got your friends and family covered too!)

• Access to PerkSpot and additional benefits such as pet insurance, discounted tickets, personal finance coaching, healthy rewards, and more!

jobs.description:

Benesch is a growing, multi-disciplined planning, engineering, and professional services firm. We enhance infrastructure and communities across the country – creating spaces and providing connections in ways that make a difference.

We pride ourselves on being nimble enough to remain responsive to client needs yet large enough to offer exceptional bench strength. At Benesch, we are looking for candidates with varied backgrounds and worldviews. We are committed to offering an inclusive work environment where everyone feels valued and respected. Railroad Grade Crossing – Traffic Project Engineer

Benesch’s Rail Division provides trusted expertise in rail grade crossing safety, rail signal systems, and traffic operations. Our Rail Grade Crossing team focuses on designing safe and efficient rail crossings, traffic signal preemption, and related traffic and transportation improvements for both public agencies and private clients.

As a Traffic Project Engineer on the Rail Grade Crossing team, you will deliver technical leadership on rail-traffic and safety projects. You will manage traffic studies, prepare engineering analyses, coordinate plan development, and oversee the technical execution of deliverables. This role also includes mentoring junior staff, coordinating across disciplines, and ensuring designs meet client, safety, and regulatory standards.

Location

This position is part of Benesch’s national Rail Division, anchored in Fort Worth, TX, with hybrid work flexibility. Fully remote arrangements will be considered for qualified candidates.

The Impact You Will Have

• Conduct traffic operations and safety analyses for rail grade crossings and associated roadway projects

• Prepare preliminary and final design plans, specifications, and engineering calculations

• Coordinate drafting of project deliverables and ensure compliance with local, state, and federal standards

• Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams and mentor junior engineers

• Build and maintain client relationships, including local and state transportation agencies

• Represent Benesch at industry and professional events

What We Are Looking For#LI-MM1

• B.S. Degree in Civil Engineering or closely related discipline

• Professional Engineer (PE) license; PTOE a plus

• 5–10 years of experience in rail/traffic engineering, grade crossing design, or related transportation work

• Experience working with public agencies and municipalities; state DOT experience preferred

• Strong knowledge of traffic operations, signal design, safety analyses, and roadway design

• Proficiency with CADD, Synchro, GIS, and other traffic modeling or design software

• Demonstrated ability to work independently, manage project deliverables, and mentor staff

• Excellent communication, client relations, and organizational skills #LI-Ag1

jobs.title: Emergency Veterinary Nurse Trainer - Ardmore, PA
jobs.description:
ABOUT VEG

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most. This meant challenging the status quo and fixing everything that was wrong with the ER experience. Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

This also means saying yes to creating the greatest experience possible for our VEGgies. Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.

VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

THE JOB

As a Nursing Trainer, you have one of the most meaningful jobs at VEG: helping others grow. You’ll lead with curiosity, coach with compassion, and obsess over development. You’re not just building skills—you’re building confidence, momentum, and careers in emergency medicine. Whether you’re working 1:1 on the floor, guiding peer-led sessions, or developing educational tools, your impact will be felt hospital-wide. You’ll tailor training to every learning style, celebrate every milestone, and say yes to every VEGgie who is ready to take the next step. Your work helps make VEG a place where people learn, lead, and love what they do.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Partner with leadership to identify individual and team training needs

• Assess assistants and credentialed technicians through direct observation and real-time immersion

• Drive advancement through VEG’s Cultivate program

• Implement VEG training programs and serve as the go-to training lead at your hospital

• Split your time between on-the-floor mentoring and strategic development

• Provide tailored, hands-on training for all learning styles and skill levels with patience and understanding

• Organize peer training opportunities and build a strong mentoring culture

• Collaborate with nursing managers and professional networks to broaden impact

• Develop and refine training content (i.e. presentations, videos, simulations, and assessments)

• Ensure all training aligns with VEG’s culture, mission, and emergency standards of care

• Continually evaluate and improve leveling programs for assistants and technicians

WHAT YOU NEED

• High school diploma or equivalent required; associate’s degree or higher in veterinary technology from an AVMA accredited program strongly preferred

• Credentialed as a veterinary technician (CVT, RVT, LVT, LVMT) in the state the VEG practice is located; VTS in ECC, internal medicine, or anesthesia/analgesia a plus and will lead to extra considerations in compensation

• High level of knowledge and skill in emergency medicine

• Previous training experience preferred

• A relentless passion for teaching and uplifting others

• An ownership mindset around your team’s growth and development

• Strong communicator and collaborator across teams

• Excitement about VEG’s culture and mission, with a desire to lead by example

• Willingness to travel to other VEG hospitals in your region to help with new veterinarian onboarding as needed

• Must be willing to work in a noisy environment with strong or unpleasant odors.

• Availability to work nights, weekends, and holidays on a rotating or as needed basis based on hospital needs

• Work well in a fast-paced environment with people from all backgrounds and different personality types

WHO YOU ARE

• Empathetic, instinctively taking a people-centric approach, whether supporting your colleagues or making an effort to understand different perspectives

• Have a sense of humility; acknowledging mistakes, sharing credit with others, and lifting up your team’s’ accomplishments

• Feel a strong sense of ownership over your work, taking responsibility for outcomes and staying committed to achieving long-term, impactful results

• Curious by nature; you ask insightful questions and continuously seek out opportunities to learn and grow your skills and knowledge

HOW WE INVEST IN YOU

• Competitive compensation, including base and 401K match

• Comprehensive health and wellness benefits that start on day one, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, QPR training, and access to free therapy or counseling

• Depending on your role, you may be eligible for equity after one year of full time, active employment with VEG, so you can share in our growth and success

• A BIG focus on learning and growth, from VEG-created clinical and leadership programs to unlimited ER CE + travel stipend (no really!). Full-time credentialed VEGgies receive a $2,500/year travel stipend. Full-time uncredentialed VEGgies receive a $1,000/year travel stipend.

• Clinical student loan repayment so you don’t need to worry about your student debt

• Paid parental leave; up to 12 weeks at 100% of regular salary and inclusive fertility and family-building care for all types of families

• Flexible work schedules to support your life outside of work

• Generous employee referral program, so our awesome people can bring in more awesome people

• And the little (big) things, like comfy scrubs, cool VEG swag, and food in the fridge for when you’re hungry

DEI

At VEG, diversity is not just a word—it's a strength that fuels innovation and kindness. Our mission is “Helping people and their pets when they need it most.” And we do that better when our VEGgies (employees) feel valued, respected, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. That's why we're devoted to creating an environment that reflects the diverse communities we serve—where different perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated.

We are focused on providing equitable opportunities for growth, promoting inclusive decision-making, and ensuring that everyone's perspective is considered. Saying yes to VEG means helping us build a culture where your unique experiences and background contribute to a shared vision: being the world’s veterinary emergency company.
